title: Andy Reid: Mansoor Delane is doing well in recovery from shoulder injury
summary: The Chiefs traded first-, third- and fifth-round picks to move up and draft cornerback Mansoor Delane sixth overall, so when he was knocked out of Organized Team Activities with a shoulder injury, it was a concern.
full_text: ' The Chiefs traded first-, third- and fifth-round picks to move up and draft cornerback Mansoor Delane sixth overall, so when he was knocked out of Organized Team Activities with a shoulder injury, it was a concern. But it doesn't sound like a big concern going forward. Chiefs coach Andy Reid addressed reporters on Friday as the team reported to training camp, and he said Delane was in the process of getting medical clearance to practice. "Delane right now is having his final physical. Right now. So he's right in the process of that and is doing well there," Reid said. The precise details of how Delane suffered the injury are not known, but Reid indicated it was a matter of going too hard during offseason work. "We like the way he goes about his business," Reid said. "He's a focused kid, he seems to be a smart, sharp kid. He's willing to work. He was banged up a little bit but he's willing to work. He's aggressive that way — too aggressive in the way he hurt himself there. You've got a good player and he's got to get in and go and get the reps in the defensive scheme." The Chiefs expect Delane to get plenty of reps in training camp, and they hope he's ready to make an immediate impact in Week One.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Patrick Mahomes will wear a brace on his knee, "I can still move and be myself with it"
summary: "It's not like I've been told I have to wear it or how long I have to wear it. It's just going to be my comfortability how I feel," Mahomes said.
full_text: As he returns to the practice field, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes will wear a brace on his surgically repaired knee. But he says he isn't sure how long he'll wear it. Mahomes, who tore his ACL on December 14, said he could keep wearing the brace going forward, or he could choose to take it off, depending on how he feels. "There isn't really a plan for it," Mahomes said. "I'm going start off with it just because I've worn it before and I feel comfortable with it. So that that's kind of where we will start, but it's not like I've been told I have to wear it or how long I have to wear it. It's just going to be my comfortability how I feel. But I will start with it on just because I feel like I can still move and be myself with it. I played with it in college and then we'll just see where we go from there." Mahomes wore a brace in 2015 at Texas Tech, after he suffered a knee injury in a game against TCU, and played well with it. If he plays well with it through training camp he'll keep it on, but if he decides to ditch the brace, he's medically cleared to play without it.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike LaFleur has no concerns about Josh Sweat
summary: Josh Sweat was the subject of trade chatter in the offseason, as the Cardinals received calls about the outside linebacker.
full_text: '' Josh Sweat was the subject of trade chatter in the offseason, as the Cardinals received calls about the outside linebacker. He missed all of the voluntary offseason program, choosing to work out on his own as he has done in the past. It was unclear whether that was related to the firing of Jonathan Gannon, who Sweat followed from Philadelphia after two seasons together with the Eagles. Additional questions were raised when the Cardinals placed Sweat on the active/physically unable to perform list to start training camp this week. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that the move was related to Sweat's ramp-up for training camp and not any unhappiness from the one-time Pro Bowler. " I’m going to say no ," LaFleur said, via Darren Urban of the team website, "because I don't see any discontent, and he's never expressed any discontent to me." LaFleur clarified that while Sweat missed the voluntary work, he was around the Dignity Health Training Center and in contact with the team. "Everyone is on the same page the entire time," LaFleur said. "You guys can believe me or not, but I am not worried about Josh Sweat at all in terms of his health. He's logged a lot of miles in this league, and I think not only for Josh to peak on Sept. 13 [for the opener], but for Josh to also get through the rigors of a 17-game season the way that he plays and the motor he plays with, this is best for him and the Cardinals." Sweat led the team with a career-high 12 sacks last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jacoby Brissett isn't participating in 11-on-11 drills
summary: Yes, Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett is practicing as he tries to get a contract that pays him like a starter, not a backup.
full_text: ' Yes, Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett is practicing as he tries to get a contract that pays him like a starter, not a backup. But he's not really practicing. As noted by Darren Urban of the team's official website, Brissett " isn’t participating in 11-on-11 drills yet ." That's surely a direct result of his dissatisfaction with a deal he signed under the impression that he wouldn't be the team's QB1. Now that he's the presumptive Week 1 starter, he's seeking an adjustment. The current range for veteran starters begins in the low $20 millions and stretches into the $60 millions. With Brissett currently at $6.5 million per year, triple that to $19.5 million and call it a day. He'd be the lowest-paid veteran starter, while still making much more than he's due to make. And it would help get him as ready as he can be with a new coaching staff and a new offense. Which is even more critical, given that the Cardinals are in a division with three Super Bowl contenders. Who would have thought that the Cardinals would long for the days that they were the which-doesn't-belong-and-why fifth team in the NFC East?
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers CEO Ed Policy repeats concern about ability of other teams to raise money
summary: In March 2026, Packers president and CEO Ed Policy raised concerns about the inability of his team to sell limited shares for unlimited funds.
full_text: In March 2026, Packers president and CEO Ed Policy raised concerns about the inability of his team to sell limited shares for unlimited funds. On Friday, he repeated those concerns in connection with the release of the franchise's latest annual report. "It's like other teams have access to this ATM machine that we just don't have right now," Policy said, via the Associated Press. "We're going to have to be more aggressive with revenue generation going forward. We all know the cost of competing in the NFL is going up, and other teams have access to capital sources that we just don't have." He was specifically referring to the inability of the publicly-owned Packers to sell a minority interest for a large influx of cash. "For example, a team can sell five to 10 percent of their equity without giving up any controlling interest in the team, and they could raise more money than we have in our capital reserve fund in just a matter of months," Policy said. It's not a problem for now, but it could become one. "I feel very good about the Packers' financial strength and condition in the medium term and the short term, certainly," Policy said. "But we are keeping a very close eye on some of these long-term trends, looking at how they impact us and our financial health in the long term. . . . We do have to make sure that we're always in a position where we can continue to invest wisely in whatever it takes to field a championship-caliber team, whether that's player costs, football staff or facilities." And that's why we recently spelled out the path toward solving the problem : Dissolve Green Bay Packers Inc., sell the assets to an expansion franchise established by a traditional owner, and give the team the same structure that the other 31 franchises have. If Policy is going to keep identifying the problem, at some point he needs to articulate a solution. Changing the overall nature of the organization is one way to do it. And if the current shareholders don't like that idea, there are other ways to increase revenue. With a lengthy season-ticket waiting list, there's an obvious supply-and-demand issue in Green Bay. That issue can be addressed by charging more for tickets. Alternatively, or additionally, the Packers could sell Personal Seat Licenses. Other teams use these money-for-nothing devices to raise revenue. With tens of thousands waiting for the ability to buy season tickets, why not implement a similar approach? Then there's the stadium naming rights. That's $20 million or so per year that the Packers are choosing to not earn. "It's their choice to not sell naming rights," a source from another team observed. "Or don't trade for Micah [Parsons]." If the Packers are going to continue to operate as a corporation that can't raise money in the ways other teams can (and do), the Packers need to find other ways to make money. Or they need to be more careful in how they spend the money they have. Or they need to stop being a corporation and sell the franchise to a multi-billionaire who grew up with a Cheesehead covering their scalp.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike Vrabel avoids the question of grass vs. turf
summary: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was a player.
full_text: ' Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was a player. He knows the difference between playing on real grass and playing on fake grass. His team plays its home games on fake grass, even though the stadium had real grass for the World Cup. Vrabel was asked about the issue of real grass vs. fake grass during his first press conference of 2026 training camp. He avoided addressing the question. "My take is we would play anywhere we possibly have to," Vrabel said. "That’s my take. It's the kind of football team that I want to create — one that doesn't make excuses, that doesn't care what the environment is. We’re going to go open the season in a great environment in Seattle, and we're going to play on grass, we're going to play on turf, and it's going to rain, it's going to snow. There's a lot of things that are going to come up, and my job is to make sure that we're prepared for whatever does happen." That's fine, but what does he think about the fact that 92 percent of the players prefer real grass? Does he prefer real grass? Does he always practice on real grass, even when the Patriots are preparing to play a game on fake grass? It's a tough spot for any coach of any team whose owners have decided to play home games on the surface that the players don't prefer. The fact that Vrabel didn't answer the question says plenty about what he personally thinks about the issue.
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers' annual report reveals $14.5 billion in shared NFL revenue
summary: Business is still booming.
full_text: '' The corporate structure of the Green Bay Packers requires their books to be open. Which results in the disclosure of the annual revenue that the 32 teams share. Via Matt Schneidman of The Athletic , the Packers' latest annual report shows that they received $453.2 million in their most recent fiscal year. The report was released in advance of Monday's annual shareholder meeting. This means that the teams shared $14.5 billion in national revenue. As to the money that isn't shared, the Packers made $299.8 million. That's $753 million in total revenue for the Packers. And it's a $34 million increase over the team's last annual report. Bottom line? Business is still booming in the NFL. And if the Packers weren't a publicly-traded corporation, we wouldn't have the kind of information that the Packers provide as to the revenue shared by all teams.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chargers put OT Isaiah World on NFI list
summary: The Chargers made a roster move ahead of the start of their training camp.
full_text: ' The Chargers made a roster move ahead of the start of their training camp. The NFL's transaction report for Friday shows that they placed offensive tackle Isaiah World on the non-football injury list. World signed with the Chargers after going undrafted out of Oregon. He tore his ACL during the team's college football playoff loss to Indiana, so it may be some time before he's ready to get back on the field. World played three seasons at Nevada before transferring to Oregon. He started 14 games at left tackle during his only season with the Ducks. Chargers rookies reported to training camp this week. They will have their full squad in camp on July 28 with their first practice set for the next day.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ravens to sign Chris Moore after working out several receivers
summary: Wide receiver Chris Moore is back in Baltimore.
full_text: ' Wide receiver Chris Moore is back in Baltimore. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that Moore worked out for the Ravens on Friday and multiple reports say that he is signing on for a second tour of duty with the team. Moore was a 2016 fourth-round pick and spent his first five seasons with the AFC North club. Moore had 47 catches for 511 yards and four touchdowns during that stint. He spent time with the Texans, Titans and Cardinals before playing in 14 games for the Commanders last season. He had 11 catches for 207 yards and a touchdown. The Ravens worked out wideouts Sterling Shepard, Dante Pettis, and Casey Washington along with Moore. Offensive tackles Hakeem Adenjii and Geron Christian also worked out while quarterback William Atkins handled the throwing during the tryout.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patrick Mahomes consulted with Tom Brady, others during the rehab process
summary: Patrick Mahomes has made a remarkable recovery from a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee.
full_text: Patrick Mahomes has made a remarkable recovery from a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee. The Chiefs quarterback injured his knee in a Dec. 14 game and underwent surgery the following day. A little over seven months later, he is cleared for training camp . Mahomes said he consulted with several players who went through a similar rehab. “I talked to Tom [Brady] early in the process because he had the same injury, a very similar injury that I had,” Mahomes said Friday, via Pete Sweeney of the Kansas City Star . Brady tore the ACL and MCL in his left knee during the season opener in 2008 before winning Comeback Player of the Year in 2009. “It’s just talking to guys that have been through this process and just saying how you have to stay on top of it,” Mahomes said. “It’s a long process. I remember sitting on the table and watching us play those last few games and how much it hurt me, but I knew that if I continued to work, I could be at this spot where I get cleared for practice. Now I’m just trying to get to that spot where I’m cleared to play in the regular season on that first week.” Mahomes also talked to former Chiefs safety Tyrann Mathieu and veteran tight end Zach Ertz. Mathieu tore the ACL and LCL in his left knee in 2013 and had another ACL tear in 2015, and Ertz tore his ACL a week before Mahomes' injury. His conversations with Ertz turned into a rehab competition. “We kind of had like competitions on where we were at, and where we were rehabbing,” Mahomes said of Ertz. “It would start off as how much deadlift — what you’re deadlifting, where you’re at — and then [we would] send little videos. He’s jumping and doing certain acceleration things, and I’m sending him next week doing cutting and stuff like that. “It keeps the competition going because it’s a long process and you feel like sometimes you’re lonely because you’re doing stuff by yourself, and you’re just competing against yourself, so it gave me someone else that I can compete with to push my competitive drive.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Rashee Rice's knee is good to go for training camp
summary: Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice is cleared for training camp, coach Andy Reid said Friday.
full_text: ' Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice is cleared for training camp, coach Andy Reid said Friday. "Rashee Rice, with his knee debridement, is doing great ," Reid said, via Jordan Foote of SI.com. "So he will, again, go. We'll keep an eye on him, but he's cleared to go." Rice underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right knee in May before serving a 30-day sentence for violating his probation by testing positive for THC. Rice was released from Dallas County Jail on June 16. "He's done a great job rehabbing up here," Reid said. "He's been up here the whole time. He'll be in and out here in the next couple of days, but he's been here throughout." Undrafted rookie wideout John Michael Gyllenborg is working through a knee sprain that kept him out of the offseason program. "Gyllenborg, he's still working through the knee sprain which he had," Reid said. "They're doing some other evaluations on him, so we'll just see for this camp here, most likely, he won't get much work there."
author: Charean Williams

title: Patriots waive WR Jimmy Kibble with an injury designation
summary: The Patriots agreed to terms with tight end Jeremiah Franklin on Thursday.
full_text: ' The Patriots agreed to terms with tight end Jeremiah Franklin on Thursday. They made a corresponding move on Friday to get Franklin on the roster. The Patriots waived wide receiver Jimmy Kibble with an injury designation, according to the NFL's personnel notice. Kibble, 22, signed as an unrestricted free agent in May. He appeared in 39 games at Georgetown, totaling 149 receptions for 2,642 yards and 16 touchdowns. Kibble earned first-team All-Patriot League honors last season after catching 63 passes for 1,002 yards and four touchdowns. The Patriots now have 11 wideouts on the roster.
author: Charean Williams

title: JC Tretter wins first round of looming CBA fight with the NFL
summary: New NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter has won the first round of the looming Collective Bargaining Agreement fight with the NFL by doing the one thing that we are all capable of doing.
full_text: ' New NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter has won the first round of the looming Collective Bargaining Agreement fight with the NFL by doing the one thing that we are all capable of doing. Absolutely nothing. By refusing to engage with the league on a potential extension that could have implemented an 18-game regular season by 2027, Tretter has forced the league to throw in the towel on extending the season that quickly. That's the most practical result of the league finally announcing a date for Super Bowl LXII. As PFT reported immediately after Super Bowl LX, the game to be played in February 2028 in Atlanta did not have a specific date because the league was keeping the door open for adding a game to the regular season and moving Super Bowl LXII later in the month. By picking February 13, 2028 as the date for Super Bowl LXII, the NFL has abandoned the effort to get to 18 in 2027. It remains to be seen whether talks will happen in time to potentially add an 18th game in 2028. And it will be an annual question until the current CBA expires, after the 2030 season. Frankly, there's a good chance that the 18-game season would have happened in time for the 2027 season, if Lloyd Howell hadn't resigned as the NFLPA executive director. His exit and the turmoil that ensued made it impossible to engage in negotiations. With Tretter now in place, it would have been impossible to push an 18th game through so quickly. There will be player opposition to it. And it may take a creative solution to get there, like an 18-game season with a 17-game limit for all players except quarterbacks and specialists.
author: Mike Florio

title: Titans agree to terms with DB Nazeeh Johnson
summary: The Titans have agreed to terms with free agent defensive back Nazeeh Johnson, according to his representation, Katz Brothers Sports.
full_text: ' The Titans have agreed to terms with free agent defensive back Nazeeh Johnson, according to his representation, Katz Brothers Sports. Johnson, 28, visited the Eagles and Giants this offseason after becoming a free agent in March. The Chiefs made Johnson a seventh-round pick in 2022, and he spent his first four seasons with them. He played only two games last season after injuring a shoulder in the preseason. Johnson missed all of 2023 with a torn ACL. He has played 29 games with six starts in his career, with all of his 494 defensive snaps coming in 2024. He has also played 286 special teams snaps. Johnson has totaled 66 tackles and a sack in the regular season, with eight tackles in the postseason.
author: Charean Williams

title: Seahawks sign TE Nick Vannett
summary: The Seahawks have brought back a veteran player on offense.
full_text: ' The Seahawks have brought back a veteran player on offense. Seattle announced on Friday that the club has signed tight end Nick Vannett. Vannett, 33, was a Seahawks third-round pick back in 2016. He was traded to Pittsburgh midway through the 2019 season after appearing in 42 games for Seattle with 16 starts over his first four seasons. Since ending 2019 with Pittsburgh, Vannett has spent time with the Broncos, Saints, Giants, Texans, Chargers, Titans, Vikings, and Rams. He’s appeared in a total of 121 games with 54 starts, tallying 108 catches for 1,012 yards with nine touchdowns. Vannett appeared in 10 games with one start for the Vikings and Rams last season. As a corresponding move, the Seahawks have waived cornerback Tyrone Broden.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Panthers claim Ryan Hayes off waivers from the Titans
summary: The Panthers added even more depth at offensive tackle on Friday, after signing offensive tackle Derrell Bailey earlier in the day.
full_text: '' The Panthers added even more depth at offensive tackle on Friday, after signing offensive tackle Derrell Bailey earlier in the day. Carolina claimed offensive tackle Ryan Hayes off waivers from the Titans, the team announced. The Panthers are currently practicing without tackles Ikem Ekwonu and Taylor Moton. Hayes, 26, was on the practice squad of the Falcons last season. He entered the NFL as a seventh-round pick of the Dolphins in 2023 out of Michigan. He has also spent time with the Colts, the Dolphins a second time and the Falcons. He has appeared in one game, which came with the Dolphins in 2024. In a corresponding move, the Panthers waived wide receiver Kobe Prentice.
author: Charean Williams

title: Patrick Mahomes: This is just a checkpoint on the schedule, you have to continue to work
summary: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes has said throughout the offseason that his goal is to be ready for the start of the regular season after suffering a torn ACL in December.
full_text: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes has said throughout the offseason that his goal is to be ready for the start of the regular season after suffering a torn ACL in December. He's officially taken another step in that endeavor, as he's been medically cleared to fully participate in training camp . Mahomes said in his Friday press conference that he found out he'd been cleared two days ago. But while he's looking forward to practicing, he's not making any declarations about his Week 1 availability quite yet. "Just looking at the dates, and there were certain checkpoints I had to get to, to get to this point," Mahomes said. "And this is just another checkpoint on the schedule . So you have to continue to work. It’s not like it’s over and I’m going to be able to play a game tomorrow. You’ve got to continue to work and get better and better and go throughout practice and prove to the coaches, prove to the doctors, everybody that I’m the same quarterback I was before — if not better — and I can go out there and take care of myself and win football games." Mahomes said he's doing much better when it comes to changing directions than he was during the offseason program when he last spoke to the media. "That’s the stuff I had to prove to the doctors and the coaches and everybody like that to be at this point," Mahomes said. "So, it’s a long process. The process isn’t over. It’ll be something I’ll probably deal with for the next few years of my career and throughout the rest of my career. But you have to stay on top of that stuff. But I feel comfortable now of being able to go out there and run the offense the way the offense is supposed to be run." Both Reid and Mahomes talked about taking things day by day when it comes to the quarterback practicing, as he's still coming off of a major injury. But Mahomes wants to be fully immersed in whatever the Chiefs are doing to get himself ready for September. "I want him to call [the offense in practice] like he’s going to call it in the regular season," Mahomes said. "So, whatever that is, that’s going to be the best way for me to prepare myself. I can always let him know if I need to get pulled back or anything like that. But how I am as a competitor, I want to go out there and test it. You want to test it now in training camp, see where you’re at, so when you get to the regular season, it’s almost a little bit easier because you’ve kind of been through it all. That's how he runs training camp. "I don’t think he’s going to take it light on anyone — including me. And then, I’m going to go out there and see what I can do." Mahomes usually plays in preseason games, but that could change this year given the status of his knee. "I think we’ll just see when we get there," Mahomes said. "I’m a competitor, so gameday, I’m going to want to be out there. But I understand the process of getting myself ready to play in the regular season is more important. But, we will see. The coaches and docs will kind of make that decision for me. But I’ll prepare myself like I”m going to play. And if I’m just doing a very hard warm-up, I will take that as serious as playing in the preseason game. It’s a couple weeks away, but it feels like a long way away. I’m going to go with the next step of just going out with the rookies this week." After a grueling process during the offseason, Mahomes is glad to be back out of the training room full-time. "I’m excited just to be able to play football," Mahomes said. "I’ve been seeing cinderblock walls rehabbing every day in Kansas City. So, now to get to be on the practice field with my teammates and my brothers, it’s going to be a lot of fun."
author: Myles Simmons

title: Andy Reid: Patrick Mahomes has been cleared to fully participate
summary: Mahomes will not start training camp on the physically unable to perform list and is set to take his full reps at training camp.
full_text: ' Though he tore his ACL in December, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes has been fully cleared to practice, head coach Andy Reid said in his Friday press conference. “Pat’s doing great with his [rehab]," Reid said. "Right now he’s got clearance to practice and do all the different periods that we have in this camp. We’ll just take it day by day and see how he does. He’ll have plenty of eyes on him from coaches to trainers to doctors. "But right now, he’s been cleared to go ahead and participate fully ." Does that mean he's going to play Week 1? "I’m optimistic, and I know he is extremely optimistic," Reid said. "But I think you’ve got to see how things go here. Let’s just see where we’re at and not make any predictions or anything else. Take it day by day and see where it goes." Reid noted that Mahomes will go through his normal reps at the start of camp. Chiefs quarterbacks and rookies reported to camp on Friday, which inherently gives the QBs a little more ramp-up time before the rest of the squad reports on July 28. But either way, Reid doesn't anticipate Mahomes' reps will be any different in camp. "We’ll see about games and all that once we get there. But right now, we’re just going to take it day by day and see how he does," Reid said. "But he’s been given clearance. "He’s been up here every day, doing his thing, rehabbing. I mentioned before how much time he spent — if anybody spent time doing this thing the right way, he’s it. We appreciate that. And he’s been given clearance by the doctors to work. And they’re pretty comfortable with that. But keeping an eye on him."
author: Myles Simmons

title: Patriots to put Brenden Schooler on NFI list
summary: The Patriots put three players on injury lists earlier this week and head coach Mike Vrabel said that a fourth will be joining them.
full_text: ' The Patriots put three players on injury lists earlier this week and head coach Mike Vrabel said that a fourth will be joining them. Vrabel said at his Friday press conference that safety/special teamer Brenden Schooler will go on the non-football injury list to open training camp. Vrabel did not share the nature of the issue that Schooler is dealing with, but said "he may be away for a little bit or out for a little bit." Schooler had 19 tackles in the 2025 regular season and added six more in the playoffs. He was an All-Pro for his special teams work in 2024. Linebacker Harold Landry and tight end C.J. Dippre are on the physically unable to perform list while running back Terrell Jennings joins Schooler on NFI.
author: Josh Alper

title: Will Grier joins Cowboys' coaching staff
summary: A week after retiring as a player, Will Grier is embarking on his next career, as a coach.
full_text: '' A week after retiring as a player, Will Grier is embarking on his next career, as a coach. Grier is joining the Cowboys' staff as an offensive assistant, according to Todd Archer of ESPN. The move is no surprise, as Grier had been considering an offer to join the Cowboys' coaching staff earlier this offseason, before deciding to sign with the Panthers. The 31-year-old Grier was a third-round pick of the Panthers in 2019. In his playing career he has had two stints with the Panthers and two with the Cowboys, plus time with the Bengals, Chargers and Eagles.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Tony Romo is arrested for OWI in Milwaukee
summary: Romo is due in court on September 21.
full_text: Former NFL quarterback and No. 1 CBS NFL analyst Tony Romo was arrested in Milwaukee Thursday night for Operating While Intoxicated, first offense. Fox News 6 obtained Romo's arrest detention report. Per the arrest report, Romo was taken into custody after performing poorly on standard field sobriety tests . Romo was booked and released. He's due in court on Monday, September 21. The Fox News 6 report doesn't specify whether Romo submitted to breath testing, or whether he declined. Undrafted in 2003, Romo became the Cowboys' starter during the 2006 season. He retired after the 2016 season, and he immediately became the top analyst at CBS.
author: Mike Florio

title: Patriots second-rounder Gabe Jacas remains unsigned, did not report to camp
summary: The Patriots will hold their first practice of training camp on Saturday and it looks like second-round pick Gabe Jacas will not be part of it.
full_text: ' The Patriots will hold their first practice of training camp on Saturday and it looks like second-round pick Gabe Jacas will not be part of it. Jacas remains unsigned — he is the only unsigned second-round pick in the league — and head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed on Friday that the linebacker did not report to camp. Jacas dealt with a number of injuries this offseason and did not take part in any part of the team's offseason program. Vrabel said he's "positive" that Jacas's contract will get done at some point, but declined to put a timeline on the process. He also said he doesn't know if the rookie is healthy enough to take part in practice. “I can only go by what [Jacas] says. And so when he gets here, we’ll evaluate that,” Vrabel said, via Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald . “Of course, we’ll be as smart as we can just to see because we haven’t seen him with us. But I would say that — I’d use the words cautiously optimistic. But again, those conversations have been great, and excited to see where he’s at.” It's not the ideal way for Jacas to start his NFL career, but getting healthy and on the field as soon as possible would make it easier to turn the rocky beginning around.
author: Josh Alper

title: Drew Allar signs rookie contract with Steelers
summary: And then there was one.
full_text: '' And then there was one. Quarterback Drew Allar has signed his rookie deal with the Steelers, the team announced on Friday. That means Rams quarterback Ty Simpson is the lone remaining unsigned QB from the 2026 draft. Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza and Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck put pen to paper with their respective teams earlier this week. Allar was the No. 78 overall pick in the third round in April after four seasons at Penn State. He is one of four in Pittsburgh’s QBs room, along with Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, and Will Howard.
author: Myles Simmons

title: DeAndre Hopkins working with Patriots coaches, personnel department at training camp
summary: Mike Vrabel has been reunited with another one of his former receivers.
full_text: ' Mike Vrabel has been reunited with another one of his former receivers. But this time, that receiver won't be playing. Vrabel told reporters in his Friday press conference that DeAndre Hopkins will be at Patriots training camp for the next few days, working as a coach and with the personnel department. "Him and I talked, and he asked if he could come hang out for a couple of days, and be around the coaches, and be around the personnel department ," Vrabel said. "I called the league and made sure that was going to be OK. And then I invited him back, and that’s where he’s been the last couple of days and he’ll be here the next couple of days. "[H]e has got coaching gear on and he is helping out the offensive coaches. And meeting with our personnel guys. I mean, he loves football. People that love football and have played the game for the length of time that he did, [he] wants, I think, to explore the opportunities and what that looks like after his playing career is over." Hopkins said in an interview last month that he feels like he has “ a lot of ball left ,” but wasn’t trying to force anything when it comes to being with a team. Hopkins appeared in all 17 games for Baltimore last season, recording 22 catches for 330 yards with a pair of touchdowns.

title: What's next for Diego Pavia?
summary: After failing to win a chance at training camp to secure a spot as one of Lamar Jackson's backups, former Ravens quarterback Diego Pavia has entered the NFL's waiver system.
full_text: ' After failing to win a chance at training camp to secure a spot as one of Lamar Jackson's backups, former Ravens quarterback Diego Pavia has entered the NFL's waiver system. If unclaimed, what's next? He could choose to wait for another NFL opportunity. Injuries could open a door for Pavia to participate in a training camp as an extra arm, which would in turn give him an opportunity to earn a 53-man roster spot or a position on a practice squad. If there's no NFL interest, Pavia could go to the CFL. The Winnipeg Blue Bombers hold his negotiating rights, and they've made it clear that they are interested . The UFL apparently has interest, too — if the social-media team has its finger on the pulse of the league's priorities. The league retweeted the announcement of Pavia's waiver by the Ravens with the eyes emoji . Then there's college football. While he doesn't fit within the NCAA’s new eligibility rule (he turned 20 the year before his four-year college career began), Pavia could try to sue for another season. He played two years of junior-college football before commencing a four-season NCAA career in four years. With every NCAA rule currently subject to an antitrust challenge, Pavia could give it a shot. Of course, the fact that he signed a contract with the Ravens would make it harder. But he didn't get a signing bonus or a game check; at most, he received the standard per diem for his offseason work. It doesn't hurt to try, and it wouldn't be ridiculously expensive (in theory) to hire a lawyer to file the paperwork and roll the dice. Surely, someone would be interested. Pavia finished second in the 2025 Heisman Trophy voting. It's a path to getting more game experience — and to getting paid more than he'd receive in the CFL or the UFL.

title: Mike Vrabel: Christian Gonzalez is here, I expect him to participate
summary: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez has been seeking a new contract throughout the offseason.
full_text: ' Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez has been seeking a new contract throughout the offseason. He did not participate in portions of New England’s voluntary offseason program, though he did attend mandatory minicamp while not participating much on the field. New England head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Friday that Gonzalez officially reported for training camp. “He is here. I expect him to participate ,” Vrabel said. “So, those contract negotiations are ongoing between the club and his agents. And I’m excited about having Christian back here with us and the impact he can make on our football team. Really enjoy the person, enjoy the player, and that’s what I’m looking forward to.” There was reporting earlier this week that part of the hold up for Gonzalez’s new deal is the ongoing negotiations between the Seahawks and cornerback Devon Witherspoon — with whom Gonzalez shares an agent. Vrabel told reporters, however, that it does not have much of an effect. “I don’t think they have anything to do with one another,” Vrabel said. “We’re not negotiating with the Seahawks, we’re negotiating with Christian’s representatives. I don’t think that there’s anything different than just our communication with him.” Gonzalez is slated to make $2.259 million in base salary in 2026. Vrabel said he’s expecting Gonzalez to do more work on the field during camp than he did during the offseason program. “We’re getting ready to prepare to win,” Vrabel said.” And that’s what this is going to take through training camp. We talked about this last year — earning a role, building a team, and preparing to win. And players have an opportunity to earn a role. Coaches are going to be there to help them. We all have to build a team and I have to do my best to prepare us to win by our situations and the way we practice throughout training camp.”

title: Agent's Take: Brandon Aiyuk has only himself to blame for 49ers limbo chaos
summary: The wide receiver remains tied to San Francisco through the reserve/left squad list, and his refusal to seek reinstatement has kept his NFL future frozen
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers report to training camp this weekend, and wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is still under contract. Aiyuk's situation is one of the most bizarre in the salary cap era. He has nobody to blame but himself for his predicament.
The 2023 second team All-Pro's situation with the 49ers reached a point of no return last December when he was placed on the reserve/left squad list after going AWOL. It is rare for a team to put a player on the reserve/left squad list.
In order to be placed on the reserve/left squad list, a team must send a player who has left a letter warning him that he can be put on this list if he doesn't return within five days of his departure (i.e., a five-day letter). The player is prevented from playing for the rest of the season and isn't paid either once placed on this list. The player's contract also tolls, where it is frozen until he resumes playing.
Players on reserve/left squad are deemed retired, according to the NFL Constitution and Bylaws. A retired player must apply to the Commissioner for reinstatement where his last team retains his contractual rights.
Aiyuk likely would have been promptly released by applying for reinstatement at any time during the offseason workout program. The 49ers wouldn't have wanted to be on the hook for $26.15 million of his $27 million 2026 salary if he got hurt on their watch. Had Aiyuk taken this approach, he probably would be with another team, eager to prove that there aren't any ill effects from tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus.
Aiyuk chose to spend his time posting videos and messages on social media rather than taking constructive steps to accelerate his departure from the 49ers. It is believed that Aiyuk still hasn't started the reinstatement process. He has vowed that he will never set foot in the 49ers' facility.
"I will not be reinstating with [the 49ers] nor doing any kind of business with them," Aiyuk said via 49ers Web Zone recently. That's probably going to be a necessity for Aiyuk to resume his NFL career.
Aiyuk took a scorched-earth approach with his social media posts. He is playing the victim and isn't taking any responsibility for his circumstances.
Aiyuk revealed that he rehabbed his knee injury away from the 49ers, which wasn't their preference, and didn't stay in contact with the team during the process. This set the stage for the beginning of the end of Aiyuk's tenure in San Francisco. Under the NFL's Collective Bargaining Agreement, injured players may be required to report to training camp up to five days before the mandatory reporting date for veterans. Given Aiyuk's rehab choices, he should have expected the 49ers to exercise this right.
The 49ers voided the $27 million in 2026 salary guarantees late last July in the four-year, $120 million contract extension Aiyuk signed at the end of August 2024. Contract guarantees are typically voided for an exhaustive list of defaults by a player. Aiyuk has the exact same default language in his contract as All-Pro edge rusher Nick Bosa and Pro Bowl quarterback Brock Purdy .
The most logical explanation is that the voiding resulted from Aiyuk breaching his contract by refusing to show up to training camp early, as required, due to his injury. The 49ers certainly aren't the only NFL team that would have taken this course of action if in those same shoes. Aiyuk also incurred a mandatory $50,000 fine for each day of training camp he missed.
The 49ers already had buyer's remorse about giving Aiyuk a contract extension after contentious negotiations in which he requested a trade and was a training camp hold in. Aiyuk was reportedly put on the trading block at the beginning of the 2025 offseason, but there was a soft trade market because of his knee injury.
Curiously, Aiyuk informed the NFLPA that he didn't want to fight the voiding of his guarantees. Aiyuk alleges that the NFLPA has engaged in a smear campaign to tarnish his image.
It's the NFLPA's job to protect players' rights. The NFLPA will routinely file a grievance on behalf of a player when a team voids salary guarantees, including cases where there isn't a great likelihood of prevailing. Knowing the NFLPA is going to fight can deter teams from overreaching in the future.
Aiyuk blamed his former agent, Athletes First's Ryan Williams, for his problems with the 49ers during the latter part of June. Williams also represents 49ers general manager John Lynch. He was Lynch's marketing agent during his playing career.
Representing a player and a general manager on the same team can be viewed as a conflict of interest. It's permissible under the NFLPA's agent regulations. The agent is required to disclose to the player, in writing, the NFL coaches and front-office personnel he also represents, in an addendum to the representation agreements of players he signs.
Aiyuk claimed he fired Williams in November. Williams was still listed as Aiyuk's agent of record by the NFLPA until the end of June, when Aiyuk sent a written notice as required by their agent regulations. Presumably, Aiyuk told Williams verbally last November that his services were no longer needed. Although Williams hadn't received a termination letter, it's understandable that he wouldn't be trying to protect Aiyuk's interest anymore after such a conversation.
There wasn't anything preventing Williams from making the split official at any time by sending Aiyuk a termination letter. For example, Antonio Brown and Johnny Manziel were fired by their respective agents.
I don't doubt that Aiyuk was told by the NFLPA and/or Williams that he would be released in early June at the latest. That was likely before Aiyuk went AWOL. The 49ers are less inclined to reward what can reasonably be viewed as negative behavior.
It would be in Aiyuk's best interest to get a new agent. At the very least, he should hire a former team executive for a flat fee or on an hourly basis, because his approach on his own is counterproductive.
A new agent or the team executive would surely give Aiyuk the same advice. He needs to apply for reinstatement to get off the reserve/left squad list and show up for training camp. Until Aiyuk does, he will remain in football limbo. The 49ers can effectively squat on his rights where he won't be paid, including a $24.935 million option bonus due Sept. 1 for a fake/dummy 2030 contract year since his contract continues to be tolled. As soon as Aiyuk reports to the 49ers, he will probably be released within the next 24 hours to avoid the payment, since the money is unsecured.
Aiyuk has openly campaigned to play for the Washington Commanders . He just announced on social media that he purchased a home in Northern Virginia for $10 million. That may no longer be an option. Aiyuk appears to have burned a bridge with Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels , who has been a close friend since their playing days together at Arizona State in 2019, and his mother. It's conceivable that Aiyuk and Daniels were trolling the public or have quietly made up behind the scenes.
Aiyuk's eagerness to play specifically for one team and his social media antics have undermined his contract leverage. His best-case scenario, considering his injury, if he had been acting more professionally, probably would have been a one-year contract similar to Odell Beckham Jr.'s in 2023 after missing the entire 2022 season recovering from tearing the ACL in his left knee for a second time during Super Bowl LVI. Beckham signed a one-year, $15 million contract worth up to $18 million through incentives with the Baltimore Ravens .
It wouldn't be surprising for Aiyuk to sign an incentive-laden one-year deal at or near his $1.215 million league minimum salary. Of course, that's predicated on Aiyuk getting reinstated. There is some speculation that Aiyuk's social media posts have raised enough red flags to deter any team from signing him.
Sometimes, silence is golden. Aiyuk should start taking that notion to heart if he's truly interested in…
author: Joel Corry

title: Rams are unprecedented Super Bowl favorites, but history offers a stark warning
summary: The Rams have Matthew Stafford, Myles Garrett, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, but past overwhelming Super Bowl favorites have rarely lived up to the hype
full_text:
On paper, the Los Angeles Rams have arguably the best roster in the NFL . They boast the reigning MVP in Matthew Stafford , the reigning Defensive Player of the Year in Myles Garrett and one of the top receiving duos in the NFL with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams .
If there was one roster hole going into the offseason, it was at cornerback. They quickly fixed that by stealing two players from Kansas City: They made a trade for Trent McDuffie and then signed Jaylen Watson .
Basically, the Rams' roster is absolutely stacked, and because of that, Sean McVay's team is an overwhelming favorite to win Super Bowl LXI.
As a matter of fact, the Rams are an unprecedented favorite to win the Super Bowl this year.
Let's check out the top five favorites (odds via FanDuel ):
1. Rams (+550) 2. Bills (+1000) 3. Ravens (+1100) 4. Seahawks (+1200) T-5. Chiefs (+1600) T-5. Chargers (+1600)
Since the NFL expanded to 32 teams in 2002, this marks just the fifth time that we've seen an overwhelming Super Bowl favorite like this with odds under +1000. It's just the second time for an NFC team.
Being a heavy favorite can create crushing expectations, and sometimes it can be difficult to live up to them. If you need proof, just look at the other four teams that have gone through what the Rams are about to go through.
Here are the previous four instances where there was only one team with preseason odds under +1000 (odds via Pro Football Reference ).
Super Bowl odds: +800 Over/under: 10.5 wins
Coming off their Super Bowl win in 2002, the Bucs were expected to make a run at another Lombardi Trophy. Their season fell apart quickly. They got off to a 2-1 start, but after a Week 4 bye, their season came crashing down. In Week 5, Tampa Bay blew a historic lead against Peyton Manning's Colts : The Bucs led 35-14 with just four minutes left in a game they eventually lost 38-35. They dropped the Bucs to 2-2, and they eventually finished 7-9 on the season.
The Bucs were the favorites to make the Super Bowl, but in the end, they didn't even make the playoffs. The Rams are the first NFC team in 23 years to be an overwhelming Super Bowl favorite, and as we can see here, things didn't work out so well for the last NFC team to be in this situation.
Super Bowl odds: +450 Over/under: 11.5
Tom Brady missed the 2008 season after tearing his ACL in Week 1, but that didn't slow down the Patriots . With Matt Cassel running the show, they won 11 games. In 2009, the Pats got their legendary QB back on the field, and when that happened, the thought was that New England was going to steamroll the competition, but that's not exactly what happened. With Brady back in the lineup, the Patriots went just 10-6, which means they didn't even match their win total from 2008. To make matters worse, they didn't even make it past the opening round of the playoffs. During the wild-card round, the Pats were absolutely destroyed 33-14 by the Ravens after falling behind 24-0.
Super Bowl odds: +800 Over/under: 10.5
The Patriots were the Super Bowl favorite in 2009, but they didn't make it to the big game. Instead, it was Peyton Manning and the Colts who came out of the AFC (They lost to the saints in Super Bowl XLIV). Manning and the Colts went 14-2 in 2009, which set the stage for oddsmakers to crown them as the overwhelming Super Bowl favorite in 2010.
The Colts had sky-high expectations, and they were viewed as a heavy favorite to get back to the big game, but that didn't happen. In Manning's final healthy season with the team, the Colts finished 10-6, and they didn't come close to sniffing the Super Bowl after a shocking 17-16 loss to the Jets in the wild-card round.
Super Bowl odds: +600 Over/under: 11
The 2018 Patriots were the only team that could handle the expectations that come with being an overwhelming Super Bowl favorite. Although the Patriots were viewed as the best team going into the season, it was the Chiefs who ended up earning the No. 1 overall seed in the AFC, and they did that in Patrick Mahomes ' first year as the team's starter.
In the playoffs, the 11-5 Patriots had to travel to Kansas City for the AFC title game in what ended up being an all-time classic with New England coming out on top, 37-31, in overtime.
One of the most infamous plays from that game came when Dee Ford jumped offside with roughly a minute left to play in the fourth quarter, and the Chiefs were up 28-24. The penalty nullified a Brady interception, which set the stage for New England's dramatic win.
The Chiefs would be headed to Super Bowl LIII...if only Dee Ford had not lined up offsides. 🤦 pic.twitter.com/mIuuL1W2O7
In the Super Bowl, the Patriots beat the Rams 13-3 to give Tom Brady and Bill Belichick their final Lombardi Trophy together.
When you're the Super Bowl favorite, you have high expectations, but when you're an overwhelming favorite, the expectations that come with that can crush you, and history shows that.
When you look at the four big Super Bowl favorites that came before the Rams, all four of them fell short of expectations during the regular season. Three of the four teams finished under their projected win total, while the 2018 Patriots pushed, so none of them hit the over. The Rams' over/under has been set at 11.5, and although the over feels like a lock, history has shown that the teams perceived to be the best can sometimes stumble.
The Rams came one game short of making the Super Bowl last year, but it's worth noting that their 2025 season nearly derailed before it even started. Stafford missed most of training camp with a back injury last season, and if that flares up on him this year, that would be a serious problem for the Rams. Stafford made it through the 2025 season unscathed, but he always seems to be thinking about his back. At the NFL Honors ceremony in February, he half-jokingly mentioned his back when he was asked how he felt about the Rams' Week 1 game in Australia.
"Seems like a long flight," Stafford said. "I hope my back's not too sore afterwards, to be honest with you."
Even if Stafford and the Rams stay healthy, getting to the Super Bowl won't be easy. They play in one of football's toughest divisions, which just happens to include the defending Super Bowl champs. The Seahawks won the Lombardi Trophy, but it's the Rams who have the giant target on their back thanks to their status as the unprecedented Super Bowl favorite.

title: Ranking top five rookie tight ends by projected 2026 NFL production
summary: As tight end usage continues to rise across the NFL, which first-year playmakers are poised to make the biggest impact on your favorite team?
full_text:
Tight end usage is on the rise. In fact, the league utilized two-plus tight ends on 33.2% of offensive snaps last season, according to TruMedia; a full 3% higher than the previous high set in 2024 over the past 10 years. Over the same time period, four of the 10 best seasons, in terms of receiving yards, by a rookie tight end occurred last season.
There were 22 tight ends selected as part of the 2026 NFL Draft , including nine in the top-100 overall.
Will Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq follow in the footsteps of last year's first-round selections, Tyler Warren and Colston Loveland ? Will there be non-first-round selections to make an impact in the pass game just as Harold Fannin Jr . and Oronde Gadsden had in 2025?
Here are my top five rookie tight ends for the 2026 NFL season based upon anticipated production:
All five members of the list were drafted in the top 100 overall. The fifth and final spot on the list really boiled down to opportunity. In Chicago, Sam Roush has to contend with Cole Kmet and Colston Loveland. Los Angeles has a quartet of other useful tight ends, including last year's second-round selection Terrance Ferguson and now Max Klare . The Texans have Dalton Schultz and Cade Stover , in addition to third-round pick Marlin Klein . The Saints drafted Oscar Delp in the third round, but he joins Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant .
Hunter Henry has recorded at least 35 receptions in every season he has been healthy, but that dates back to when the Chargers were still in San Diego. Henry is closer to the end of his career than the beginning and Raridon is the heir apparent. New England was below average in terms of two-plus tight end usage last season, according to TruMedia.
CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project Raridon to record 22 receptions for 241 yards and two touchdowns, which would be equivalent to 55.8 fantasy points.
Boerkircher was the third tight end off the board and the subject of consensus big board discourse. Jacksonville will likely be motivated to validate its choice. The Texas A&M product is more adept as a blocker, so his impact on the game may not be as obvious as others on this list.
The Jaguars utilized two-plus tight ends on 24.9% of their snaps last season, according to TruMedia, which was the ninth-lowest in the league. The presence of Boerkircher, combined with Brenton Strange , almost certainly ensures that figure will rise this season.
CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project him to record 32 receptions for 237 yards and 2 touchdowns this season, equivalent to 54.1 fantasy points in a PPR league.
Stowers is a former college quarterback who is still developing his body and learning the tight end position. His athleticism and contributions in the pass game are his most endearing traits at this stage of his career, but that one-dimensional play style may prevent him from being on the field every down, which limits potential production.
Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion comes over from Green Bay, where they had ranked No. 15 in usage of two-plus tight ends, according to TruMedia. 31-year-old Dallas Goedert is expected to be the team's primary outlet at the position.
CBS Sports' fantasy football experts predict 31 receptions for 322 yards and two touchdowns for Stowers.
Kacmarek was one of eight tight ends picked on Day 2. Despite being more of a predominant blocker in college, Kacmarek has fewer roadblocks to targets this season. His competition at tight end involves Greg Dulcich and Ben Sims as opposed to Goedert, Strange or Johnson. The talent at wide receiver is uninspiring as well after shipping Jaylen Waddle to Denver. The franchise is tasked with replacing 51.7% of its targets from last season.
Kacmarek has the second-highest projected point total among rookie tight ends (83.3). CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project 35 receptions for 327 yards and three touchdowns.
Sadiq was the only tight end drafted in the top-50 overall, which is essentially the only reason for him being at the top of the list. New York used a second-round pick on LSU tight end Mason Taylor a year ago, and offensive coordinator Frank Reich has not been known for his innovative thinking in recent years.
Dating back to 2016, there have been 11 tight ends taken in the first round. Those players averaged 59.4 receptions for 705.5 yards and 4 touchdowns as rookies.
CBS Sports' fantasy football experts project 47 receptions for 527 yards and six touchdowns. He ranks No. 23 among all tight ends with 133.7 projected points.

Kyle Odegard, the former Arizona Cardinals beat writer (and employee of the Cardinals) talked about those three, because to be fair no one has any idea what is happening with Josh Sweat, and his take was the first time I have seen him praise Monti Ossenfort . The Arizona Cardinals’ general manager is 15-36 in his three seasons at the helm, and his team is projected to be the worst in the NFL in Year 4. Based on a juggernaut early-season schedule, it wouldn’t be a surprise if Ossenfort gets canned before Halloween. And I’d be shocked if he is retained for a fifth year. All that being said, he’s done a good job in contract negotiations this offseason… From Odegard on Brissett: While coach Mike LaFleur said negotiations are ongoing with Brissett, the Cardinals spoke loudly by slotting in Minshew with the first-team at the start of the drills. The message: We may give you a few bucks, Jacoby, but nothing close to what you want. The Cardinals are not winning many games with or without Brissett this season, so it’s the smart play. Brissett has no leverage, and Ossenfort must stand his ground even if the noise grows louder. That is just it. While people have said they need to give Brissett a raise since he is the starter, the reality is they don’t. The team looked everywhere for a replacement, then drafted Carson Beck, and only then begrudgingly made it seem like Brissett may be the starter. But here is the reality. Brissett would have to start at least six games, keep them all competitive, and actually win some of them to hold off any changes. If the Cardinals are 1-5 or worse, even if they are “competitive” in some games like last year, the calls will grow louder for a change at quarterback. So, why pay “starter money” for that? If they want to give Brissett a bump up to the $8-10 million range, then do it, but there is no reason to go to his “ $15 million will get it done ” when you are talking about a guy who may start eight games this year. Odegard on Michael Wilson: But there was more than meets the eye there, as Wilson put up incredible numbers down the stretch when Marvin Harrison Jr. was injured and the Cardinals became extremely pass-happy. When Trey McBride and Harrison, Jr. were both healthy, Wilson was the quieter third option. Wilson seems like a great person and a good receiver, but he doesn’t have the same quick-twitch movements of an unquestioned star. If Ossenfort agreed to an extension, it would have been a buy-high scenario, so he was smart to wait to see if Wilson can duplicate those results in 2026. This is an interesting one. Both sides seem like they want to get something done, but neither side wants to do it right now. Wilson’s side of things is he could produce another 1,000+ yard season and break the bank. The Cardinals side is, why pay for this receiver now? Not saying they won’t extend Wilson, but if Marv breaks out, and Wilson is the sidekick, then why are you paying him? You know the offense will run through WR1, Trey McBride and eventually Jeremiyah Love. You have time, no need to hurry to extend Wilson. Odegard on Paris: If Ossenfort does dole one out, this is the easy call. Johnson has top-10 draft pick pedigree, is durable and has a high ceiling. He also plays a premium position that needs to be locked down for whenever the Cardinals do find a franchise quarterback. But Johnson hasn’t quite reached Pro Bowl level performance yet, and with a fifth-year option available, the Cardinals do have time to wait this out and make sure he elevates to a star. My singular quibble is that Paris has not been durable. Everything else is accurate, especially the last piece, he has not hit the ceiling that he needs to and having the fifth year option is the right way to approach this. While Paris has played in 43 career games, his only full season was his rookie season, and he has gotten hurt trying to hold up at the more premiere left tackle position. While expecting anyone, let alone an offensive lineman to play 17 games a year is a lot to ask, I like to look at 15 games as full seasons. PJJ has one of those as well, hitting 14 his second year and a career low 12 last year. Take the time, make sure he can give you the 15+ games this year at a consistently high level, then make him one of, if not the highest paid tackles in the NFL. What are your thoughts?

title: Cardinals roster: Training Camp OG Outlook
summary: The Arizona Cardinals version of an NFL team in 2026 is a lot better than this year’s edition. Last year, the running back room was decimated via injury, as well as the offensive line. GM Monti Ossenfort did a good job at attempting to fix the offensive line. He saw that right tackle was a […]
full_text: Arizona Cardinals offensive lineman Chase Bisontis (57) Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The Arizona Cardinals version of an NFL team in 2026 is a lot better than this year’s edition. Last year, the running back room was decimated via injury, as well as the offensive line. GM Monti Ossenfort did a good job at attempting to fix the offensive line. He saw that right tackle was a problem. He identified that both guard spots were an issue. Ossenfort took a good effort and did not bring back Evan Brown, Kelvin Beachum, and Jonah Williams. RELATED: ADAMS ARRESTED FOR GUN POSSESSION Numerous players were signed during free agency and then selected in April’s NFL draft. Now that training camp is here, what battles for positions will this year’s Cardinals offensive line become involved in? This training camp has a lot riding on getting this group into a productive unit. The new offense wants to run the ball a lot more than before. It takes good bodies in the room. Preseason games will tell what is going on. A new head coach, Mike LaFleur, plus a new offensive scheme, is being installed. Ahead of training camp opening, let’s look at the offensive guard group. This year’s group has a lot riding on it. There should be a lot of improvement with this group. New this year is Kendrick Bourne, signed during free agency from the San Francisco 49ers, Riggie Virgil, who was chosen in Round 5 of the NFL draft, along with undrafted rookie Harrison Wallace, III. Cardinals’ OG depth chart Right guard: Chase Bisonti, backup Isaiah Adams, Matt Pryor Left guard: Issac Seumalo, backup Jon Gaines II Best expectations? Seumalo was absolutely the splash of free agency for Arizona. Complete stud for the offensive guard position. His signing alone will change the narrative along the offensive line. Now, the rookie Bisontis, who was selected in Round 2, will become the Wild Card along the line. He will be given every opportunity to win the right guard spot this year. If he can come through and provide the production he did in college, Ossenfort will have fixed both guard positions in one swoop this year. Pryor is another great signing. He can come in at any time and play either guard position. However, he will push Bisontis for starting reps and could end up with the job. Adams was also penciled in to compete, but with his recent arrest, we will see how that plays out. He was the darling of the line in training camp, and did well in preseason games while facing each team’s second- and third-string defensive players. But once the season began with the regular defensive starters, he struggled. Mightily. This may become a three-player battle throughout training camp. Gaines will most likely become the key backup again this year, but has one more year of experience. This group should shine as long as everyone remains vertical. This offense will want to run effectively and throw the ball in short and intermediate passing zones. This means the amount of time to throw becomes minimal. Worst case? Just like Adams had a great training camp last year but struggled in real games, that very well could be what happens to Biscontis. Even though he played in a tough conference, this is big boy football now. 2026 version? This group will need to learn this new offense and lead the way. Effective runs up the middle are going to be the norm. Jon Gaines is an adequate backup, having played in 30 NFL games, but with only five starts. Signing Pryor this year is a huge advantage, giving the offensive line a guy who can play all three interior positions. These two make the depth way ahead of last year’s line options. We will have to see how the legal issues with Adams play out. He has been viewed in the mix for the starting job, which may now change. He struggled early last year, then played the remainder of the schedule after Will Hernandez was injured and was thrown back onto the field. The dark horse here is Bisontis. If he kills it in training camp, the line’s overall view will increase. Seumalo is a steady player who is durable and really strong.
author: Barry Shuck

title: Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett at training camp. Is he working or watching?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals opened 2026 training camp with a lot on their minds. Like, installing a new offense. A new coach, OC, and special teams coordinator. Guys who are now healthy for the defensive backfield, and maybe nobody injured right away. There were a few players who have already been added to the PUP list. […]
full_text: Jul 23, 2026; Glendale, AZ, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) during training camp at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The Arizona Cardinals opened 2026 training camp with a lot on their minds. Like, installing a new offense. A new coach, OC, and special teams coordinator. Guys who are now healthy for the defensive backfield, and maybe nobody injured right away. There were a few players who have already been added to the PUP list. This link describes all those types of issues: RELATED: NEWS FROM CARDINALS TRAINING CAMP While the defense had its issues last year, the offense has been on everyone’s mind going into camp this year. Playing in the NFC West Division, the Cardinals have front-row seats to both the Los Angeles Rams’ and San Francisco 49ers’ offensive outputs. Arizona’s new head coach, Mike LaFleur, was employed by both clubs and is part of their extensive coaching trees. The Cardinals offense will look like both of these clubs’ offenses. Eventually. Maybe. Hopefully. What was the question? Having said this, it isn’t as simple as substituting Splenda for sugar while making Kool-Aid. This new offense is complicated. It is new, and so is the terminology and scheme. These players have better been studying during the 40-days away from the training facility. Three quarterbacks, journeyman Gardner Minshew, veteran Kedon Slovis, and rookie Carson Beck, have arrived early during OTAs and spent every moment on the field. They have attended each minicamp and class meetings. Do these three have this offense down pat? Of course not, but they have been working that clutch in grandad’s old truck instead of crying that it isn’t an automatic transmission. New stuff takes time to adjust – and learn. Jacoby Brissett has missed all of this. The only appearance he has made up until the beginning of camp was as a ball boy during the mandatory minicamp. “I’m just here so I won’t get fined.” Yeah, something like that. But lo and behold, Brissett has shown up for the Cardinals’ training camp. Or should we say, “Well, he’s here.” On Thursday, Brissett worked out in his first practice session of 2026. Word is, his desire to have his contract reworked with added years and/or an additional bump in salary remains in the same spot it has always been. In limbo. He is appearing at practice despite not signing a restructured deal. Hmmm….. According to team sources, the contract negotiations are ongoing. Now, Brissett is his own agent, right? If he knows his number and the number of years he wants attached, why is this still ongoing? Exactly what is the roadblock? Because all of us regular folk understand the process between agents – who are attorneys – and a team’s GM. It’s friggin’ back and forth with wants, desires, and demands until one side or the other (usually both) caves in and gets less than they wanted. However, in the duel between Brissett and Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort, there aren’t any lawyers involved. Brissett is a communications major out of NC State. Ossenfort earned two master’s degrees in business administration and sports management while at Ohio University. God made the Earth, but attorneys run it. So, what’s the issue? On July 9, Arizona safety Budda Baker tweeted out: “Just want bro to get his (expletive) done… he is not asking for what you think. Bro is asking for below the bare minimum. Let’s just get it done!!! At the end of the day, I want all of our players to get theirs and ultimately all of our players to be in the building, being able to practice (and) being able to get better because you only get better by practicing.” A day to before the Cardinals report, and there is not yet a resolution to Jacoby Brissett’s contract situation. AZ and Brissett (who is his own agent) have been actively negotiating for the last several months and agree he’s due a raise. No consensus yet on the number. https://t.co/GwHgf03Rlq — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) July 21, 2026 Both sides seem to be in agreement that Brissett deserves more money than the backup position deal he signed last year. LaFleur was asked about the contract status. He told ESPN Arizona : “It’s been productive between us and his team, so still ongoing, but I’d say we’re productive.” Meanwhile, back on the practice field. When the four quarterbacks were getting reps, no matter what the drill was, Brissett was last. Remember when the Cardinals ditched Kyler Murray after LaFleur was hired? Recall that LaFleur came right out and announced that Brissett was his starting quarterback for the season? Which raises the question: Is the starting job now up for competition among all four QBs? Well, of course, LaFleur was asked about this. His response? “I’d describe it as practice one on July 23.” Another moment to go hmmm….. LaFleur did state that he is doing everything he can to help Brissett as these sessions roll along. And he should. It is not his fault that his presumed starting quarterback hasn’t been around. And it’s not like LaFleur doesn’t see Brissett as the probable starter for the Week 1 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers. Maybe he still does. Maybe LaFleur is frustrated with the whole ordeal and was hoping that being an NFL head coach was going to come with a lot less drama. After all, didn’t they cut the drama, who then signed with the Minnesota Vikings? Another hmmm…..? LaFleur’s job at this juncture with 90 players in camp is to do everything himself and his coaching staff can to field the best Arizona team they can place on the pitch (yes, still have some World Cup feelings lingering). If that is Brissett under center, or someone else, now that Brissett has bit the bullet and showed up regardless of if he gets what he wants or not, the coaches can’t really harp on what his quarterback has or has not done in these past few months. Can he catch up? Can he excel beyond the other three guys? LaFleur added: “Not really worried about that stuff right now. It’s just about building that one day at a time and seeing how good we can be every single day. We need to have the best first block we can without pads. And then we put the pads on; now we get to play a little bit more real football, and we don’t have to peak on July 30 or whenever.” Right now, Brissett isn’t competing against Minshew, Slovis, or Beck. He is competing against himself and the Week 1 timeline.

title: Beatdown roundtable: favorite almost-draft pick in Ravens history
summary: Baltimore Beatdown is all about Almost Ravens this week! In addition to our reader-driven bracket narrowing down the biggest near-acquisitions in team history, our staff will also be providing their opinions on their favorite moves the Ravens almost pulled off. Today, we’re focusing on trades: This one is easy. Imagine a prime Cooper Kupp as […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 08: Cooper Kupp #10 and Puka Nacua #17 of the Los Angeles Rams come to the line of scrimmage during a 44-42 win over the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on December 08, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Beatdown is all about Almost Ravens this week! In addition to our reader-driven bracket narrowing down the biggest near-acquisitions in team history, our staff will also be providing their opinions on their favorite moves the Ravens almost pulled off. Today, we’re focusing on trades: This one is easy. Imagine a prime Cooper Kupp as Lamar Jackson’s WR1 from 2019 to 2021. He was one of the most complete receivers in the game and could have been the kind of do-it-all target Jackson has never really had in his career. Does he still hit his receiving Triple Crown in Baltimore? Probably not, but Kupp was the kind of difference-maker that could have changed the outcome of a playoff game or two. – Nikhil Mehta My favorite player the Ravens almost drafted is Puka Nacua. Nobody predicted Nacua would instantly become one of the league’s top wide receivers, evidenced by him falling to the fifth round, but he’s exceeded expectations in a major way. The Ravens selected CB Kyu Blu Kelly at No. 157 overall, 20 picks earlier then Nacua was drafted by the Los Angeles Rams. Blu Kelly went on to be released by the Ravens before Week 1. Nacua would have been a huge weapon for Lamar Jackson and an ideal fit alongside Zay Flowers as an elite possession-catch threat. Instead, the Ravens have struggled to get consistent production from their supporting wideouts over the last few seasons. – Frank Platko I could do Jalen Ramsey here again, but I’m more upset that the Ravens never traded for Ramsey after the fact, considering they got Ronnie Stanley in the 2016 draft. The one I think about a lot is the 2010 draft and both Dez Bryant and Rob Gronkowski. It was also no secret that the Ravens coveted Dez Bryant in that draft, and probably would have taken him with their 25th overall pick but the Cowboys traded up to the 24th pick and nabbed him. Then, the Ravens nearly drafted Gronk…twice. Gronkowski recently told a story where he said the Ravens were going to pick him at #25 overall in 2010 draft, likely their top option once Bryant was taken. Instread of drafting Gronk once they were on the clock, the Broncos traded up with the Ravens to take that pick and draft Tim Tebow. Later, in the second round, the Ravens were prepared to take Gronk once again at #43 overall, probably thrilled that he had fallen so far after prepping to take him with the 25th pick. Instead, history will remember the Patriots swooping at 42, drafting the tight end, and the Patriot dynasty continued for another near-decade. You have to wonder what Joe Flacco and the Ravens could have accomplished with such a dominate tight end, a favorite position for Flacco to target. And maybe wonder what would have happened with the Tom Brady and Patriots without Gronk in New England. Instead the Ravens lost two high impact receiving threats that would go on to become legends in the game. – Zach Canter I have to go with Rob Gronkoswki here. Possibly the greatest tight end in NFL history was so close to being a Baltimore Raven. Instead, Gronk’s name is forever etched in history as a key figure in the Patriots’ dynasty. While the Ravens certainly had quality tight ends over the years after failing to draft Gronk, you have to imagine just how much he could have helped Joe Flacco in the passing game as Baltimore struggled to field quality wide receiver corps following the 2012 Super Bowl. Not to mention Gronk’s dominance as a run blocker, which would have obviously fit in perfectly with the Ravens. – Dustin Cox Who is the biggest Almost-Raven in franchise history? | Baltimore Beatdown
