Mandatory Credit: Chris Jones-Imagn Images | Chris Jones-Imagn Images Ask anyone which Dallas Cowboys defensive rookie they are most excited to see throughout training camp and you will get the same answer over and over: Caleb Downs. This is the right answer, to be clear. Downs is projected as a generational player and is set to transform what the Cowboys are able to do on the defensive side of the ball. Watching him in action with the rest of the team is going to be incredible and help justify the lofty beliefs that we have in him. If you ask someone to mix it up though you will probably hear about Jaishawn Barham. The Cowboys have a need at linebacker and he may fit the mold that new defensive coordinator Christian Parker is lookig for there, so excitement is also warranted with him. We often talk about how difficult it is to fly under the radar as a member of the Cowboys, but first-rounder Malachi Lawrence may be doing that thanks to what’s going on around him. How he fares is going to be an essential part of the team’s overall defensive story this season. Recently I was scheduled to interview Malachi while he was at Great Wolf Lodge Grapevine as a part of a special charity challenge benefitting Make-A-Wish North Texas. Unfortunately we were not able to make it fully happen in a traditional sense, but Malachi and the Great Wolf Lodge team got creative and had him answer some questions that I posed to him. You can watch his answers in those videos, but here are the relevant quotes. Malachi on his goals for the season: My goals are really just to get better, 1% every day. You know, keep continuing to learn from our vets. They’ve been telling me some great things and I believe in them. Malachi on who he has been bonding with so far, whether rookie or veterans: I’ve been bonding with both. From my rookies like LT Overton, Caleb Downs, Anthony Smith… we’ve been bowling. And some from my vets like RG [Rashan Gary], EZ [Donovan Ezeiruaku], Sam [Williams], just guys in my room and it’s been a great experience. Malachi on what his impression has been of Christian Parker: It’s been great. He believes that we are a great group from top to bottom from where it starts, from the D-line to the secondary. And so we’re just coming together, building that bond, building that culture, and it’s just the identity, like he wants guys that are just versatile but also do their job. As noted, Malachi was interacting with children as a part of the event in question. It looks like it was a rather great time. Let’s see how camp goes for the young rookie.

title: Cowboys 2026 roster rundown: WR George Pickens
summary: Since the 2000s began, the Cowboys have had several trades for big-name wide receivers. It’s still too early to make an official proclamation, but so far, the trade for George Pickens is looking like it may be the most successful. Our rundown series now comes to one of Dallas’ brightest stars, and perhaps their most […]
full_text: Since the 2000s began, the Cowboys have had several trades for big-name wide receivers. It’s still too early to make an official proclamation, but so far, the trade for George Pickens is looking like it may be the most successful. Our rundown series now comes to one of Dallas’ brightest stars, and perhaps their most talked-about player this offseason. Background Years in NFL: 4 Acquired by: Trade (2025) 2022 was a year of sweeping change for the Pittsburgh Steelers. Ben Roethlisberger retired, there was a new general manager, and the receiver position was also in flux. George Pickens was part of this new offensive era, a second-round pick to go with first-round quarterback Kenny Pickett. Unlike the rookie QB, Pickens was an immediate contributor in a trio with Diontae Johnson and Chase Claypool. Pittsburgh traded Claypool away in November, leaving Johnson and Pickens as the clear starting duo. For three years, Pickens’ talent was clear but so were issues with his maturity and relationship with the Steelers. The team struggled to find its next QB, going through the poo-poo platter of Pickett, Mitch Trubisky, and Mason Rudolph before bringing in Russell Wilson in 2023. While Wilson helped bring some respectability back at QB, Pickens’ status with the team was already breaking down. Criticism of his effort became public, and he went into his fourth year without a clear path forward in Pittsburgh. As it turned out, the path led to Dallas. Pickens and a 2027 sixth-round pick were sent to the Cowboys for a 2026 third-rounder and Dallas’ fifth-round pick in 2027. For the Steelers, it was a decent return on a former second-rounder who they clearly had no intention of re-signing after his rookie deal. For the Cowboys, it was an immediate upgrade at WR2 and a much-needed wingman for CeeDee Lamb, who’d been carrying too much of the receiving load since the departure of Amari Cooper and the decline of Michael Gallup. For Pickens, the fresh start was clearly needed. Whether it was a new set of coaches, the pressure from his expiring contract, finally having the right QB in Dak Prescott, or all of the above, Pickens exploded in 2025 with new career highs of 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. He went to his first Pro Bowl and was a Second-Team All-Pro. In one year, Pickens went from the Steelers’ chopping block to the Cowboys’ franchise tag. A long-term deal was not reached this offseason, but Pickens reported to all mandatory activities and has said he’s ready to be at camp and play 2026 on the franchise tag. Even with the contract issue, Pickens’ relationship with Dallas seems undamaged and there’s plenty of excitement for his second season. Contract Status Years Left: 1 2026 Cap Hit: $27.3 million Honestly, we’ve been waiting to do this one until we saw how the contract negotiations played out. But as of July 15th, the window for franchised players to sign a long-term deal closed and Pickens is now locked in to the franchise deal for 2026. We’ll circle back to this circus next February/March. 2026 Projections Role: Starting WR Roster Chance: 100% We have one of those “great problems to have” with the rising debate over who the Cowboys’ true franchise receiver is between Pickens and Lamb. How you feel about it depends on what you value in a receiver, and much credit you give one guy’s presence to helping the other thrive. In the end, does it even matter? Dallas has two receivers that would be the clear number one for most NFL teams, so let’s just enjoy it. One of the fascinating things to watch in 2026 will be how defenses adjust to Pickens’ breakout. Does he get increased attention, making life easier for Lamb? Do teams commit so much to stopping the superstar receivers that guys like Ryan Flournoy and Jake Ferguson have huge years? Will Dallas’ running backs be the biggest beneficiaries from high concern over the passing attack? Without a doubt, Pickens’ presence makes all of this possible. As good as Lamb was from 2022-2024, Pickens’ arrival opened things up and helped make the offense much less predictable. It also helped that Brian Schottenheimer was here for the locker room side, probably a much better coach for Pickens than Mike McCarthy would have been. In life and in football, not everyone is suited for everyone. For whatever reasons, Pittsburgh wasn’t the right fit for Pickens at that point in his career. And for at least one season, his new relationship with Dallas was mutually beneficial. If it stays that way this season, maybe the courtship will become a marriage in 2027. title: One prediction for training camp, inside linebackers edition
summary: Our Dallas Cowboys training camp prediction series continues. Today we will analyze a position of great importance on the defensive side of the ball – the interior linebackers. The Cowboys defense has gone through significant changes in the offseason. Gone is Matt Eberflus. Replacing him is Christian Parker, who has fundamentally changed how the defense […]
full_text: Michigan linebacker Jaishawn Barham (1) sacks Central Michigan quarterback Joe Labas (2)during the first half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 13, 2025. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Our Dallas Cowboys training camp prediction series continues. Today we will analyze a position of great importance on the defensive side of the ball – the interior linebackers. The Cowboys defense has gone through significant changes in the offseason. Gone is Matt Eberflus. Replacing him is Christian Parker, who has fundamentally changed how the defense lines up by shifting to a base 3-4. With this shift, the role of linebacker has not only expanded but also insulated the interior backers, which anybody could tell you was a significant weakness last year. Personnel changes have also followed. Draft capital was spent this year to address some of the issues this group had last season. Dee Winters was brought here for a fifth-round pick, and the Cowboys spent their third-round pick in this year’s draft to select Jaishawn Barham. Although Winters could become the lead backer on this defense, it’s Barham who is arguably the most intriguing player within this group. Barham is a physical specimen who can play both off-the-ball linebacker and the edge. In fact, many teams had him as an edge rusher in the draft. As for now, the Cowboys have him listed as an interior linebacker, and the idea is that he will likely be a chess piece that Dallas uses all over the field. At 6’3” 240 lbs., Barham has the prototypical size that defensive coordinators dream about, but it’s the explosiveness that stands out. The ability to beat blockers paired with a high motor will stand out at camp and force the Cowboys to not only get him as many snaps as possible but also help him get to the quarterback at a high clip. Prediction: Jaishawn Barham will secure five sacks in his rookie campaign We see Barham as being a weapon that Parker deploys in many ways, but he will be part of the pass rush and blitz packages a lot more than the other interior linebackers. Given his background rushing the passer in college, we predict big things for him in the pass rush part of the game. Agree or disagree? How do you think Barham will play in 2026?

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 51
summary: It is Day 51 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: Oct 9, 1977; St. Louis, MO, USA; FILE PHOTO; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Roger Staubach (12) in action against the St. Louis Cardinals at Busch Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Herb Weitman-Imagn Images It is Day 51 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. Settle in and get ready for Day 51 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit a non-playoff win that still captures exactly what the 1977 Cowboys were becoming. Dallas hosted the Detroit Lions in Week 7, entered the day unbeaten, and left with massive victory that pushed the Cowboys to 7-0. It was not a postseason classic or a rivalry drama game. It was simply a championship team taking care of business with total control. Sunday, October 30, 1977 — 2:00 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 37, Detroit Lions 0 The first quarter was quiet, with Efren Herrera giving Dallas a 3-0 lead on a 21-yard field goal. Then the Cowboys broke the game open in the second quarter. Herrera added another field goal, Roger Staubach found Billy Joe DuPree for a 14-yard touchdown, then hit Scott Laidlaw for an 18-yard score. Another Herrera field goal made it 23-0 by halftime. Detroit had already been swallowed up by the moment. Dallas kept control after the break. Staubach threw his third touchdown of the day, a one-yard pass to Jay Saldi, pushing the lead to 30-0 in the third quarter. In the fourth, Larry Brinson finished the scoring with a 20-yard touchdown run. The Cowboys did not need anything dramatic. They scored through special teams, the passing game, the ground game, and a defense that never let Detroit breathe. Staubach was extremely sharp and efficient, completing 16 of 25 passes for 179 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions. Tony Dorsett was not the dominant rushing force in this one, finishing with 48 yards on 13 carries, but he was heavily involved as a receiver with five catches for 48 yards. That versatility was part of what made Dallas so difficult to defend during his rookie season. The defense was the real statement. Detroit finished with just 120 total yards, only seven first downs, and three turnovers. Joe Reed and Greg Landry combined for only 78 passing yards, and the Lions never found any rhythm. Mark Washington and Mike Hegman each had an interception for Dallas, while Detroit punted nine times. This was the Doomsday Defense doing what it did best, squeezing an opponent until the scoreboard told the story. This game belongs on the countdown because it reflects the regular-season dominance of the 1977 Cowboys. That team finished 12-2, rolled through the NFC playoffs, and beat the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl XII. Games like this were the foundation of that run. Dallas did not merely beat Detroit, it made the Lions look completely overmatched. For a non-playoff game, that kind of shutout dominance from a championship team deserves its place on the countdown. #Cowboys vs #Lions 1977 Week 7 Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 37, Detroit Lions 0 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/kaqu2X0nRG — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) July 23, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The 1977 Cowboys led the NFC in points scored and gave up only 212 points during the regular season. The shutout of Detroit was one of the clearest regular-season examples of how balanced that Super Bowl team was. title: Power ranking the Cowboys roster before training camp
summary: The Dallas Cowboys begin their odyssey towards the 2026 season next week with the opening of training camp. A lot of new pieces have been added to the roster, and bad players from last year are no longer with the team. Brian Schottenheimer’s first season as head coach ended with a losing record, but there […]
full_text: OXNARD, CA - AUGUST 05: Dallas Cowboys defensive end Earnest Brown IV (51) during the Los Angeles Rams - Dallas Cowboys joint Training Camp on August 05, 2025, at the River Ridge Playing Fields in Oxnard, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys begin their odyssey towards the 2026 season next week with the opening of training camp. A lot of new pieces have been added to the roster, and bad players from last year are no longer with the team. Brian Schottenheimer’s first season as head coach ended with a losing record, but there were a lot of great moments. Those moments were usually headlined by Dallas’ high-powered offense with Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens. The players added on the defensive side of the ball in Rashan Gary, Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson, P.J. Locke, and Malachi Lawrence will help execute Christian Parker’s vision. Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams have their first full offseason with the Cowboys. A lot will be riding on their success this year. Training camp is an exciting time because it’s when fans and media learn more about what the season could look like, which star players shine brightest, and which unsung heroes might rise to the top from competition. Before camp gets kicked off in just a few days, here is the current power ranking of the Top 60 Cowboys on the roster. Tier 1: All-Pro caliber players 1. Tyler Smith 2. Dak Prescott 3. Quinnen Williams 4. CeeDee Lamb 5. George Pickens 6. Brandon Aubrey All six of these players are, no doubt about it, the most highest-ceiling players who have proven it on the Cowboys team. Tyler Smith has taken the crown as the best player on the team, following the footsteps of his mentor, Zack Martin. There was a lot of back-and-forth trying to figure out whether Pickens should be above Lamb, but considering last year was a down year due to injuries, 88 got the nod above him based on his usual reliability. Tier 2: Pro Bowl-level 7. Tyler Booker 8. Javonte Williams 9. Kenny Clark 10. Rashan Gary 11. Caleb Downs 12. Jake Ferguson 13. DeMarvion Overshown 14. Malik Hooker 15. Bryan Anger 16. Jalen Thompson 17. DaRon Bland The players who have the biggest chance to jump from this list to the one above are Tyler Booker, Caleb Downs, and a healthy DeMarvion Overshown. Booker showed amazing things as a rookie, which puts him just outside tier one, but another strong year and Dallas might have the best offensive guard duo in the NFL. Bryan Anger is usually the forgotten man, but he didn’t have a single touchback in any of his punts last season . That’s pretty impressive. Given the down year across the board on defense, betting on bounce-back years from DaRon Bland and Malik Hooker put them in this category. Bland could be the biggest rise or fall candidate, depending on whether he stays healthy. Jalen Thompson was given a hefty free agent contract this offseason. He should have a big role in Parker’s defense, being his Swiss Army knife, along with Downs. Missing most of the offseason workouts so far with a pectoral injury could have lowered Thompson to the tier below, but the money says he should be one of the best secondary players in 2026. Tier 3: The Twilight Zone 18. Terence Steele 19. Cooper Beebe 20. Donovan Ezeiruaku 21. Cobie Durant 22. Ryan Flournoy 23. KaVontae Turpin 24. Dee Winters 25. Malachi Lawrence 26. P.J. Locke 27. Otito Ogbonnia 28. Trent Sieg This tier is the Twilight Zone of the power rankings. Terence Steele, Cooper Beebe, and Donovan Ezeiruaku sit at the top because they are all starters when healthy, but Dallas wants to see them take a huge step forward. Consistency is key. Malachi Lawrence and P.J. Locke earned rave reviews coming out of OTAs and minicamp, but can that momentum carry over into August? Cobie Durant, Otito Ogbonnia, and Dee Winters are veteran players that could have big roles for Dallas on defense this year. Will any of the young players beat them out? That’s what we’ll find out in camp. Long snappers are never valued until the kicking operation is mishandled. Trent Sieg has been a steady Eddy for Dallas in the snapping department, which gets him in tier three. Tier 4: Ross and Rachel (will they, won’t they) 29. Tyler Guyton 30. Shavon Revel 31. Jaishawn Barham 32. James Houston 33. Brevyn Spann-Ford 34. Reddy Steward 35. Sam Williams 36. Malik Davis 37. Jonathan Bullard 38. Markquese Bell 39. T.J. Bass 40. Nate Thomas 41. Jonathan Bullard 42. Hunter Luepke 43. Jaydon Blue 44. Joe Milton III / Sam Howell Will they or won’t they? The question often asked of the popular sitcom couple from Friends . Every player in tier four feels like 2026 is a pivotal year for them with Dallas, none more important than Tyler Guyton and Shavon Revel. Both players are walking on the same ice as Commissioner Gordon in The Dark Knight Rises . Some players, like Jonathan Bullard, Sam Williams, Reddy Steward, and T.J. Bass, are all on one-year deals. They could stick around for the entire season or be cut after camp, with the exception of Bass. Where do things stand with Brevyn Spann-Ford, Nate Thomas, Hunter Luepke, Markquese Bell, and Jaydon Blue? If things don’t work out for these young players, maybe how Dallas develops their players should start coming into question. Joe Milton and Sam Howell are the only two players who share a spot on this list, considering one of them will end up being the backup behind Prescott. Cooper Rush is no longer around to have his name penciled in this spot, or maybe he comes back for Act III? Tier 5: Depth players in the Danger Zone 45. Phil Mafah 46. Marist Liufau 47. Luke Schoonmaker 48. Caelen Carson 49. Shemar James 50. LT Overton 51. Drew Shelton 52. Curtis Robinson 53. Derion Kendrick 54. Josh Butler 55. Ajani Cornelius 56. Alijah Clark 57. Jay Toia 58. Devin Moore 59. Trevor Keegan 60. Tyrus Wheat Once the roster gets past tier four, this section becomes more about the depth of the roster and who can crack the final back part of the 53 come September. Phil Mafah is certainly a fan favorite, but will the Cowboys carry five running backs (that includes Hunter Luepke) to start the year? It might come down to who can contribute on special teams, and he could be in a training camp battle with Malik Davis. A lot of the secondary players here should be fighting for depth as well. The flashes from Josh Butler in 2024 were a pleasant surprise, but a torn ACL derailed his momentum and sidelined him for most of 2025. Can lightning strike twice for him? He could be in a battle with 2024 draft pick Caelen Carson and Derion Kendrick for the fourth and fifth cornerback spots. How does Christian Parker feel about Jay Toia and Shemar James, who were draft picks last year? They were drafted by the previous coaching staff. Does Parker view them as integral pieces in what he’s developing, or are they no longer a fit? Marist Liufau and Luke Schoonmaker might be running out of runway to show something for Dallas. Both players had high hopes as rookies, but that feels so long ago at this point. Tyrus Wheat rounds out the Top 60, considering he made the team as an undrafted free agent once upon a time and is in his second stint with the team. Maybe he can show the makings of a solid special teams player with the upside as a depth piece at defensive end. He had his best year as a pro last year with the Detroit Lions, so maybe the arrow is pointing up.

title: Here’s why the Cowboys need to win now
summary: The term “window” is silly when it comes to sports. We have all heard it said. Team X has to capitalize because the proverbial window is closing. The idea here is that their core is comprised of players who are likely not going to be playing at a high level for much longer which is […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 07: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys throws a pass during Day 12 of Dallas Cowboys Training Camp at Staybridge Suites Oxnard on August 07, 2025 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The term “window” is silly when it comes to sports. We have all heard it said. Team X has to capitalize because the proverbial window is closing. The idea here is that their core is comprised of players who are likely not going to be playing at a high level for much longer which is why the pressure is on to get it done immediately. The NFL has proven that teams can reset their “windows” (obviously it is hardly easy), and given that they are a league of parity, there is never truly a window that is shut. With all of that being said, the Cowboys do sort of have a window. ESPN’s ranking of young talent proves the window is now The folks at ESPN put together a ranking of NFL teams by under-25 talent . With all due respect to the list, the age of 25 is an arbitrary point and that should be said. If the same exercise was done for under-26 talent then things significantly change based off of just a single year. You get the point. We can still have takeaways from this type of thing, though. The idea here is that these are teams in the NFL who are on the rise as their young groups gather experience and time in the league. The New England Patriots came in at the top spot for some context. The Dallas Cowboys are nowhere near the top, though. In fact they are much closer to the bottom. Dallas ranked 24th for under-25 talent with not much to show for their name in this particular capacity. 24. Dallas Cowboys Last year’s rank: 17 Blue chips: G Tyler Booker, S Caleb Downs Notable graduated players: OT Tyler Guyton, WR George Pickens, G Tyler Smith Most of Dallas’ offensive line graduated from our list this year, but right guard Booker is still only 22 years old, as is fourth-round offensive tackle Drew Shelton. The rest of the young talent is mostly on defense. On the edge, Donovan Ezeiruaku is 22, and Malachi Lawrence is 23; but their birthdays are only two months apart (Sept. 25 for Ezeiruaku, July 21 for Lawrence). First-rounder Downs is 21. Linebacker Shemar James, who started six games last season, is 22. As you can see our point up top carries particular merit for the Cowboys. George Pickens and Tyler Smith would do some serious carrying for this team if they were able to right now, but they are not due to the exercise’s parameters. That’s just the way it goes sometimes. It is certainly great to see the team’s recent first- and second-round picks here in Tyler Booker, Donovan Ezeiruaku, Caleb Downs, and Malachi Lawrence. They are all a part of the new foundation that the team is building. Drew Shelton joining that fold would help, too. But the meat of this team is part of the elder statesmen crowd right now in Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, Quinnen Williams joining Pickens and Smith above the threshold. This is where the idea of this team having a “window” comes from. The most prevalent of those players is obviously the one who plays the most important position in Prescott. When the Cowboys are forced to find a successor is when things are going to get particularly dicey. For the most part the Cowboys have had stable quarterback play between Prescott and Tony Romo, both of whom the team fully lucked into. We have not seen the front office have to design a solution at the game’s most important position since the dawn of the internet. So the pressure is on, but the pressure is always on in the NFL It is just a little bit more loud with this team at the moment.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys must break the cycle of late-game letdowns
summary: They say that football is a game of inches, and the Dallas Cowboys discovered exactly how agonizing those inches could be during their 2023 Week 9 trip to the unfriendly confines of Lincoln Financial Field against the Philadelphia Eagles. It was a battle for supremacy in the NFC East, carrying massive divisional weight and eventual […]
full_text: They say that football is a game of inches, and the Dallas Cowboys discovered exactly how agonizing those inches could be during their 2023 Week 9 trip to the unfriendly confines of Lincoln Financial Field against the Philadelphia Eagles. It was a battle for supremacy in the NFC East, carrying massive divisional weight and eventual playoff seeding implications. When the clock struck double-zeros, Dallas fell on the short side of a 28-23 loss. This particular defeat was an especially difficult pill to swallow because of just how many close moments refused to go the team’s way. It was a fantastic back-and-forth battle, but Dallas struggled to keep pace for a stretch and found itself staring at a 28-17 deficit in the fourth quarter. Pre-snap penalties, a stagnant running game, and blown defensive assignments allowed the Eagles to take control. Then, a sudden late surge sparked a comeback. The defense abruptly came to life, forcing three consecutive three-and-outs and throwing the door wide open for the Cowboys to steal a huge divisional win on the road. What happened next in that final quarter is still a little hard to stomach. The team endured one close-call letdown after another. The heartbreak started when a replay review overturned a Luke Schoonmaker touchdown, showing the ball was just short of the goal line when his knee touched the turf. Instead of closing the gap to 28-24, Dallas walked away with zero points and still trailed by 11. Do you remember how you felt when you saw this? pic.twitter.com/B4Y6LB3PfJ — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) July 20, 2026 The team kept fighting and got the ball back quickly. Dak Prescott marched them down the field, going 5/6 for 57 yards in just over two minutes, capping the drive with a seven-yard touchdown to Jalen Tolbert. Unfortunately, they fell victim to another close call after replay again spat in their faces. A two-point conversion was overturned because Prescott had stepped out of bounds before extending the ball past the goal line, keeping it a five-point game instead of a three-point game. That was massive. How about this one? pic.twitter.com/B03GnTZjiE — Dan Rogers (@DannyPhantom24) July 20, 2026 Dallas got the ball back quickly yet again and drove 45 yards, but again they came up short at the Eagles’ 25-yard line, turning the ball over on downs with 1:17 left. The defense continued to come up huge, forcing another quick series for the Eagles’ offense. And Philly narrowly escaped disaster after running back D’Andre Swift ran into his own teammate and put the football on the turf. Micah Parsons was in perfect position to fall on it, but rookie offensive lineman Tyler Steen somehow pulled it in. The offense still got one final possession and strung together a great final drive. Well, almost. They got all the way down to the Eagles’ six-yard line with first-and-goal with 27 seconds left on the clock. The game was right there for the taking. What followed was an absolute debacle. False start. Terence Steele completely whiffs on a block, and Dak gets sacked. With no timeouts left, the clock continued to run. Incomplete pass. Delay of game. Suddenly, four shots at the six turned into one shot at the Eagles’ 27-yard line. Prescott hit CeeDee Lamb over the middle, but he was tackled well short of the goal line. That’s your ball game. You might be asking yourself why we are choosing to relive this nightmare. These are bad memories. What kind of sadomasochist subjects people to this on a perfectly fine day? The reason is to show that fans are still living with the pain of what could have been. A mid-year regular-season game from three years ago might not seem all that important on the surface, but had the Cowboys emerged victorious, it could have completely altered the 2023 season. Winning this game likely flips their record to 13-4 instead of 12-5, earning the highly coveted No. 1 seed in the NFC along with a first-round bye. That means dodging Green Bay entirely in the Wild Card round. Sure, you could argue that Dallas could have easily shown up just as unprepared in the Divisional Round against a different opponent or even that same Packers team. Then again, maybe they draw a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team where they match up a lot better? But that’s still not the important part of this article. While all those hypothetical scenarios can clutter our headspace, the real crux of the matter is that the Cowboys must find a way to stop being the team that falls short. They need to stop putting themselves into these stressful, high-chance situations in the first place. Enough with digging deep holes early in games , only to spend the remainder playing catch-up. They need to stop relying on last-minute miracles and the team that is ready to go from the outset. A better defense will always help, but we often overlook the times when the defense actually comes through, and the offense simply fails to make up the necessary ground. The team needs to get its act together and build a true culture of winning rather than being the poster child for late-game letdowns.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys O-line: Pressure from the edges, stability from the inside
summary: The Cowboys don’t have an offensive line problem. They have an edge protection problem. The data from 2025 makes that distinction surprisingly clear. While both tackle spots allowed well above-average pressure, Dallas’ three interior starters quietly performed at or above the NFL average. Today, we look at how the Cowboys linemen compared against the NFL […]
full_text: Dec 24, 2023; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) looks over the offensive line during the first half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jasen Vinlove-Imagn Images The Cowboys don’t have an offensive line problem. They have an edge protection problem. The data from 2025 makes that distinction surprisingly clear. While both tackle spots allowed well above-average pressure, Dallas’ three interior starters quietly performed at or above the NFL average. Today, we look at how the Cowboys linemen compared against the NFL average in 2025, how many splash plays (sacks + hits + hurries) they gave up, and what that could mean for 2026. The numbers we’re going to use are from Pro Football Focus (PFF), but we’re only looking at their raw stats, not the grades. Importantly, the PFF numbers can differ from the official totals because PFF only lists splash plays that are directly attributable to an offensive line player. But before we start comparing sacks, hits, and hurries among players along the offensive line, it’s important to understand that you can’t compare players without also accounting for their snap count, because one guy may have played 450 pass blocking snaps, while the other guy played 650 snaps. Example: Tyler Guyton gave up 31 total pressures (sacks + hits + hurries) according to PFF. Buffalo’s Pro Bowl left tackle Dion Dawkins gave up 33 pressures. If you’re a proponent of volume stats, you would argue that both gave up almost the same amount of pressures. Technically, you’d be right, but Guyton reached his total in just 384 pass-blocking snaps, while Dawkins played 528. Once you account for workload, the comparison looks very different. To make every player directly comparable, I’ve normalized all pressure statistics to 600 pass-blocking snaps, roughly a full season for an NFL starter. Here’s how many sacks, hits, and pressures an average NFL O-line gave up in 2025, adjusted to 600 pass-blocking snaps. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 4px 6px !important; } 2025 NFL average splash plays given up by O-line (adjusted) NFL average LT LG C RG RT Sacks 6.1 3.2 1.8 3.3 4.0 QB Hits 6.7 5.0 3.5 3.7 4.4 QB Hurries 26.8 22.3 15.6 22.6 26 Total Pressures 39.8 30.4 20.9 29.6 34.4 One interesting takeaway is that right tackles now allow almost as much pressure as left tackles. Whether that’s because elite edge rushers line up on both sides or offenses have become more balanced, the traditional blind-side gap has largely disappeared. Now that we’ve established the baseline, or ‘average’ for these splash plays, let’s have a look at how the Cowboys five starting linemen compare. Note on the color scheme: green is better than the NFL average at the position, yellow is up to 25% below the NFL average, red is more than 25% worse than the NFL average. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 4px 6px !important; } 2025 splash plays given up by Cowboys O-line (adjusted) Cowboys Starters LT Guyton LG Smith OC Beebe RG Booker RT Steele Sacks 3.1 2.2 1.4 3.1 5.4 QB Hits 9.4 0.0 4.1 6.3 8.1 QB Hurries 35.9 21.3 16.3 16.7 33.4 Total Pressures 48.4 28.0 21.7 26.1 47.0 When comparing each starter’s pass protection to the 2025 league average at his position, a clear pattern emerges: Dallas doesn’t have an offensive line problem. It has an edge protection problem. Three starters are already performing at or above league average. The interior of the offensive line has already become one of the strengths of the roster. Tyler Smith (LG) continues to perform at a high level, allowing about 8% fewer total pressures than the average NFL left guard. Cooper Beebe (C) is almost exactly league average in total pressures allowed. While his QB hit rate is slightly elevated, he developed into a dependable center in just his second season, though you’d still like to see a little more green in his profile. The biggest surprise may be rookie Tyler Booker (RG). Booker allowed fewer sacks than the average right guard, fewer QB hurries and 12% fewer total pressures than the league average. For a rookie stepping into the starting lineup, that’s an outstanding start. Collectively, Dallas’ three interior starters are performing at, or slightly above, the NFL average. In fact, the three interior positions collectively rank 11th across the NFL in total adjusted pressures and 13th in adjusted sacks. The problems in Dallas are almost entirely on the outside At left tackle, Tyler Guyton allowed 48.4 total adjusted pressures, compared to a league average of 39.8. That’s roughly 22% more pressure than the average NFL left tackle. At right tackle, Terence Steele allowed 47.0 adjusted pressures against a positional average of 34.4, nearly 37% above league average. Viewed as a unit, the offensive line appears inconsistent. Viewed by position, the interior trio is providing reliable pass protection while the tackles are giving up the majority of the pressure. That distinction matters because it changes the conversation. Instead of saying “the offensive line needs to improve,” it’s more accurate to say “the tackles need to improve.” Those are very different problems. One suggests rebuilding. The other suggests targeted development or a free-agent addition. Because the depth at tackle? title: Cowboys news: Previewing training camp for Dallas
summary: Dallas Cowboys 2026 Training Camp Preview – Todd Archer, ESPN.com Training camp 2026 is almost here. Biggest question the Cowboys are facing How quickly can Parker’s defense get up to speed? There are a lot of changes in personnel — potentially up to seven new starters — and scheme, as they move to a 3-4 […]
full_text: Dallas Cowboys 2026 Training Camp Preview – Todd Archer, ESPN.co m Training camp 2026 is almost here. Biggest question the Cowboys are facing How quickly can Parker’s defense get up to speed? There are a lot of changes in personnel — potentially up to seven new starters — and scheme, as they move to a 3-4 system. The pass rush has much to prove with the biggest addition being the trade for edge rusher Rashan Gary from the Green Bay Packers . The linebacker room is not particularly deep, and DeMarvion Overshown will have to prove he can stay healthy. The secondary has improved with additions in free agency (S Jalen Thompson , CB Cobie Durant ) and the draft (first-rounder S Caleb Downs ). The Cowboys do not have to have another Doomsday Defense to succeed in 2026, but the defense needs to be much improved over last season to make a difference. Three players to watch WR George Pickens : He is on the franchise tag at a cost of $27.3 million as the Cowboys want to see more from him in his second season before deciding whether to commit long term to the receiver. He set career highs in catches (93), yards (1,429) and touchdowns (nine) in his first season. The contract issue is resolved for at least this season, but how will Pickens respond? LB Malachi Lawrence : Downs has received most of the attention as the Cowboys’ first of two first-round picks (No. 11), but Lawrence, selected at No. 22, is as imperative to the defense’s success as Downs. He has to be a factor in the pass-rush department for the defense to succeed. LT Tyler Guyton : The left tackle is entering his third year, and he could hold the key to the offense. Injuries have slowed his progress, but he was better in 2025 before a high ankle injury ended his season. He has to stay healthy and perform at a high level. If he can, then the Cowboys can keep their front five in the spots they want them in, which means Tyler Smith stays at left guard. The Oxnard Iliad: Cowboys’ 0 to 99 training camp guide – Dan Rogers, Blogging the Boys Get the rundown on the Cowboys training camp roster. As the cool Pacific breeze rolls off Mandalay Beach into Oxnard, the countdown to Dallas Cowboys training camp signals the arrival of a new battle. Much like the grueling siege on the beaches of Troy, the upcoming weeks will transform the practice fields into a theater of war where hungry longshots and seasoned veterans clash in fierce, unforgiving roster battles. Every depth-chart skirmish is driven by tactical deception, where coaching staffs look to unveil their own Trojan Horse surprises, whether through a hidden-gem player or an unexpected battlefield wrinkle drawn up from their new young general. With 90 soldiers descending on the practice fields, keeping track of every fresh face can be a little difficult. That is why we have broken down the entire roster by the numbers, literally, to provide you with an ultimate cheat sheet for every single player running around this summer. From elite cornerstone pillars to the fiery undrafted rookies clawing for a spot on the practice squad, here is one thing you should know about every Cowboys’ player as the pads go on and the battles begin. Cowboys Executive Will McClay Addresses George Pickens’ Future in Dallas – Randy Gurzi, SI.com Will McClay speaks on George Pickens future. While appearing on Crown Global Media’s Doin’ Alright podcast, McClay said he’s not concerned with outside perceptions . He even said he doesn’t want anyone to tell him how to handle his checkbook, just like he wouldn’t tell anyone what to do with theirs. ”Public perception is, oh, you should sign this guy and do that. But, you know, I don’t tell you how to run your checkbook, you don’t tell me how to run mine. And it’s, you know, our businesses. And so I really, everybody’s philosophy is a little bit different. And we love George Pickens,” McClay said. “Finding a way to fill the team with 53 of the best players in today’s day and age is very, very difficult. So you go through the different contracts and the different aspects and all those different ways and you put it together. And that situation with George presented itself in a way that we could do it that way and still keep our team together. That’s the best way for me to put it.” Could McClay’s comments mean George Pickens will stay in Dallas long-term? Dallas Cowboys insider disagreed with some of my 38 roster locks, and he makes some fair points – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports Who could be some surprise cuts this offseason? LT Nate Thomas I see why Fisher isn’t treating Thomas as a lock. The likes of fourth-round rookie Drew Shelton and even Ajani Cornelius could change the math quickly in camp. But with Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer announcing to the world former first-round rookie Tyler Guyton is competing with Thomas for the starting role, that to me means Thomas is on another tier compared to other linemen. If he’s competing to start, he has to be a lock, right? To Fisher’s point, I do believe the so-called open competition at offensive tackle is more of a motivation tactic to light a fire for Guyton than anything else. Role Call: Otito Ogbonnia tasked with replacing impact DT in 2026 – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Otito Ogbonnia will likely play a big role in 2026. How He Got Here: This should all feel very familiar for Ogbonnia, being in Texas, I mean. That’s because he hails from Katy, TX, an afternoon drive south of NTX in the Houston area. His talent in high school took him to UCLA, meaning there’s an added familiarity in that it’s also the school attended by fellow defensive linemen Kenny Clark and Jay Toia. Ogbonnia, a former fifth-round pick of the Los Angeles Chargers in 2022, was signed this offseason as a free agent to help add depth following the decision to trade another former Bruin, Osa Odighizuwa, to the San Francisco 49ers. What’s Next: Ogbonnia will walk into training camp with the express mission of proving he can be a worthy backup to Clark and All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams. That will, of course, pit him against Toia, but also Jonathan Bullard and others. Working in his favor is the fact he’s got 21 NFL starts in 40 active games under his belt, with 82 combined tackles through his first four seasons in the league. He’ll need to combine his youth with his experience to make waves in Oxnard and beyond for Christian Parker. Daily discussion question: What will we be talking about this time next week?

That is the price of hype and high expectations. I am here for it. The players […]

Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images | Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Denver Broncos training camp it now finally upon us. Later next week, they will report and training camp will be open to the fans who already vacuumed up the ‘free’ tickets to these public events. There are none left. That is the price of hype and high expectations. I am here for it. The players are too. One of the best on the defense side of the ball, Nik Bonitto, was asked a few questions while at a charity event on Thursday. He was a myriad of questions covered on the teams’ main website , but it was two comments that really stood out to me. First, he talked about how he can improve his skillset next season. He understands there is always ways even the league’s most elite players can get better. He clearly has the drive and desire to be the best and for a defense that has league the NFL in sacks in back-to-back seasons, that is great to see. “All facets,” said Bonitto of where he hopes to improve. “I still have a lot of room to grow in my game — in the run and in the pass. Just keep trying to fine-tune these things, keep looking at other guys around the league that are doing it at a high level and seeing how I can put it into my game to continue to be the best player I know I can be.” He then segued into how the team is feel about the upcoming season and the hunger is there. They finished one game from the Super Bowl without their franchise quarterback in that final defeat, so the expectations have to be through the roof in that locker room heading into this season. “I’m really excited,” Bonitto said. “Especially how the season ended, I know everybody’s champing at the bit to get the pads back on and compete against each other these next couple months. It’s going to be real fun for sure.” That is a big deal to be honest. A team can only go as far as the players in that building and if they are driven by an intense desire for greatness combined with superior talent, then the sky is truly the limit for these guys. I can’t wait for this season to begin. How about you? Horse Tracks

title: Jonathon Cooper’s arraignment set for August 31
summary: The Denver Broncos are just days away from having their veterans report on July 28 for this year’s training camp festivities. A lot of questions and headlines are out there leading up to camp, but perhaps none other is bigger than the legal situation with outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper. After sitting out all of minicamp […]
full_text: Nov 30, 2025; Landover, Maryland, USA; Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper (0) runs off the field after the game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | Geoff Burke-Imagn Images The Denver Broncos are just days away from having their veterans report on July 28 for this year’s training camp festivities. A lot of questions and headlines are out there leading up to camp, but perhaps none other is bigger than the legal situation with outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper. After sitting out all of minicamp last month, Cooper recently completed a handful of measures that focused on his mental health and over all well-being. Today, according to 9News Broncos insider Mike Klis, Cooper had a virtual hearing relating to his two arrests and subsequent charges in June. Those include second and third-degree assault, violation of a protection order, criminal mischief, and harassment. The arraignment for those charges has now been scheduled for August 31. That date is well after training camp and two weeks before the regular season kickoff against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football. Arraignment means Jonathon Cooper is to enter a plea or guilty or not guilty. That step is Aug. 31. That means legal system could potentially play out for months to come. https://t.co/qZ9AAwxY4s — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) July 24, 2026 Keep in mind, the lengthy legal process doesn’t have to play out for the NFL to suspend players in any incidents related to domestic violence. Per the league’s Personal Conduct Policy, first time offenses in this area carry a minimum suspension of six games without pay. Prior decisions [suspensions] on matters like this have often been rendered by the league by the middle of August. As of now, it’s unknown whether or not Cooper will be present for training camp. Moreover, what his potential availability may be for the start of the season given his legal issues. In the event Cooper is suspended, the Broncos will turn to Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman to help offset his loss. Cooper, a late seventh-round draft selection by the Broncos in the 2021 NFL Draft, has went from a reserve player his first two seasons in the NFL to a key starter for the Broncos’ defense. In each of the last three seasons, Cooper has started every game and has posted 27 sacks and 180 tackles.

title: Denver Broncos 2026 Training Camp: 7 positional battles to watch
summary: One of the more interesting aspects of training camp each year is the positional battles ongoing throughout camp and into the preseason. We have seen multiple quarterback competitions happen during Broncos camp, but thankfully, Bo Nix has that job locked down for the foreseeable future. However, the Broncos will have multiple camp battles happening this […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 17: Marvin Mims Jr. #19 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Buffalo Bills at Empower Field At Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the more interesting aspects of training camp each year is the positional battles ongoing throughout camp and into the preseason. We have seen multiple quarterback competitions happen during Broncos camp, but thankfully, Bo Nix has that job locked down for the foreseeable future. However, the Broncos will have multiple camp battles happening this summer that could greatly impact how this team looks come Week 1. While the Broncos starters are mostly locked and loaded for Week 1, there still will be plenty of competition for roles and even roster spots happening during camp. So, with all that said, here are the Denver Broncos positional battles I will be paying attention to during Broncos Camp. Backup Quarterback Veteran Jarrett Stidham has been Sean Payton’s backup since he was acquired and hired by the Broncos, but could his role be up for grabs this summer? Sam Ehlinger joined the team as the QB3 last season and quickly impressed the Broncos coaches on and off the field. Ehlinger re-signed with the team this offseason and, according to reports from OTA and minicamp, looked pretty good and may have even outplayed Stidham. Denver Broncos roster review: QB Sam Ehlinger https://t.co/OPvYowMoQv — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) July 18, 2026 Do I think Ehlinger can really take the QB2 role from Stidham? I have my doubts. Payton has spoken fondly of Stiddy in the past; he was Payton’s first free agent signing with the Broncos, and he knows the system well. With that said, his performance in the AFC Championship Game was, well, not great. In fairness to Stidham, the circumstances were not great for him, but you still hoped he would have played a little better than that. However, if Ehlinger outplays Stidham throughout camp, we could have a real conversation here. I will need to see it happen consistently for me to really believe this could happen, but we’ll have to wait and see. It certainly is possible. Running Back – The battle for carries The Broncos are expected to enter Week 1 with veteran JK Dobbins, second-year back RJ Harvey, and rookie Jonah Coleman as their three running backs on the roster. All three backs are expected to have a role on this offense this season, but the exact details remain up in the air. Veteran JK Dobbins re-signed with the team after a successful 2025 season that was unfortunately cut short by injuries. Unfortunately, that has been the story of Dobbins’ career, and the Broncos have to be wary of his injury history. To his credit, he has bounced back and performed well despite multiple serious lower-body injuries, but the concern remains. He will be the Broncos’ starting running back this season, but could we see him share carries with a pair of young Broncos ball carriers? RJ Harvey had a mixed bag when it came to his rookie year. On a positive note, he had 12 total touchdowns last season, which is pretty damn good for a rookie running back. However, once Dobbins went down with an injury, Harvey struggled as the Broncos’ main ball carrier. Harvey averaged just 3.7 yards per carry but did look better as a receiver and in space, which was the role the team envisioned for him when he was drafted. I would anticipate he would have a similar role this season, but could he lose snaps to rookie Jonah Coleman? Broncos RB Jonah Coleman pic.twitter.com/hM87I7VuGb — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) April 25, 2026 The real X-Factor here is rookie Jonah Coleman. The talented rookie back has three-down traits and could push for significant playing time his rookie year. He is a powerful and patient runner who can run between the tackles, catch passes out of the backfield, and probably most importantly, come in on third downs and be a pass blocker. If he were to have a strong camp and preseason, he could push for significant snaps early on this season. Sean Payton in the past has said it is difficult to manage a three-headed backfield, so it will be interesting to see how this plays out. All three backs will be on the team, but it will be interesting to see the pecking order come Week 1. WR3 battle Probably the most interesting positional battle to happen this summer during Broncos Camp will be the WR3 battle between Marvin Mims, Troy Franklin, and Pat Bryant. As we know, the team made a blockbuster trade for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle during the offseason, and that addition shook up the Broncos’ wide receiver room. With Waddle and veteran Courtland Sutton being your WR1 and WR2 in the offense, that battle for the WR3 job is expected to be a competitive one. Marvin Mims Jr. has shown up in the biggest moments throughout his career and has routinely made big plays down the field. On top of that, he is also an All-Pro returner who can take one all the way back for a touchdown whenever he touches the ball. However, he has never fully lived up to his potential as a wide receiver. Now in a contract year, could that all change? This time last year, all the hype was about Troy Franklin. He added weight and was making plays throughout OTAs and minicamp and carried that into training camp, preseason, and into the regular season. He finished the 2025 season with 65 receptions for 709 yards and 6 touchdowns, which is pretty decent considering how his rookie year went. However, with Waddle now on the team, Franklin seems like the player most negatively impacted by this addition. He will once again need to have a strong summer if he wants to solidify himself in this Denver Broncos wide receiver room. Pat Bryant had himself a solid rookie season. His role in the offense was growing as the season progressed, and it appeared he surpassed Troy Franklin late in the season. However, the injury bug bit him late in the year and derailed what could have been a strong end to his rookie year. Now, in year two, Bryant is hoping to put the concussions behind him and take that big second-year jump and become a mainstay in the Broncos offense. Bryant is a big and physical target who can work the middle of the field, contribute as a blocker, and was arguably the Broncos’ most reliable wide receiver when it came to catching the ball. He is my personal favorite in this competition, but all three can and should make strong cases for the Broncos’ WR3 job. The bigger picture here is: how will the team utilize all three of these receivers? Will there be a potential trade? Will they rely on the depth and use all three in a rotation? It could go a number of ways right now and I am excited to see how it plays out throughout camp. Is there a LG competition? I’ll say this from the start. This is pure speculation on my part, but I believe there will be a three-way battle for the Broncos starting left guard position. Veteran Ben Powers is in the final year of his contract, and despite briefly being rumored to be a pay cut or trade/cut candidate, he is back with the team and expected to be their starting left guard. However, the team does have competition on the roster that could change things down the road. First, the team signed versatile reserve lineman Alex Palczewski to a two-year extension this offseason. He started at left guard last season while Powers was sidelined with an injury and performed well. He provides the team with a talented, younger, and cheaper option and someone they know they can plug and play at the position. Some Kage Casey highlights pic.twitter.com/Ec7daUOJ4c — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) April 25, 2026 The team also drafted Boise State offensive lineman Kage Casey in the 4th round of the 2026 NFL Draft. He played left tackle throughout his college career but is expected to focus on the left guard position his rookie year. Left guard is coincidentally the position Ben…

title: Ranking the Denver Broncos’ defensive position groups prior to training camp
summary: Over the past two seasons, the Denver Broncos have sported one of the best defenses in the National Football League. Under the leadership of Vance Joseph, the team has embarked on a significant turnaround since his first year back leading the defense in 2023. They’ve led the NFL and posted franchise record breaking sack numbers […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - DECEMBER 21: Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph of the Denver Broncos stands on the field before a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High on December 21, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Over the past two seasons, the Denver Broncos have sported one of the best defenses in the National Football League. Under the leadership of Vance Joseph, the team has embarked on a significant turnaround since his first year back leading the defense in 2023. They’ve led the NFL and posted franchise record breaking sack numbers in back-to-back years. In order to achieve their goal of earning a fourth Lombardi Trophy, the defense is going to have to perform impeccably again this season. Leading up to training camp, here is my ranking of the Broncos’ defensive position groups. Feel free to offer your rankings and reasoning in the comments section. #1: The Cornerbacks The Broncos boast the best slate of corners in the NFL. I don’t believe that’s debatable. In fact, I bet every team wishes they had a starting trio of cornerbacks like Denver possesses. Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja’Quan McMillian are head and shoulders above the competition. That formidable trio is set to lead the way at the position once again in 2026. After them, Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron are good players who would easily start for most any other franchise. They do a fantastic job at limiting big plays down the field. Denver’s cornerback prowess was a big reason why they ranked second in the NFL in completion percentage and yards per attempt. They tied for fifth in touchdowns allowed and ranked seventh-best in yards per game. While there were several pick-sixes by the group in ‘25, Denver’s defense only had 10 interceptions for the entire season. That’s something I’m optimistic will change for their upcoming ‘26 gridiron campaign. In fact, I believe they have ability to be one of the best in the league this season if they live up to their potential. #2: The Edge Rushers Denver’s group of edge rushers are definitely a big strength. They are a huge reason why the defense was able to put up eye-popping sack totals in ‘24 and ‘25. However, I have them just a smidge behind the cornerbacks in the overall positional group rankings. There is no doubt fifth-year pro Nik Bonitto is the top player within the unit. After posting 27.5 sacks the past two seasons, Bonitto has earned two Pro-Bowl nods and is well on his way to an All-Pro honor in the future. His get-off at the line of scrimmage is amongst the league’s best. Moreover, his astounding 20-percent pressure rate is something Defensive Coordinator’s dream of with their edge rushers. While I’m high the trio of Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman, the potential absence of Jonathon Cooper—at least for a portion of the season due to off the field issues—could become an issue. Cooper has been an underrated performer for the team. While his sack numbers waned down the stretch, his pressure rate of nearly 14-percent is Top 20 at the position. Can Denver’s group of edge rushers pave the way for them to lead the league in sacks for a third straight season? I think so, but I wonder more if they have what it takes to get more sacks than they did last season. If so, that would be quite the accomplishment. #3: The Defensive Line The departure of John Franklin-Myers to the Tennessee Titans is the main reason I have Denver’s defensive line group ranked third. Even with Franklin-Myers gone, they still have one top-tier performer at the position. Zach Allen is one of the team’s best players and one of the most underrated defensive trench players in the NFL. He’ll lead the way for the group upfront and is poised to have another dominant season. Outside of Allen, I do like the depth they have. Nose tackle D.J. Jones has been a solid and reliable defender for the team since signing with them several seasons ago. Malcolm Roach was a good addition in last year’s free agent cycle. Fourth-year pro Eyioma Uwazurike could be a breakout candidate for the team this year and will be first in line to help offset the loss of Franklin-Myers. The big question is how well and how much Sai’vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim will play this year. The franchise’s third round picks the past two drafts, both have tantalizing traits and pass rushing skills. But will they be able to flash enough in camp to show they are worthy of significant snaps this year? I can’t wait to find out. #4: Safety I don’t consider the safety position to be a liability. It’s just that the three aforementioned positions have superior production, impact, and talent levels. Nevertheless, both Brandon Jones and Talanoa Hufanga are quality starters and are certainly an underrated backend duo. My big question is the depth behind them. In the event either Jones or Hufanga were to miss time, the Broncos would be banking on players with mostly special team’s experience to take over and start. However, potentially sliding Jahdae Barron back there could also be a part of the equation. Devon Key is an All-Pro player on special teams. Boasting top-tier physical traits, JL Skinner has been a mainstay on special teams the past few years, but very little experience in games defensively. Tycen Anderson, the free agent signing from the Cincinnati Bengals, has virtually the same story as Skinner. Miles Scott was a ballhawk at Illinois, though is still a virtual unknown as a late-round rookie selection. #5: Inside Linebacker Your mileage may vary, but the position group on defense that concerns me the most is inside linebacker. It’s a shame the Dre Greenlaw experiment didn’t pan out. I was cautiously optimistic about the signing, but in the end, his inability to stay healthy was the primary culprit in his early exit from the Mile High City. Given such, Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad will be the Broncos’ starting tandem on the inside. This was one area I thought they may have been aggressive in free agency upgrading. Yet continuity and knowledge of the defensive system meant a lot to the coaching staff and front office. Outside of Singleton and Strnad, Denver’s group of inside linebackers doesn’t have a lot of NFL experience—especially when it comes to starting. Five players, most all of them UDFAs from the past several years, will be vying for several backup spots on the roster. Jordan Turner, Levelle Bailey, Karene Reid, Red Murdock, and Taurean York will be in a fierce competition. That just might be the most heated position battle in all of training camp. These players won’t just be looking to prove themselves on special teams, they will be given the opportunity to show they have what it takes to start if called upon.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Denver Broncos roster review: Cornerback Patrick Surtain II
summary: Patrick Surtain II started his rookie season with the Denver Broncos as ready as any NFL player has been to step on the field and be an impact player. He racked up 4 INTs his first season, earned his first All-Pro nod his second season, and earned the AP Defensive Player of the Year in […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - DECEMBER 14: Pat Surtain II #2 of the Denver Broncos catches an interception against Christian Watson #9 of the Green Bay Packers during the third quarter at Empower Field At Mile High on December 14, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Patrick Surtain II started his rookie season with the Denver Broncos as ready as any NFL player has been to step on the field and be an impact player. He racked up 4 INTs his first season, earned his first All-Pro nod his second season, and earned the AP Defensive Player of the Year in 2024. Surtain is an elite shutdown cornerback who is arguably the best in the NFL over the past couple of years. He commonly draws the best receiver the opponents have and never blinks. Many would say Surtain had a down year last season if they look at the stat sheet, but I don’t think that was the case at all. Most quarterbacks ignore his matchup on game days, which leaves him with fewer chances to rack up the stats in the first place. Surtain is a relentless competitor with true dedication to the game and a deep desire to be truly great. He will continue that pursuit in 2026, hungry to help this Broncos team climb to higher ground. Player Profile Pat Surtain II | Cornerback | Denver Broncos Height: 6’2″ Weight: 202 pounds Age: 26 years old Experience: 6th season College: Alabama 2025 stats: 47 tackles, 12 passes defended, 1 INT, 1 TFL 2026 Broncos outlook Surtain is a player in his absolute prime. He signed an extension in 2024 with a revision last year with the goal of avoiding any potential holdout situations. Surtain is a key reason that this defense is as elite as it is. His ability to shut down the best receiver on the other team allows the defense to gain more time for their deadly pass rush to get home. This also allows Vance Joseph to roll coverage to help out other areas of the field that face challenging matchups. I expect nothing short of amazing from Surtain. He’s bounced back from his partially torn pectoral muscle after missing 3 games last season and was able to finish the season strong. Final Word The Denver Broncos defense with Patrick Surtain II in the defensive backfield is an absolute juggernaut. He’s one of the (if not the ) best corners in the league. I expect Surtain to be elite again this year, continuing his Pro Bowl streak and hopefully reclaiming a spot on the 2026 All-Pro team.

title: A monster season was just the beginning for Nik Bonitto
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Nik Bonitto is coming off a career season. The Denver Broncos edge totaled 14 sacks, finished fourth in the NFL Defensive Player of the Year voting, and went to his second Pro Bowl. It’s Bonitto’s second straight season of double-digit sacks. In the win over the Buffalo Bills in the AFC […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 25: Nik Bonitto #15 of the Denver Broncos lines up before the snap during the AFC Championship NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Nik Bonitto is coming off a career season. The Denver Broncos edge totaled 14 sacks, finished fourth in the NFL Defensive Player of the Year voting, and went to his second Pro Bowl. It’s Bonitto’s second straight season of double-digit sacks. In the win over the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Playoffs, he was a game-wrecker, tallying two forced fumbles, including a strip sack of Josh Allen. Bonitto is now in the discussion as one of the top pass rushers in the NFL. Now, he wants to get even better. As Bonitto said to the Broncos website on Thursday: “All facets. I still have a lot of room to grow in my game — in the run and in the pass. Just keep trying to fine-tune these things, keep looking at other guys around the league that are doing it at a high level and seeing how I can put it into my game to continue to be the best player I know I can be.” What gives Bonitto the confidence is the success he had in the win over the Bills. How could it not? He was a huge reason Denver recorded one of the best wins in franchise history. “It’s obviously great when you can do it in the regular season,” Bonitto said Thursday to the Broncos website. But doing it in the postseason in those big type of moments, it gives you that confidence to know you’re supposed to be there and you can make those types of plays on big stages.” "I still have a lot of room to grow in my game. Just keep trying to fine-tune these things." OLB Nik Bonitto eyes improvement in 'all facets' in Year 5 » https://t.co/6vN2y2cm08 pic.twitter.com/kz4hlxPAx8 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) July 23, 2026 As Bonitto and Denver look to take the next step after finishing one game away from the Super Bowl, Bonitto will play a key role in making that come to life. He’s one of the leaders on defense and has put himself in the discussion as one of the best edge rushers in the NFL. If Bonitto is able to take his game to another level this season, that makes the Broncos defense better and the team. His mindset will force his teammates to match his commitment and desire. It’s exactly what a team needs looking to build off a season like Denver just had. “I’m really excited,” Bonitto said to the team website. “Especially how the season ended, I know everybody’s champing at the bit to get the pads back on and compete against each other these next couple months. It’s going to be real fun for sure.”

Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | David Reginek-Imagn Images Over at our mothership, Jarrett Bailey made 61 predictions for the 2026 NFL season . Four of those 61 predictions involve the Lions, and each of them come with varying degrees of likelihood, in my opinion. To kick off Notes today, I’ll go through each of Bailey’s Lions-related predictions. 10. Lions score 40 points in consecutive weeks Bailey doesn’t just make this prediction, he picks the two games Detroit will do it against. They then have a two-game road-trip, facing the Carolina Panthers and Arizona Cardinals. In front of a national audience on Sunday Night Football , Jahmyr Gibbs goes off for three total touchdowns while Jared Goff goes for 303 yards and four scores, defeating the Panthers 41-17. The next week against Arizona, Goff and rising playmaker Isaac TeSlaa hook up for seven receptions, 88 yards, and two scores while the defense forces three takeaways in a 40-9 public execution. The Panthers had a pretty average defense last year, and just lost their starting linebacker for the season . The Cardinals had one of the worst defenses in football and just hit the reset button. I could see this happening. 14. Bills open new Highmark Stadium with a bang Detroit plays the Bills in Week 2 on “Thursday Night Football,” and it will be the christening of Buffalo’s new stadium. Bailey predicts the Lions to lose 38-24. Obviously, that’s a tough matchup for Detroit, and they’re currently underdogs to the Bills, but that feels like a pretty big score difference. 18. Cardinals trade S Budda Baker to the Lions Okay, now we’re getting juicy. Obviously, the Lions’ safety situation is in flux as they await to see how quickly Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph can return from injury. With the Cardinals likely heading for a rebuild year, it totally makes sense for them to be a seller, and Baker is still a great player. Unfortunately, he comes with a $14.4 million salary in 2026 and over $16 million in 2027. Additionally, Branch’s return should come right around the trade deadline, so this one feels pretty unlikely. 44. Lions win the NFC North Bailey admits he’s skeptical about Detroit’s roster on defense, but he’s very high on the hiring of Drew Petzing as the team’s new offensive coordinator. “I’ll be optimistic about the Lions and have them rebound and win the division with a high-powered offense that outscores its problems,” Bailey writes. With the Lions currently being favorites to win the division, this is a perfectly reasonable prediction. Check out all of Bailey’s 61 predictions here.
