title: Rams should sign Joey Bosa, if not Aaron Donald
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have effectively gone all-in this offseason with their defensive additions, with a possible Aaron Donald reunion in tow. Should anything fail to pan out on the Donald front or the Rams wisely opt not to go that route, then they should continue their all-in push by signing Joey Bosa. After nine […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 17: Joey Bosa #97 of the Buffalo Bills defends /ad during the first half of an AFC Divisional Playoff game at Empower Field At Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have effectively gone all-in this offseason with their defensive additions, with a possible Aaron Donald reunion in tow. Should anything fail to pan out on the Donald front or the Rams wisely opt not to go that route, then they should continue their all-in push by signing Joey Bosa. After nine seasons with the Chargers to begin his career, Bosa signed a one-year deal with the Bills in March 2025. With the Chargers, he made three playoff appearances, yet immediately made a trip with Super Bowl-contending Buffalo in his lone season there, falling just short of an AFC Championship berth. In 15 games, he finished with a modest 29 combined tackles, five sacks, nine tackles-for-loss and led the league with five forced fumbles. Those were his most forced fumbles since he had a career-high seven in 2021. Even if he isn’t a pass rushing machine as he was early in his career, Bosa can still make quarterbacks uncomfortable in the pocket, as evidenced by this strip-sack of Aaron Rodgers in a Week 13 win over the Steelers. View this post on Instagram Again, while Bosa doesn’t stuff the stat sheet as he did coming out of Ohio State, he would be a less risky option for the Rams compared to Donald. Let’s simply state the obvious here, as I want to make it clear that I’m no AD hater. Donald has been out of football since the conclusion of the 2023 campaign. That is something fans should be well aware of. Even though he continues to stay in game shape, he hasn’t played in an NFL game for TWO SEASONS. With absolutely no disrespect to a legend, all the rumors and the front office considering bringing him back are ridiculous, because a player like Bosa would be as effective at this stage. We already know about Bosa’s ability to force turnovers, but he also led Buffalo with 16 QB hits . Additionally, he also had eight QB hurries and 11 knockdowns — which is where the quarterback hits the ground after throwing — his most in three seasons. Missed tackles have been a problem throughout his career; according to Pro Football Reference , he averages seven per season, for a total of 41. He had six missed tackles with the Bills, for a missed tackle percentage of 17.1. While that does seem high, Bosa has had a double-digit missed tackle percentage in all but two career seasons and has made four Pro Bowls in that span. He’s always been a disruptive pass rusher. Even if he doesn’t always hit home, his presence is felt constantly, so opposing offenses must always know where he is. Joey Bosa tips the pass and it's picked! BUFvsCLE on CBS/Paramount+ https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/Rj0srczUD2 — NFL (@NFL) December 21, 2025 Los Angeles would be able to sign Bosa for cheap, since Buffalo signed him to a one-year, $12.6 million deal last offseason. He will also be entering his age-31 season, which might make him a no-brainer consideration for the Rams aiming for a championship run if Donald wasn’t lurking in the shadows. Look, Bosa isn’t going to have the same appeal to Rams fans or draw the headlines as a potential AD reunion would. However, Bosa shouldn’t be discounted in any way, as he remains a strong and effective pass rusher as he pushes into his 30s. If the whole Donald storyline doesn’t end up working for Los Angeles, then the Rams must consider signing Bosa to maintain their Super Bowl trajectory in 2026.

title: Ranking the Rams uniform closet
summary: The Los Angeles Rams first made sweeping uniform changes in 2020, opting to use a new color palette of royal and sol to fit the Los Angeles culture. The color scheme was widely accepted but parts of the Rams uniforms still left fans “hoping for more”. In 2021, the Rams added their first alternate, modernizing […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams first made sweeping uniform changes in 2020, opting to use a new color palette of royal and sol to fit the Los Angeles culture. The color scheme was widely accepted but parts of the Rams uniforms still left fans “hoping for more”. In 2021, the Rams added their first alternate, modernizing the 1990s white throwback. That jersey would become the jersey the Rams won Super Bowl LVI in against the Cincinnati Bengals at SoFi Stadium. Last year, the Rams introduced their rivalries “Midnight Mode” jersey. Earlier this offseason, the Rams adjusted their modern white and royal blue uniforms; ditching certain features like the gradient look and chest tag. The team also added a horn on the sleeve and a white pants set. And finally last night, the Rams completed their look with two more alternate uniforms – an all white and blue, known as “Fearsome White” to honor the 1960s Fearsome Foursome. The other alternate added was “Classic Sol”, a modern throwback to the 1950s championship team. Now threaded with 5 uniform sets for the 2026 season, fans will get to see their team in a variety of different looks. But my question to fans is this: which Rams set is the best uniform? The Los Angeles Rams have just dropped their two new uniforms. Classic Sol and Fearsome White. What’s your rank of the entire wardrobe, 1 – 5? pic.twitter.com/1xJD55uwKY — RAMS REPORT🗯 (@RamsNFLReport) July 24, 2026 My Rankings 1. Modern White The Rams main road uniform is as clean as they come. The team nailed its initial look and the adjustments this offseason continue to make it the most appealing uniform compared to the rest. It’s hard not to look at those uniforms and not see or relive Matthew Stafford’s no look pass to Cooper Kupp in Super Bowl LVI. Or Aaron Donald’s celebration after his game sealing play on 4th down. 2. Fearsome White Fans had been begging for the Rams to bring this look into the fold. And its reception is nothing short of excellent. We’ll only get to see the uniform once in Week 13 against the Green Bay Packers but I would not be surprised if that changes in 2027. 3. Royal Blue The Rams main home uniform. I might have had this uniform lower if the team had not removed the gradient look for the jersey numbers and pants. But with the solid color for the numbers, this uniform is now a strong look as home uniforms go. 4. Rivalries “Midnight Mode” This uniform grew on me when the Rams debuted them against the Seattle Seahawks. The jury is still out on them with the midnight navy and the royal blue trying to coincide on the shoulders/sleeve. 5. Classic Sol It’s hard to pull off a yellow alternate. The Rams kept it simple by designing the uniform to be a modern version of the 1950s team uniform. I’m still undecided on its look but the others are definitely better.
author: Steven Ridings

title: L.A. Rams News: Tyreek Hill is damaged goods
summary: There’s been some talk about the Los Angeles Rams adding another veteran wide receiver like Stefon Diggs to the roster, but Tyreek Hill was someone the Rams possibly maybe could have considered, but that seems highly unlikely with Hill revealing he seems to have a long way to go before he suits up again. If […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 11: Tyreek Hill #10 of the Miami Dolphins runs the ball against Kamren Kinchens #26 of the Los Angeles Rams during the second quarter in the game at SoFi Stadium on November 11, 2024 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s been some talk about the Los Angeles Rams adding another veteran wide receiver like Stefon Diggs to the roster, but Tyreek Hill was someone the Rams possibly maybe could have considered, but that seems highly unlikely with Hill revealing he seems to have a long way to go before he suits up again. If he suits up again. Hill was one of the best receivers in the NFL for a time, but that time seems long gone after a few seemingly wasted seasons with the Miami Dolphins, and some serious injuries. To be fair, Hill was still crushing it in Miami until he wasn’t. Now, even if he were to come back to the NFL, it’s unclear how effective he would be. So, the Rams have options when it comes to adding another receiver and or seeing if someone on their roster can fill whatever void the fans (and potentially the Rams) think they have. Hill was a bit of a controversial player, he had some negative press regarding him and his time in the NFL, he was also a true talent, so teams wanted him. He may still be talented, but his body may be slowing down, and at this point, it remains to be seen if any team will want to take a shot on him, or if he’ll be able to take the field. Either way, the season is coming whether Hill is ready or not. Thank you for checking out Turf Show Times and I have great news! It’s Friday. We made it. Comment on whatever you want, and thank you (again) for checking out Turf Show Times! Tyreek Hill posts workout video, says still ‘no power’ in leg (espn) “Hill posted a YouTube video Wednesday night that showed him working out as he discussed the dislocated knee and multiple ligament tears he suffered in Week 4 last season against the New York Jets . “So it’s about 10 months after doing two surgeries,” Hill said. “My left leg is the one that I injured. I have no power in my left leg, so I’m trying to regain all the power back in my left leg. But it’s one day at a time.” Rams CEO’s statement leaves door open for Aaron Donald’s NFL return (clutchpoints) “Demoff called Donald one of the most accomplished players in franchise and NFL history, crediting him as a major reason the Rams won Super Bowl 56. “I think we all follow along like you,” Demoff said. “When Aaron Donald raises his hand and said he’s considering coming back … we’re fans as well. He’s one of the most decorated players in NFL history, in franchise history. We don’t have a ring or a Lombardi Trophy or banner if it’s not for Aaron Donald.” Los Angeles Rams unveil two new alternate uniforms for 2026 (espn.com) “The Classic Sol uniform, a tribute to the team’s 1951 NFL Championship and that title’s 75th anniversary, features a yellow-on-white jersey and pants combination. The most prominent detail comes in the form of a trio of stripes on the sleeve, with the jersey also containing a Sol monogram neck tag. The Fearsome White threads sport an icy white color scheme and honor the club’s iconic Fearsome Foursome defensive line of the 1960s and early 1970s. The alternates contain subtle but distinct details of their own — the most prominent being a ram horn-themed shoulder stripe on the jersey that matches the team’s classic helmet. The look also comes with an accompanying helmet that adds a new lid to Los Angeles’ collection, a callback to the team’s 1960s appearance in the form of a white ram horn on a blue background.“ Rams Feed:

title: Reactions to Rams alternate jerseys
summary: The Los Angeles Rams finally unveiled their two long-awaited alternate uniforms, and the response across the NFL has been overwhelmingly positive. While every uniform release generates debate, the Rams appear to have accomplished something many franchises strive for: blending modern design with the organization’s rich history. The two new alternates — the “Fearsome White” and […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams finally unveiled their two long-awaited alternate uniforms, and the response across the NFL has been overwhelmingly positive. While every uniform release generates debate, the Rams appear to have accomplished something many franchises strive for: blending modern design with the organization’s rich history. The two new alternates — the “Fearsome White” and “Classic Sol” uniforms — immediately sparked conversation among fans, media members, and designers throughout the football world. The all-white “Fearsome White” look pays tribute to the legendary Fearsome Foursome era of the 1960s, while the bright yellow “Classic Sol” uniform embraces the franchise’s earliest Los Angeles roots. The Classic Sol uniforms have all kinds of cool touches. The numerals & shoulder stripes are era-accurate & made of actual satin, which isn’t usual now. The wordmark on the helmet is taken straight from the font of the title banner given by the Rams to Tim Bergin’s bar in 1951. pic.twitter.com/IQqAl0UPJU — Greg Beacham (@gregbeacham) July 24, 2026 I’m drenched, tired, and coming off an unparalleled high of hearing Jukebox Hero & Free Bird live… BUT WE GOT RAMS UNIFORMS TO REVIEW, BABY! At first glance, I’m a fan of the Los Angeles Rams’ 2 new throwback alternate uniforms. I’ll have more thoughts later, lmk yours 👇 https://t.co/VbrmKKSCTC pic.twitter.com/UMRILP4TWy — Zach Cohen (@ZachCohenFB) July 24, 2026 Steve Wyche, Chief National Reporter for NFL Network and NFL.com clearly thought highly of the Rams “Fearsome White” uniform. The Rams D-Line (for now) rocking the new alternate Fearsome Foursome threads that will debut Thanksgiving Eve vs. Green Bay🧊🧊🧊🧊 pic.twitter.com/XdmJLUOva1 — Steve Wyche (@wyche89) July 24, 2026 Application received. One of the best dressed teams in football. https://t.co/U3woNSccp0 pic.twitter.com/8ZTFWLT7ZS — NFL Fashion Advice (@fashion_nfl) July 24, 2026 Around the NFL, many fans pointed to the “Fearsome White” uniform as an instant favorite. The clean white-on-white combination with royal blue accents has been described as timeless, with many comparing it favorably to some of the league’s best throwback-inspired uniforms. …and it's finally here! The all yellows are pretty sick! LOVE the blue and whites. Pretty much what everyone was expecting, but now it's confirmed. Two awesome throwback options in the rotation for the Rams this season. — Blaine Grisak 💭 (@BGMediaOnSI) July 24, 2026 Uniform analysts around the league have called the Rams’ redesign one of the biggest improvements of the NFL offseason, noting that small changes—such as eliminating gradients, simplifying the numbering, and embracing historical color palettes—dramatically elevated the franchise’s overall look. Ultimately, the true test will come under the lights at SoFi Stadium. Jerseys often look different during game action than they do during photo shoots or social media reveals. But if the early reactions are any indication, the Rams may have delivered one of the NFL’s biggest offseason victories without a single snap being played. Whether fans prefer the crisp “Fearsome White” or the vibrant “Classic Sol,” Los Angeles has once again become one of the league’s most talked-about teams—and this time, it’s because of what they’re wearing.

title: Continuing upward trend vital for Jonah Laulu and Raiders’ defense
summary: More snaps equals more production tends to the tale of the NFL tape. Such was the case for Las Vegas Raiders defensive tackle Jonah Laulu. Logging 764 snaps over the course of 17 games (15 starts) in 2025, the Sin City-native had a productive Year 2 totaling 51 tackles (eight behind the line of scrimmage), […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - DECEMBER 14: Las Vegas Raiders defensive tackle Jonah Laulu #96 gets set during the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Philadelphia Eagles on December 14th, 2025 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images More snaps equals more production tends to the tale of the NFL tape. Such was the case for Las Vegas Raiders defensive tackle Jonah Laulu. Logging 764 snaps over the course of 17 games (15 starts) in 2025, the Sin City-native had a productive Year 2 totaling 51 tackles (eight behind the line of scrimmage), four sacks, and five pass deflections — all career highs. As a rookie in 2024, Laulu notched 475 snaps and in 17 games (seven starts) tallied 35 total tackles (three stops for loss) alongside a sack and a trio of pass deflections. Not bad for a scrapheap-type flier waiver claim by the Silver & Black a day after after Laulu was waived as a 2024 NFL Draft seventh-round pick (234th overall) by the Indianapolis Colts on August 27, 2024. By The Numbers Jonah Laulu, Defensive Tackle, 3rd Year 2025: 17 games (15 starts), 51 total tackles (24 solo), 8 tackles for loss, 4 sacks, 5 pass deflections Career: 34 games (22 starts), 86 total tackles (39 solo), 11 tackles for loss, 5 sacks, 8 pass deflections Continuing that upward trend is vital for both Laulu and the Raiders defense. The 26-year-old is not only an ascending young player but at 6-foot-5 and 289 pounds, the Oklahoma product has the size and versatility to line up at defensive end in Las Vegas base 3-4 alignment and shifting back inside to tackle when defensive coordinator Rob Leonard deploys even-man fronts. Vegas native, #Raiders DT Jonah Laulu says ‘it’d be dope’ to be a part of the core group that turns the team into a winner “When I went to Hawaii, that's kind of how it was. Before I got there, they didn't really have that many wins. When I got there, we got the culture turned… pic.twitter.com/xyu5DAyhi4 — Nick Walters (@nickwalt) January 5, 2026 While he brings plenty of height, Laulu’s listed weight is lighter in comparison to other Raiders interior defensive linemen. At 289 pounds, the only other counterpart lighter is Tonka Hemingway (6-foot-2 and 284 pounds). Why is this distinction important? While athletic and bringing suddenness off the snap, Laulu has struggled taking on heavy double teams — which are frequent on the interior. Fortunately for Laulu, Las Vegas’ transition to a 3-4 base defensive front will help insulate him from this exact thing. A well-executed odd front naturally limits offensive lines from executing combination blocks as it’s unclear to the offense what defenders are doing exactly. The 3-4 front helps create confusion as a combination of defenders can be sent on blitzes to get after the quarterback or stuff running lanes while others may feign rush only to drop back in coverage. Laulu’s quickness off the snap looms large as a positive as lining up as a defensive end in 3-4 looks provides him the opportunity to take on tackles and use his ample length and explosion to make an impact as both rusher and run stopper. Sustained Statistics “It’s an effort-based front,” Raiders defensive line boss Travis Smith noted. “Whether we’re rushing four, we’re rushing five, we’re rushing three — it doesn’t matter. The intensity and disposition that we play with is non-negotiable.” Count Laulu as an effort-based paragon in Silver & Black. Arriving with a chip on his shoulder getting waived after about four months of time with the Colts, Laulu showcased an exceptionally high motor and relentlessness that endeared himself to Leonard, who served as the Raiders defensive line coach before being elevated by head coach Klint Kubiak as the defensive coordinator this offseason. Leonard saw up close that urgency and it aligns with his own aggressive philosophy of never quit. While not on the gold standard level of Maxx Crosby, Laulu’s grit allows him to overcome technical shortcomings as he’s able to stay on a play and continue to chase down quarterbacks and ballcarriers, alike. The four sacks the defensive tackle accumulated in the first six weeks of the 2025 regular season is a testament to that. However, the quarterback takedown in a 20-10 victory over the visiting Tennessee Titans in Week 6 was the final sack of Laulu’s tally this past year. Sustaining sack production throughout the course of a 17-week regular season is a must for the defender. While Laulu did well to rack up 11 pressures, two hurries, and seven quarterback hits — according to Pro Football Reference — I’ll go with the patented Crosby phrase (from the late great Kobe Bryant): More is required. Colts 7th round pick Jonah Laulu thought he was being prank called by GM Chris Ballard 💀 pic.twitter.com/tP3aOmm2GW — NFL Retweet (@NFLRT) April 28, 2024 An Anchor Refining his deficiencies as a run defender is integral for Laulu’s continued development and for the betterment of Las Vegas defense, overall. To improve on this portion of his game, he’ll need to work on pad level, hand usage, and lower-body strength and leverage. Excelling as a pass rusher only gets you so far and if teams identify you as a weak link against the run, they’ll attack Laulu until he proves he’s a stout run stuffer. Gaining more functional lower-body strength presents more of an anchor factor and keeping his base wide and pad level low helps prevent Laulu from getting washed out by offensive linemen. And quicker hand fighting can present more fluid block shedding at the point of attack. And this all belabors one of the stark statistics on Laulu’s resume, from Pro Football Reference: Missed tackles. The group charted Laulu with 10 missed tackles in 2025 , a distinction that ties the defensive lineman with safety Jeremy Chinn as the fourth most on the team. Improved tackling is a team issue I’ll explore in a separate piece later this week. Fiscal Future Being claimed off waivers, Las Vegas inherited the four-year, $4.124-plus million contract Laulu inked as a seventh-round pick by Indianapolis. The 2026 season represents Year 3 of that pact with the defender earning a modest $1.075 million this coming year. The 2027 season marks the final of the rookie pact with Laulu slated to earn $1.19 million. Continuing his upward trajectory as viable contributor on the Raiders certainly has a fiscal impact on his future as he can earn vastly more with stacked productive seasons this coming year and next — from Las Vegas or one of the other 31 teams in the league. As it stands now, Laulu is set to hit unrestricted free agency in the 2028 offseason sans a contract extension with the Raiders before then.

title: Las Vegas Raiders pushing for All-Pro honors in 2026
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders didn’t have an All-Pro selected for the 2025 season, the first time in nearly half a decade the team didn’t have a player selected with the award. In 2025, TE Brock Bowers was named as a first team All-Pro by the AP, NFLPA, PFF, & PFW while AJ Cole was named […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - DECEMBER 7: Brock Bowers #89 of the Las Vegas Raiders runs downfield during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Allegiant Stadium on December 07, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders didn’t have an All-Pro selected for the 2025 season, the first time in nearly half a decade the team didn’t have a player selected with the award. In 2025, TE Brock Bowers was named as a first team All-Pro by the AP, NFLPA, PFF, & PFW while AJ Cole was named the PFF & NFLPA 2nd team All-Pro. Extending back to 2023, Maxx Crosby & Cole were named All-Pro’s, and 2022 saw the Raiders peak with Josh Jacobs, Davante Adams, Maxx Crosby, Daniel Carlson, and AJ Cole all earn All-Pro honors. The Raiders have a variety of players that can push for a possible All-Pro selection this season, though All-Pro honors are also widely tied to team success as well, and if Las Vegas can’t cross at least 6-8 wins it may be harder for them. Strong Odds: TE Brock Bowers – Finished 10th in AP All-Pro Voting in 2025 Bowers was named an All-Pro in his rookie season after hauling in 112 receptions, 1194 yards, and 5 touchdowns. He suffered a knee injury early into the 2025 season which limited him to 12 games, but was truly healthy for only 9-10 of those and still posted 64 receptions, 680 yards, and seven touchdowns. Bowers is not without competition as Cardinals’ Trey McBride, Chiefs’ Travis Kelce, Falcons’ Kyle Pitts, and 49ers George Kittle all earned All-Pro honors last year. McBride is coming off back to back 1200+ yard seasons, Kelce remains one of the better tight ends in the NFL with top name recognition. Pitts will see a large volume of work this season operating as a big slot and thus large production, & Kittle is among the best blocking TE in the NFL and widely considered a top 3 player in the NFL at the position. Bowers will see a large volume of production moving around the Raiders offense, and thus his production should be high enough to get the All-Pro honors, especially after being ranked as the third best TE in the NFL by personnel staffs, via ESPN. Among those mentioned, Colts’ Tyler Warren, Lions’ Sam LaPorta, and Packers’ Tucker Kraft could see big seasons and also push Bowers for the honor. EDGE Maxx Crosby – Finished 8th in AP All-Pro Voting in 2025 Crosby has traditionally been viewed by All-Pro voters as a DE, instead of an OLB, which does make his competition a bit tougher. The 2025 season saw Will Anderson, Myles Garrett, Micah Parsons, and Aidan Hutchinson all earn first team EDGE rushers honor, along with Brian Burns, Tuli Tuipultou, and Byron Young. Parsons is expected to miss most of the season, and he should likely be out of the running but pending injuries you can pencil in Anderson, Garrett, and Hutchinson as shoe ins with Tuipulotu and Young having a good chance as well to push for the spot given their situations. Crosby is coming off a 2025 season, where I’m shocked he didn’t at least make a 2nd team All-Pro, after logging 73 tackles, 28 TFL, 10 sacks, an INT, 6 PBU, and 2 FF. Crosby did see his pressure rate fall, and he did miss games with injuries, but he’s remained one of the best players in the NFL against the run, which will push in his favor going forward. Crosby should see a lower workload, but that will increase his overall efficiency and thus likely higher numbers. Keep an eye on Browns’ Jared Verse, Texans’ Danielle Hunter, 49ers Nick Bosa, and Ravens’ Trey Hendrickson who can all push for the spot as well. P AJ Cole – Did not receive an AP All-Pro Vote in 2025 For the first time since 2021, AJ Cole was not named to the first or second team All-Pro, but I’d expect him back on track in 2026. Cole logged 71 punts (2nd highest in his career) for 3379 yards, a 47.6 average (3rd worst in his career), a 5.6% touchback rate, and a 34% in20 rank. Cole saw his In20 rate fall, as did his net yards/punt. The 30 year old is coming off a down season, but apparently was dealing with some lower body injuries, and the Raiders punt units were far from the previous levels they had been in 2021-2023. Last season saw Lions Jack Fox, Jaguars Logan Cooke, and Seahawks Michael Dickson all also earn honors, and I’d imagine Fox is one of the biggest competitors for Cole with his recent success. Cole has been a tremendous punter, and currently holds the NFL All-Time record for career yards/punt. Keep an eye on Packers Daniel Whelan, Jets’s Austin McNamara, Commanders’ Tress Way, & Giants Jordan Stout as others who can push for the spot. First Time but Possible: OL Tyler Linderbaum – Finished 3rd in AP All-Pro voting in 2025, 2024, & 4th in 2023 Linderbaum has never been named to a first or second team all-pro, and it’s largely due to his inconsistencies as a pass protector. Linderbaum has never been the best pass protector, but he’s been a top 3-5 center in that regard. Where Linderbaum does pop off the screen, and where he’s made his pure money is his pre snap abilities, and run blocking, which both will play huge roles in the Raiders system under Klint Kubiak. The former Ravens star has stayed healthy in his career, and he figures to be a gamechanger for the Raiders offense that struggled in the run game last year. Last season saw Chiefs’ Creed Humphrey, Bears Drew Dalman (who’s since retired), and Dolphins Aaron Brewer earn All-Pro honors. Linderbaum was named the 2nd best center in the NFL by personnel executives, a good sign for his chances, but also keep an eye on Eagles’ Cam Jurgens, Vikings’ Ryan Kelly, and Brown Elgton Jenkins. ILB Tommy Eichenberg – Finished 9th in AP All-Pro Special Teams Voting in 2025 Eichenberg won’t make the All-Pro list at linebacker, but the official PFW and AP lists include special teams standouts. As noted, Eichenberg did finish with 3 votes last season largely off his 2025 season that had 22 tackles which ranked top 5 in the NFL for special teams tackles. Additionally, his special teams EPA was 7th among all special teams players (not counting returners). Eichenberg figures to be a big staple of the Raiders special teams units in 2026, alongside Cody Lindenberg, Dareke Young, and Segun Olubi with Olubi one to watch after finishing 15th last season off just 14 tackles, a blocked punt (ironically on AJ Cole), and 2 FR. The Raiders need an overhauled special teams unit, and Eichenberg should be the staple Long Shots: RB Ashton Jeanty – Did not receive an AP All-Pro Vote in 2025 The runningback position is super volatile in the NFL, and especially in the All-Pro/Pro-Bowl spaces. Last season saw James Cook, Christian McCaffrey, Bijan Robinson, De’Von Achane, and Jonathan Taylor earn votes and they should again in 2026 if they stay healthy. Additionally, Saquon Barkley, Derrick Henry, Breece Hall, and Kenneth Walker should see some attention in the space. Jeanty was not ranked among the top 10 runningbacks in the NFL within the recent NFL executives poll, but was named an honorable mention. The top ten selection finished his rookie season with 975 yards, five touchdowns, a 3.7 yards per carry, and an additional 346 yards and five touchdowns in the air. Jeanty’s under the hood numbers were impressive in his breakaway ratings, elusiveness, missed tackles forced, broken tackles, and all while his offensive line and yards before contact ranked inside the bottom five for the NFL. Jeanty is talented, he provides a ton of big play ability, and working in a wide zone for the 2026 season should be beneficial, but it will be a long shot for him to make the All-Pro list. ILB Nakobe Dean – Did not receive an AP All-Pro Vote in 2025 & 15th in 2024 Nakobe Dean played just 15 games in 2024 but he posted 128 tackles, 10 TFL, 3 sacks, 4 PBU, a FF, interception, and 2 FR while also posting nearly 30 pressures which is largely why he earned a few All-Pro votes. Assuming Dean can stay healthy, which has been a big task in his career, I can truly…

title: Raiders training camp 2026 preview
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders’ first training camp practice will be held Wednesday. Here are three storylines to look for: The injuries: The big early training camp questions will be about star defensive end Maxx Crosby, free-agent addition, linebacker Nakobe Dean and rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy. They missed all or most of the offseason sessions. The […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 11: Nakobe Dean #17 of the Philadelphia Eagles exits the field after warmups prior to an NFL wild card playoff football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Lincoln Financial Field on January 11, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ first training camp practice will be held Wednesday. Here are three storylines to look for: The injuries: The big early training camp questions will be about star defensive end Maxx Crosby, free-agent addition, linebacker Nakobe Dean and rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy. They missed all or most of the offseason sessions. The team has said they expect them all to be ready for training camp fairly early on. So, this is a key for the Raiders as they try to be as healthy as possible for the Sept. 13 season opener against the Miami Dolphins. The quarterbacks: Eyes around the NFL will be on raining cap as veteran Kirk Cousins and rookie Fernando Mendoza will compete. There has been some media speculation that it may not be much of a battle because the Raiders are leaning toward making Cousins the starter. Still, Mendoza, who is expected to get some first-team reps in camp, has a chance to steal the job in training camp and in the preseason and that starts as soon as camp begins. The kicking battles: There will be many camp battles other than at quarterback, including at wide receiver, the offensive line, the defensive line a nd in the secondary. But the kicking battle is also key. The Daniel Carlson era is over and this competition will be one of the biggest in training camp this year. The competition between veteran addition Matt Gay and heralded undrafted rookie Kansei Matsuzawa AKA The Tokyo Toe will be worth watching on a daily basis. Join the conversation! title: Vikings Training Camp 2026: Position-by-Position Breakdown
summary: The Minnesota Vikings are officially heading into training camp, and The Real Forno Show just dropped a must-listen, position-by-position preview covering every unit on the roster — from the quarterback competition to the kicker’s contract future. Hosted by Tyler Forness with producer Dave Stefano, this episode of the Vikings 1st & SKOL podcast is exactly […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - MAY 27: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings participates in a drill during an OTA workout at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on May 27, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are officially heading into training camp, and The Real Forno Show just dropped a must-listen, position-by-position preview covering every unit on the roster — from the quarterback competition to the kicker’s contract future. Hosted by Tyler Forness with producer Dave Stefano, this episode of the Vikings 1st & SKOL podcast is exactly what every Vikings fan needs before camp kicks off. If you want to know what’s really at stake this summer in Eagan, this is your comprehensive guide. The centerpiece of this episode is the J.J. McCarthy vs. Kyler Murray quarterback competition, and Forness makes a compelling case that the decision will come well before the regular season — despite Ian Rapoport’s suggestion otherwise. Citing head coach Kevin O’Connell directly, Forness zeroes in on this quote: “We wanna make sure that by the time we play the Green Bay Packers, there’s been ample time to have the best possible offense we can have to help our football team.” Forness argues August 23rd — right after the Ravens preseason joint practices — is the ideal decision date, giving the eventual starter at least three full weeks of starter reps before Week 1. “Three-plus weeks of practice and then three weeks until the start of the season,” he said. “That’s gonna be your sweet spot.” Beyond the quarterback battle, Forness and Stefano break down every position group, surface key training camp battles to watch, and identify under-the-radar players who could make a real impact in 2026. Key Points from the Episode: QB Competition Timeline: Forness pegs August 23rd as the ideal date to end the McCarthy/Murray competition — after three weeks of camp and joint practices with Baltimore. “I think the 23rd is that date… it gives you three full weeks to roll with the starter.” Running Back Depth: Aaron Jones is likely the starter, but Jordan Mason’s fit in a wide-zone scheme makes him dangerous. “Jordan Mason thrives in the wide zone, plus 3.5 yards per carry after contact — massive amount of success.” Zavier Scott is favored over Demond Claiborne for RB3 due to special teams utility. Wide Receivers to Watch: Beyond Jefferson, Addison, and Jennings, keep an eye on Dillon Bell (big mini-camp buzz) and undrafted free agent Dontae Fleming. “If you can find a way to make plays when you don’t have opportunities, what happens when you get them?” T.J. Hockenson Bounce-Back? Forness believes Hockenson — not yet 30 — will rebound from a down year. “If he’s good, gets like 750 yards, five touchdowns, that’s a pretty good option to have considering you’re gonna have three star wide receivers.” Edge Rusher Concerns: The depth behind Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel is a genuine worry. Forness is skeptical of Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins at edge: “The second you ask him to bend the arc, it’s toast.” He advocates for a veteran addition like Jadeveon Clowney. Jake Golday, LB: His development sets off a chain reaction in the linebacker room. If he’s good, Ivan Pace Jr.’s $3.52M salary could be a cap casualty. Specialists: The punter competition between Brett Thorson and Johnny Hecker is worth watching, but Will Reichard’s kicking operation remains elite. Forness projects a four-year, $30 million extension for the All-Pro kicker. Listen: View Link Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: The Real Forno Show is one of the sharpest, most detailed Vikings podcasts in the game. Tyler Forness brings legitimate insider knowledge and analytical depth, while Dave Stefano keeps the conversation honest and engaging. Whether you’re a casual fan or a die-hard Vikings obsessive, this training camp preview episode is essential listening before the pads go on. Subscribe on YouTube, like the video, and ring the bell so you don’t miss a single episode as camp ramps up. Fan with Us!!! title: Patriots 53-man roster projection before training camp
summary: The New England Patriots’ 2026 training camp isn’t just around the corner anymore. It’s here. At 10 a.m. ET on Saturday, the reigning AFC champions will take the field for the first time. With that, the competition for the roster spots will heat up immensely. With currently 92 players on the team but only 53 […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - MAY 27: Robert Spillane #14 of the New England Patriots during New England Patriots OTA on May 27, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. Sportswire) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots’ 2026 training camp isn’t just around the corner anymore. It’s here. At 10 a.m. ET on Saturday, the reigning AFC champions will take the field for the first time. With that, the competition for the roster spots will heat up immensely. With currently 92 players on the team but only 53 spots available, players will try to put their best foot forward from the get-go and show that they are indeed deserving of making the cut over their peers. How that will shake out remains to be seen. From our perspective, at least, the following will happen. Welcome to the first roster projection of the summer. Quarterback In (2): Drake Maye, Tommy DeVito Out (1): Behren Morton Drake Maye took a massive sophomore leap last season, finishing just shy of being named MVP. In his third season and second with offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, he looks to continue his growth as The Guy in New England. Rookie seventh-round pick Behren Morton has an intriguing profile as a backup quarterback behind Drake Maye, but he lands outside the 53-man roster and likely on the practice squad here until we see him earn a spot in camp. Veteran backup Tommy DeVito is fine enough for that spot and knows the system, so he gets the nod. If we’re thinking about either Morton or DeVito at any point past Labor Day, something has gone seriously wrong. With Drake Maye at the helm, the only play either of them should need to know this year is run out of victory formation. Running back In (3): Rhamondre Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson, Jam Miller Out (3): Lan Larison, Terrell Jennings, Myles Montgomery After early fumbles had fans calling for Rhamondre Stevenson to be cut last year, he quickly turned the season around and became a dependable three-down weapon. He’s the team’s most consistent runner between the tackles, most consistent pass blocker in the backfield, and best route runner at the position. He’ll be joined by TreVeyon Henderson, a boom-or-bust threat who singlehandedly won multiple games for the Pats last season but who needs to have less “bust” in his game to be a more dependable option down to down. In this projection, they’re joined by rookie seventh-rounder Jam Miller from Alabama. Miller projects as a solid backup for Stevenson as a between-the-tackles runner, edging out Terrell Jennings for that role. Second-year UDFA Lan Larison and rookie UDFA Myles Montgomery add more in the passing game and could challenge for the third running back slot or force the team to keep four on the roster. Fullback In (1): Reggie Gilliam Out (1): Jack Westover Reggie Gilliam is a quality starter at fullback, spending the last six seasons in Buffalo where he played in 108 games and started 13. The Patriots signed him to a three-year, $12 million contract this offseason to help improve a running game that struggled for most of last season. He’s a clear upgrade over Westover, who made the position change from tight end to fullback after UDFA Brock Lampe was injured early in camp last year. Westover may still make the 53-man roster as a third tight end and backup fullback, but for now his role projects as backup fullback in camp who may make the practice squad. Tight end In (3): Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon, C.J. Dippre Out (3): Tanner Arkin, Mitch Van Vooren, Jeremiah Franklin IR (1): Julian Hill Veteran Hunter Henry returns for a sixth season in New England, looking to reprise his role as Drake Maye’s safety blanket. He had a career-best season with 768 receiving yards last year, beating out his 674 yards from the year before. It is safe to say Maye likes throwing the ball his way. New England added Dolphins tight end Julian Hill as a blocking tight end in free agency, but an injury in June ended his first year with the Patriots early. That thrusts rookie third-round pick Eli Raridon out of Notre Dame into a bigger role as the second tight end on the depth chart. Behind Raridon is an open competition for the third tight end spot. C.J. Dippre gets the nod here for his blocking skills and experience in the system, although he is starting the summer on the PUP list . That will give Westover, Tanner Arkin, and the newly signed Mitch Van Vooren and Jeremiah Franklin an opportunity to fight for that role, and the Patriots may continue to add at the position. Wide receiver In (6): A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, Kayshon Boutte, Kyle Williams, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas Out (5): Efton Chism III, Jeremiah Webb, Nick DeGennaro, Cameron Dorner, Kyle Dixon IR (1): Jimmy Kibble It’s not that long ago that wide receiver was the weakest position on New England’s roster. Now, the Patriots enter camp with it being their deepest. Trade addition AJ Brown is a clear No. 1 option who can line up anywhere on the field, and free agent signing Romeo Doubs is a consistent No. 2 who also has versatility. After those two, Josh McDaniels has a host of options to put out there in the third receiver slot. Kayshon Boutte is the best all-around receiver who has real chemistry with Maye. He may end up being traded, but for now he lands on the roster. Behind him, second-year wideout Kyle Williams is your speed option to threaten safeties and create big plays. Veteran Mack Hollins is your power-slot receiver who can block well and make catches away from his body. DeMario Douglas returns as the team’s most natural man-beating slot receiver, where his speed and twitch make him hard to cover. Efton Chism narrowly misses the cut here, but if Boutte is traded or an injury happens at this position, he’s the next guy up. It will be tough for anyone outside those seven to threaten for a roster spot, although Jeremiah Webb is another returning UDFA from last year who flashed as a kick returner in camp. Offensive tackle In (4): Will Campbell, Morgan Moses, Caleb Lomu, James Hudson III Out (3): Marcus Bryant, Dametrious Crownover, Lorenz Metz If wide receiver wasn’t the weakest position on the roster in 2024, offensive tackle was. New England responded by using their 2025 (Will Campbell) and 2026 (Caleb Lomu) first-round picks at the position while signing Morgan Moses as a bridge starter. The Patriots hope Campbell will look better at left tackle in year two after recovering from an injury that hampered his play in the second half of his rookie year, and the veteran Moses looks to put together another solid season at right tackle after playing more snaps than any other offensive lineman last season. Rookie Lomu projects as a backup at four spots on the offensive line in year one while he hits the weight room to put on muscle. Behind those three, I have veteran James Hudson cracking the roster to provide a high floor at the position. He’s a competent backup swing tackle with experience in the league, and they may need that in a group with two young players. A pair of day-three picks in Marcus Bryant, who fell out of favor last year for Thayer Munford, and rookie Dametrious Crownover are intriguing developmental options who may land on the practice squad for more seasoning. Interior offensive line In (6): Alijah Vera-Tucker, Jared Wilson, Mike Onwenu, Ben Brown, Andrew Rupcich, Caedan Wallace Out (4): Mehki Butler, Sebastian Gutierrez, Jacob Rizy, JonDarius Morgan The Patriots bolstered their line by adding one of the riskiest free agents to start at left guard. Alijah Vera-Tucker is a player who could be an All-Pro at his position, starring as a dynamic run blocker. The catch? He’s only on the field about half the time due to a series of injuries throughout his career. He’ll start next to Jared Wilson, last year’s left guard who slides over into his more natural position at center. Wilson was the weakest link on the line last year, but the position change combined with a second year in the system could be the…

title: Patriots training camp preview 2026: Eli Raridon enters spotlight at tight end
summary: Based on the New England Patriots’ 2026 offseason moves, the organization made improving quarterback Drake Maye’s offensive weapons a priority. In the process, the Patriots added to a previously aging tight end room. Following an Austin Hooper exit to the Atlanta Falcons in free agency, New England signed hybrid tight end Julian Hill. It also […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA- JUNE 11: Eli Raridon #82 of the New England Patriots speaks to the media after New England Patriots Minicamp on June 11, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Summer Lamont/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Based on the New England Patriots’ 2026 offseason moves, the organization made improving quarterback Drake Maye’s offensive weapons a priority. In the process, the Patriots added to a previously aging tight end room. Following an Austin Hooper exit to the Atlanta Falcons in free agency, New England signed hybrid tight end Julian Hill . It also selected Notre Dame’s Eli Raridon in the third round of the NFL Draft. However, a season-ending injury to Hill during a spring practice left a void in the group that remains unresolved. In the final edition of our Patriots training camp preview series, we’ll take a look at New England’s tight end corps in its entirety and discuss the biggest takeaways heading into the summer practices. *Denotes player on the Pats Pulpit 53-man roster projection Depth chart Starters: Hunter Henry (31)*, Eli Raridon (22/R)* | Backups: Tanner Arkin (22/R)*, Jack Westover (27) , C.J. Dippre (24) , Mitch Van Vooren (25), Jeremiah Franklin (22) | IR: Julian Hill (25) Hunter Henry is entering his sixth season leading the position group and has proved to be nothing short of reliable. But as he enters his age-31 season, it’s fair to question whether he’ll have the same receiving impact on offense as in recent years. So far, there haven’t been any indications this offseason of that being the case, and with unproven depth behind him, New England will need him to remain a stable presence. The Patriots drafted Raridon as another receiving threat to pair with Henry, who can also extend vertically up the seam and be a red-zone threat. Two ACL tears on the same knee frequently sidelined him during his first two collegiate seasons with the Fighting Irish; Raridon’s a developmental piece that will need to make a quick impact in Foxboro. New England’s fullback last season, Jack Westover, is also returning and switching back to tight end following the Reggie Gilliam signing . The 27-year-old has only caught two receptions in his Patriots career but was an All-Pac-12 honorable mention in 2023 as a receiver at Washington. Rounding out the depth chart are 2025 undrafted free agent C.J. Dippre, who spent the majority of his rookie campaign on the practice squad, undrafted rookies Tanner Arkin and Jeremiah Franklin. The latter, just like second-year man Mitch Van Vooren, was added right before camp. Without Hill practicing, Dippre or Arkin seem to have the best opportunity out of quartet to make the final roster primarily as a blocking tight end. Key question: Will New England keep adding to the unit? While Hill’s strength is blocking, executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf believes he has untapped potential as a receiver . However, the tight end’s injury restructures the position heading into training camp, leaving the Patriots without an immediate versatile blocker and receiving threat even after adding the likes of Van Vooren and Franklin. As a consequence, the team might keep exploring the market to add some veteran talent. A few available free agents include renowned blockers include Will Dissly, Nick Vannett and Pharaoh Brown, who was with New England in 2023. Having an established blocker in the room would. help seal the open wound left by Hill and give the team more security than the likes of Arkin, Van Vooren and Franklin can provide. This would also allow Raridon to step up in a high-volume receiving role. X-Factor: Eli Raridon Because of Raridon’s natural ability as a receiver, he can make a substantial impact as a receiving threat for Maye in year one. The athletic tight end posted a 9.46 Relative Athletic Score for his testing at the NFL Combine in March. Raridon is also a fluid mover for his size (6-foot-6, 245 pounds) with a large catch radius. He can be a consistent target over the middle of the field at the intermediate level and vertically. “Willing, conscientious, wants to learn,” Vrabel said of Raridon’s progress at minicamp. “I think there are a lot of new things that come in from college, and terminology is different, and there are a lot of things that are new to him, but I would say that he picks things up quickly. When he’s able to play with the speed that he has available to him, that’s kind of shown up.” Still, it may take considerable time for the rookie to earn consistent offensive snaps. Raridon’s extensive list of previous injuries in college makes him more of a project player to begin his young career. In addition to refining technical components, as a receiver, the issue with him immediately stepping into a high-volume role is the necessary improvement as a blocker. If Raridon finds his stride in training camp, increasing his play strength at the point of attack and refining his technique, he’ll be a dynamic weapon for the offense and quickly fill a pressing need.
author: Andrew Guindon

title: What signing Jeremiah Franklin, waiving Jimmy Kibble means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots made a pair of roster moves on the eve of their 2026 training camp. Besides making the previously-reported signing of tight end Jeremiah Franklin official, they also waived wide receiver Jimmy Kibble with an injury designation. Let’s assess what the two moves involving rookie players mean for the club. More tight […]
full_text: Nov 1, 2025; Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts, USA; Boston College Tight End Jeremiah Franklin (17) runs with the ball during warmups before the game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at Alumni Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Edward Finan-Imagn Images | Edward Finan-Imagn Images The New England Patriots made a pair of roster moves on the eve of their 2026 training camp. Besides making the previously-reported signing of tight end Jeremiah Franklin official, they also waived wide receiver Jimmy Kibble with an injury designation. Let’s assess what the two moves involving rookie players mean for the club. More tight end depth The Patriots made no secret of their desire to add to their tight end room after losing Julian Hill to a season-ending injury earlier in the offseason. They did just that this week, signing Franklin and second-year man Mitch Van Vooren on consecutive days. As a consequence, their tight end room is now seven players deep: Tight end (7): Hunter Henry (85), Jack Westover (37), Eli Raridon (82), C.J. Dippre (81), Tanner Arkin (84), Mitch Van Vooren (46), Jeremiah Franklin (80) IR (1): Julian Hill Hunter Henry is the undisputed starter, with third-round rookie Eli Raridon locked into a roster spot behind him. The rest of the group, meanwhile, is set to be participate in what could be an intense camp competition for what is unlikely to be more than one spot if even that. Based on the spring, Jack Westover looks like the frontrunner. C.J. Dippre, his top competitor as far as experience is concerned, will start camp on the physically unable to perform list. Well-rounded skillset Franklin is neither the biggest of tight ends nor the most impressive athlete, as evidenced by his comparatively uninspiring 3.29 Relative Athletic Score. What Franklin lacks in any defining traits, however, he makes up with a well-rounded skillset: he is able as an in-line blocker and also has proven himself a reliable underneath receiver during his career at Boston College; he caught 93 passes for 1,010 yards and six touchdowns in his 44 games as an Eagle. In addition, Franklin comes from a program whose offense has some similarities to the one he has just joined. While that experience will only help him so much, the transition from Chestnut Hill to Foxborough will not be quite as drastic as it could have been had he joined another team. Thinning the receiver herd The Patriots did not select any wide receivers in this year’s draft, but they opted to sign four of them as rookie free agents. Kibble was one of them, but has now become the first one to be let go again. This reduces the number of wide receivers on New England’s roster to 11: Wide receiver (11): A.J. Brown (1), Romeo Doubs (87), Kayshon Boutte (9), Mack Hollins (13), Kyle Williams (18), DeMario Douglas (3), Efton Chism III (86), Jeremiah Webb (29), Kyle Dixon (83), Nick DeGennaro (23), Cameron Dorner (88) A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs project as the top two on the depth chart after the Patriots made significant investments in both during the offseason. The complementary roster spots alongside them, meanwhile, will be subject to one of the fiercest competitions of the summer. Off to IR The Patriots’ initial announcement of the Kibble move claimed that was sent to injured reserve, but the NFL transactions wire revealed that the move was more complex than that. Before joining IR, the rookie will have to pass through the waiver wire. Given his injury status and the fact that he entered the league as a rookie free agent, demand in his services will likely be limited and he should be expected to go unclaimed. If so, Kibble will join the aforementioned Julian Hill as the only players on New England’s injured reserve so far. Both will be out for the season, unless the nature of Kibble’s ailment would allow for him to return to the field at a later point in the year. If so, he might get released off IR with an injury settlement beforehand and could therefore potentially play again later this season. No salary cap impact While every rostered NFL player has a salary cap number, not every one of those numbers actually impacts a team’s cap space during the offseason. With the Top 51 rule in place — meaning that only the most expensive 51 contracts are counted until the start of the regular season — a significant chunk of players have no such impact. That is true for Kibble and Franklin as well. Both were signed to standard undrafted rookie deals with a salary of $885,000 and no guarantees attached. Hence, no cap changes at this point even with the former moving off the roster and the latter joining it in his place.

Sportswire) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A 91-man roster spot changed hands at Gillette Stadium on the eve of training camp. The New England Patriots waived wide receiver Jimmy Kibble with an injury designation on Friday, according to the NFL transaction wire. As a result, the Georgetown product is on track to revert to injured reserve after going through the league’s claiming period over the weekend. The move effectively ends his rookie season in July, provided an injury settlement is not reached at a later date. Kibble, 22, agreed to terms in Foxborough as part of the club’s 2026 undrafted class in May. The 6-foot-1, 199-pound wideout appeared in 39 games while at Georgetown. His Hoyas career spanned 149 receptions for 2,642 yards and 16 touchdowns. First-team All-Patriot League honors arrived for Kibble in 2025 on the heels of catching 63 passes for 1,002 yards and four touchdowns as a team captain. New England’s active wideout depth chart now stands at 11. With first practice of training camp set to kick off at 10:15 a.m. ET on Saturday, the position includes A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, Kayshon Boutte, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III, Jeremiah Webb, as well as rookie free agents Kyle Dixon, Nick DeGennaro and Cameron Dorner. A corresponding move loomed for the Patriots before the previously reported signing of tight end Jeremiah Franklin could become official .

title: Former Patriots offensive lineman Jordan Devey dead at 38
summary: Jordan Devey, a member of the New England Patriots’ 2014 Super Bowl team, has passed away. He was 38 years old. Devey’s wife, Linsey, shared the news on social media. Born in American Fork, Utah, Devey did not play football in high school but instead was an avid tuba player as well as a member […]
full_text: August 1, 2015: New England Patriots tackle Jordan Devey (65) during the New England Patriots practice session for training camp. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire/Corbis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Jordan Devey, a member of the New England Patriots’ 2014 Super Bowl team, has passed away. He was 38 years old. Devey’s wife, Linsey, shared the news on social media . Born in American Fork, Utah, Devey did not play football in high school but instead was an avid tuba player as well as a member of the Cavemen’s basketball team. After serving a two-year mission in Costa Rica, he enrolled at Snow College in 2009 and two years later transferred to Memphis. Devey went on to go unselected in the 2013 NFL Draft, but he found a temporary home with the Ravens. After the Ravens let him go that same summer, the Patriots picked him up through their practice squad. He found his was to the 53-man roster the following season and went on to start four of the seven games he appeared in. To cap off the 2014 season, Devey earned a Super Bowl ring as a reserve lineman. The Patriots traded him to San Francisco the following training camp. He later also spent three seasons with the Chiefs, and one each with the Raiders and Bills. In total, he ended his eight-year NFL career with a combined 45 regular season and playoff appearances. After leaving the NFL, Devey and his family relocated to Eagle, Idaho. He worked as a volunteer coach and mentor at Eagle High School at the time of his passing. Devey is survived by his wife as well as four kids. A GoFundMe to financially support the Devey family has been set up. Please follow this link if you can donate.

title: Patriots players react to DeAndre Hopkins working with coaching staff
summary: As Robert Spillane finished his conditioning test on Friday, he spotted a familiar, but unexpected face, near the back of the practice field. full_text: Patriots cornerback Marcus Jones (25) defends Cardinals wide receiver DeAndre Hopkins (10) during the first half of a game at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Dec. 12, 2022. As Robert Spillane finished his conditioning test on Friday, he spotted a familiar, but unexpected face, near the back of the practice field. That was former Tennessee Titan teammate DeAndre Hopkins, who is working with the Patriots coaching staff the next few days to begin training camp as he searches for a post-playing career. “I immediately ran over there and gave him a big hug,” Spillane said. “A potential Hall of Fame guy. A guy that played the game the right way. I’m sure he’ll do great as a coach.” One of the best NFL receivers of this generation, Hopkins spent time with Mike Vrabel in Houston before joining the Titans in 2023. He went on to catch 75 passes for 1,057 yards and seven touchdowns for Tennessee that season and spent six games with them in 2024 following Vrabel’s departure. In between stops in Houston and Tennessee, Hopkins played three seasons with the Arizona Cardinals, which led to a matchup against the Patriots in 2022. “Unbelievable player. The expertise when it comes down to it is much respected for everyone in the DB role. So having him in the building means a lot,” captain Marcus Jones said. “[His] expertise of knowing what progression he is in the route. Guys that are veterans know if they’re the first progression or third progression. Also, having late hands was something he was really good at. His ball skills are impeccable too as well.” Now in New England in a coaching role, Hopkins will spend his time with the offensive coaches — specifically assisting the wide receivers — and personnel department. Patriots’ players on both sides of the ball are looking forward to working with him. “Any time you have a valuable asset like that in the room is a blessing for everybody,” tight end Hunter Henry said. “Some guy that’s played at the highest level. One of the best receivers of the past decade, for sure. So much production, we could pick his brain on a lot of different things, and it’ll be cool to have a guy like that.” “That’s a guy that whenever we have questions we can actually ask him and learn about the knowledge about how guys think about running routes and being a receiver,” Jones added.

title: Christian Gonzalez to participate in Patriots training camp despite contract uncertainty
summary: New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez was present at the team’s facility on Friday amid ongoing contract extension negotiations. Mike Vrabel, when speaking with the media, said he expects the All-Pro to participate when training camp begins on Saturday. Veterans reported to Foxboro on Friday after rookies arrived on Tuesday, marking the final domino to […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 08: Christian Gonzalez #0 of the New England Patriots looks on prior to Super Bowl LX against the Seattle Seahawks at Levi's Stadium on February 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez was present at the team’s facility on Friday amid ongoing contract extension negotiations. Mike Vrabel, when speaking with the media, said he expects the All-Pro to participate when training camp begins on Saturday. Veterans reported to Foxboro on Friday after rookies arrived on Tuesday, marking the final domino to fall before New England kicks off its summer sessions. With Gonzalez entering the fourth year of his rookie contract, the Patriots picked up his fifth-year option back in April. However, the 24-year-old is seeking a long-term extension. “Those contract negotiations are ongoing between the club and his agents,” Vrabel said. “I’m excited about having Christian back here with us and the impact that he can make on our football team. Really enjoy the person, really enjoy the player, and that’s what I’m looking forward to.” Gonzalez was present at all three mandatory minicamp practices in June, but he was a limited participant, sitting out of team drills. Vrabel also expects his star cornerback’s participation level to change. “Yeah. We’re getting ready to prepare to win,” Vrabel said about Gonzalez possibly increasing his participation from minicamp. “And that’s what this is going to take through training camp. We talked about this last year: earning a role, building a team, and preparing to win. “And players have an opportunity to earn a role. Coaches are going to be there to help them. We all have to build a team, and I have to do my best to prepare us to win by our situations in the way we practice throughout training camp.” Another cornerback from Gonzalez’s draft class, Devon Witherspoon of the Seattle Seahawks, is also due for an extension. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said during Tuesday’s program that Witherspoon’s negotiations seem to be further along than Gonzalez’s. Rapoport added that he wouldn’t be surprised if a new deal for Gonzalez materializes at some point shortly after a potential Witherspoon resolution in Seattle. “I don’t think they have anything to do with one another,” Vrabel said when asked if the team has been waiting for things to shake out in Seattle. “We’re not negotiating with the Seahawks. We’re negotiating with Christian’s representatives, and I don’t think that there’s anything different than just our communication with them.” New England’s first training camp practice on Saturday is scheduled to start at 10 a.m. E.T. and will be open to public attendance.

title: DeAndre Hopkins joins Patriots coaching staff ahead of training camp
summary: DeAndre Hopkins, one of the best wide receivers of his era, will be part of the New England Patriots’ training camp this summer. However, he will not be on the field catching passes. Instead, as Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel announced during a pre-camp press conference on Friday, Hopkins will be assisting the team’s coaching […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - NOVEMBER 23: DeAndre Hopkins #10 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on before the game against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images DeAndre Hopkins, one of the best wide receivers of his era, will be part of the New England Patriots’ training camp this summer. However, he will not be on the field catching passes. Instead, as Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel announced during a pre-camp press conference on Friday, Hopkins will be assisting the team’s coaching staff. “DeAndre Hopkins is here with us just to kind of check things out as far as what he wants to do as far as coaching. You’ll see him on the field,” Vrabel said. Hopkins and Vrabel go back to 2014, when the former was a second-year receiver for the Houston Texans and the latter joined the organization as its linebackers coach under Bill O’Brien. They later reunited in Tennessee during the 2023 season and have now joined forces again in New England. “He asked if he could hang out for a couple of days and be around the coaches and around the personnel department,” Vrabel said about the 34-year-old. “I called the league to make sure that was going to be okay, and then I invited him back. That’s where he’s been the last couple of days, and he’ll be here for the next couple of days.” Between entering the league as a first-round draft pick in 2013 and his 2025 season with the Baltimore Ravens, Hopkins appeared in a combined 204 regular season and playoff games. A five-time All-Pro selection and five-time Pro Bowler, he has a total of 1,046 receptions, 13,770 receiving yards and 87 on his résumé. Hopkins has not officially announced his retirement from the NFL yet, but Vrabel made sure to point out that he is not in town in hopes of continuing his active playing career. “He is coaching from here on, and he is helping the offensive coaches and work with the personnel guys. He loves football. People that love football and have played the game for the length of time that he did, once they explore the opportunities and what that looks like once his playing career is over. The Patriots’ wide receiver group is being coached by Todd Downing, and heads into training camp with offseason acquisitions A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs as the headline names. The veteran pair is being joined by returning veterans Mack Hollins, Kayshon Boutte, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams, among others. They and the rest of the 12 total wideouts on the current roster will take the practice fields on Saturday, 10 a.m. ET for the first time this summer.

title: Which former starters must prove themselves to stay on the Saints roster?
summary: Preseason is always a fun time for fans because it’s finally time to see the players back practicing, but for some, it could be the last time they are on their team. Cuts are a significant part of the preseason process, and up until that deadline, the staff will be assessing players throughout the roster. […]
full_text: Sep 21, 2025; Seattle, Washington, USA; New Orleans Saints running back Kendre Miller (5) warms up before the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images | Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Preseason is always a fun time for fans because it’s finally time to see the players back practicing, but for some, it could be the last time they are on their team. Cuts are a significant part of the preseason process, and up until that deadline, the staff will be assessing players throughout the roster. Most of the cuts are young players trying to make it in the NFL or veterans signed as competition, but there are also veterans who used to be starters who end up getting beat out. Every roster has players who may never have met expectations or have faced roadblocks they have been unable to overcome. The staff can only give so many chances, and those chances diminish if that staff also did not draft the player. The New Orleans Saints have a few former starters on their roster who could be cut at the deadline, but they will have a chance to prove themselves before that happens. Here are some of those players: Kendre Miller Out of everyone on this list, this is the most frustrating. Kendre Miller, when healthy, is truly special to watch. He has speed, explosive ability, can break tackles, and proves he can be a high-level RB in the NFL. But I had to say when healthy before getting to any of that. Miller has been injured every single year he has been in the league, and it hasn’t been just missed games here and there; it has knocked him out for multiple weeks. Dennis Allen is to blame for some of those missed games after he made the questionable decision to put the young RB on IR, but Miller was injured before that happened. Again, it’s clear Miller has talent, but the injuries are too much of an issue. He is still recovering from his devastating torn ACL that occurred last season, but if he can come back and stay healthy for the entire preseason, there’s still a chance he can make the playoffs. But it is his contract year, and if the Saints want to go in another direction, it would make sense. Davon Godchaux Last season, the Saints made a small move, trading away a 7th-rounder for DT Davon Godchaux. Around the league, many disregarded this move, but it was really smart for the Saints. This was the first season they were playing in a 3-4 scheme, and Godchaux was the perfect nose tackle to be in the middle of the defensive line. This was something the Saints did not have previously. Throughout the season, Godchaux had some good moments, but it always wasn’t as much of an impact as suspected. The Saints were unable to fully play in their desired defensive scheme, which did hurt Godchaux’s impact. Maybe Godchaux could play better this season due to the Saints having more ideal personnel for 3-4, but also, he may not get the chance. Godchaux will have competition in training camp, and if the Saints find a better nose tackle, he could be cut at the deadline. Pete Werner Last of the veterans who will need to have a good preseason and training camp is Pete Werner. Yes, of these three players, Werner has the least competition. This could stop the Saints from ever releasing him, but Werner has not had the best health history, and last season was very inconsistent. Kaden Elliss was brought in to lead this group; Danny Stutsman has some high potential and showed great moments last season; and Isaiah Stalbird is a really good depth option. This is a pretty good group, but if the Saints want to prop up Stutsman into a larger role and feel like they can get something decent in the Werner trade, he may not be on the Saints to start the season. But if Werner can stay healthy and look better than he did last season, then he will be on this roster.
author: Caleb Yaccarino

title: Are the Saints deep enough at wide receiver?
summary: A fan of either professional New Orleans sports franchise is predisposed to dealing with the disappointment of injuries. So it no doubt raised some eyebrows in the Crescent City when Jordyn Tyson was selected 8th overall in the 2026 NFL Draft. Not for his ability, of which few have any doubt, but for his injury […]
full_text: A fan of either professional New Orleans sports franchise is predisposed to dealing with the disappointment of injuries. So it no doubt raised some eyebrows in the Crescent City when Jordyn Tyson was selected 8th overall in the 2026 NFL Draft. Not for his ability, of which few have any doubt, but for his injury history. With a torn ACL, MCL, and PCL, as well as a fractured clavicle and a hamstring issue, the star receiver was plagued with missed time throughout his college career. It doesn’t bode well alongside Chris Olave’s concussion problems. While, to the immense credit of both, they missed only a combined four games to injury in their respective 2025 seasons, their past troubles have to be noted. The newly formed one-two punch at wide receiver can only produce if they’re suited up on Sundays. Therefore, given the pair’s troubled history, does Kellen Moore’s offense possess enough alternative weapons? Devaughn Vele had a strong campaign in 2025. Mason Tipton and Kevin Austin Jr. are among the other names that made an impact in spots a year ago. Bub Means will hope to get, and stay, healthy after an extended absence that saw him miss all of 2025. Alvin Kamara is always a threat out of the backfield, albeit not the one he once was. The tight end room, headlined by Juwan Johnson alongside new Saint Noah Fant, offers more in the receiving game than most. But after Olave and Tyson, the position lacks established star power. Might the Saints look to veterans in the market before the season begins? Or should they feel comfortable already? Let us know your thoughts on the receiver situation in the comments below!

Carter had an odd rookie season. He came in with a ton of hype as the third overall pick of last year’s draft, and had only four sacks. But the pressure stats were very good. He had the most quick pressures of any player in the NFL last season. The best guess is Carter turns a lot of those pressures into sacks this season. There’s no better way to get off to a good start than having a strong preseason, which would be a good sight for new Giants head coach John Harbaugh. Everyone would be excited to see Carter have a big preseason heading into his second NFL season. 20 Questions in 20 Days: Jaxson Dart in Year 2 | Giants.com Matt Citak: What the 23-year-old does as an encore from his promising rookie campaign will be an important factor in determining how much success the team has this season. With a new coaching staff in tow, Dart is now learning his second NFL offense in as many seasons. The young signal-caller picked up last year’s system rather quickly, and the hope is that he is able to do the same this year. Year 2 is always a big one for quarterbacks. Some players make the jump and take their game to the next level, which is what New England’s Drake Maye and Chicago’s Caleb Williams were able to do last year. Others suffer from the dreaded “sophomore slump” and see their game take a step back. Where Dart lands on this spectrum is the million-dollar question. Over-Under Win Predictions For Every NFL Team In 2026 | Bleacher Report New York Giants: Over 7.5. Bet Confidence Level: Moderate. I’m extremely high on the 2026 Giants. Jaxson Dart registered 24 combined passing/rushing touchdowns to five interceptions as a first-round rookie in 2025 and appears to be on track to take the reins as the franchise quarterback. He’ll now be coached by John Harbaugh and Matt Nagy, who bring considerable know-how and experience to this rising team. The offensive line should be better with top pick Francis Mauigoa on board, Dart now has vet Isaiah Likely as a safety valve, and he’s getting Malik Nabers and Cam Skattebo back from injury. If that core can put it all together, a Giants team with several elite talents on defense should keep the momentum going after scoring 68 points in back-to-back wins to conclude 2025 with a run into or above the .500 range in 2026. NFL insider offers optimistic update on health of Giants owner John Mara | USAToday.com New York Giants co-owner and CEO John Mara received an encouraging health update from long-time NFL reporter Gary Myers. Mara publicly disclosed his cancer diagnosis in September 2025, stating he felt strong and optimistic while following a recommended treatment plan. He remained involved with the organization, even adjusting his chemotherapy schedule to participate fully in the coaching search that led to John Harbaugh’s hiring. “I can tell you that John looked great when I saw him three or four weeks ago. He really looked great. I hope that’s an indication that things are going well for him health-wise,” Myers said on the Bleav in Giants podcast. “The only other time I’ve seen him publicly was at Harbaugh’s press conference in January. And, to my eyes at least, he looked much better — to the point that if you didn’t know what he was battling, you wouldn’t know. That’s how good he looked.” From Big Blue View Revisiting the NY Giants’ 2023 draft class Which undrafted players will make the Giants’ 53-man roster?
