title: Revisiting the NY Giants’ 2023 draft class
summary: The New York Giants have had plenty of problems since their last Super Bowl. One of their most persistent issues over the last decade and a half has been their player development. Regardless of head coach or general manager, the Giants have largely struggled to turn their draft picks into dependable veterans. Even when draftees […]
full_text: Dec 28, 2025; Paradise, Nevada, USA; New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks (2) returns a punt for a touchdown in the second half against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The New York Giants have had plenty of problems since their last Super Bowl. One of their most persistent issues over the last decade and a half has been their player development. Regardless of head coach or general manager, the Giants have largely struggled to turn their draft picks into dependable veterans. Even when draftees flash as rookies, they’ve seldom built upon those promising years and often regress. Every team says they want to build through the draft, but for all the attention that the executive side gets in player acquisition, the coaching side is equally vital. If fans want to know the “secret sauce” in being consistently competitive at the collegiate or professional level, it’s player development. That’s one of the most overlooked reasons why teams like the Patriots, Ravens, Steelers, 49ers, and Rams have been able to be consistently competitive in spite of consistently drafting late. And as it so happens, former Ravens’ head coach John Harbaugh is getting ready for his first training camp as the Giants’ head coach. That makes this a good time to look back at the 2023 draftees’ rookie season and see how (or if) the new regime can develop them. Cornerback Deonte Banks The Giants traded up to secure Banks with the 24th pick of the 2023 NFL Draft. At the time, Banks was drafted at the insistence of cornerbacks coach Jerome Henderson to be a “number one” corner in Wink Martindale’s aggressive blitz-happy defense. This is what was we said about Banks after his rookie season: The presence of a more developed Deonte Banks remains entrenched as the number one cornerback moving forward. Banks played 840 defensive snaps for the Giants, recording 56 tackles, two interceptions, six passes defended, and a solid 57.6% reception rate. He did, however, commit 8 penalties, which was 13th-highest of all cornerbacks. He missed the final two games of the season. Banks ranked 23rd best in reception rate of cornerbacks who played at least 50% of their team’s defensive plays. Banks has all the necessary athletic traits to thrive in man coverage, and he had a good overall rookie season, by my estimation. He also displayed very good awareness with zone and match principles. Whoever replaces Martindale as defensive coordinator will approve of having Banks on the roster. With the retention of Jerome Henderson, I expect Banks to continue his development as a number one corner in the league. GRADE: B+ As we now know, it didn’t quite work out that way. Banks’ development stalled in 2024 when he failed to meaningfully improve in Shane Bowen’s scheme and as the Giants’ No.1 corner. He never appeared as comfortable shadowing top receivers as he did sticking on the right side as a rookie. There were flashes of the player the Giants hoped he’d become, such as when he locked down D.K. Metcalf against the Seahawks and bullied George Pickens out of the endzone to deny the Steelers a touchdown. However he never sustained that level of play. Unfortunately, those flashes gave way to full-on regression after Jerome Henderson was fired following the 2024 season. Banks still possesses a legitimately elite athletic profile and his ability to be sticky in man coverage is likewise elite. At the time of Bowen’s firing last year, Banks was allowing the 2nd lowest separation and was targeted at the seventh-lowest rate in the NFL. Banks looked like a future No.1 cornerback after his rookie year, and has tools with which coaches can work. Working with those tools will be the job of Addison Lynch. Lynch was with the Denver Broncos last year, and has experience working with big, athletic corners. One of the issues with the previous coaching staff was low accountability from the top and a low attention to detail on the defensive side of things. Lynch seems to be focusing on the details with Banks, to improve his play when the margin for error as smallest. “We tried to show him that his consistency was his deal,” Lynch said. “He just wasn’t consistent getting lined up fast, wasn’t consistent with his feet. He’s improved his consistency, so now his play is improved, now his confidence is up and he can just roll into the season. “I love how he’s handling it. Right now, he’s being an absolute pro. He’s doing the extra work, he’s in his book, he’s doing everything we ask him. He’s making plays on the ball and he’s doing a really good job handling himself play in and play out. He’s made major improvements that when he’s tired, he relies on his technique and he’s getting more technical sound, so everything with him is trending in the right direction.” The question now is if improving Banks’ consistency, positioning, footwork, and technique can allow him to play with more confidence at the catch point. It isn’t always appropriate to turn back to the ball, as that can sacrifice speed allow receivers to get late separation. However, playing with more confidence can allow Banks to trust himself and more consistently locate the ball when that’s the appropriate technique — and, of course, understand when it’s appropriate to play receivers’ hands or the ball. Lynch coached one of the best secondaries in the NFL last year, and Dennard Wilson has a great track record of getting the most out of his defensive backs. This might be the best case scenario for Banks to finally become the player he was drafted to be. Center John Michael Schmitz The Giants drafted John Michael Schmitz in the second round. He was widely considered to be one of the top two centers in his draft class and one of the top five interior linemen. Schmitz immediately stepped into the starting job for the Giants, but the immediate results weren’t as hoped. Second-round pick John Michael Schmitz flashed his upside but was inconsistent overall. He allowed five sacks and 30 pressures in his 484 offensive snaps. He surrendered the fifth most sacks and pressures at the position. Here are Joe Schoen’s comments on John Michael Schmitz’s rookie season: “John Michael Schmitz is going to be a good center,” Schoen said. “The intangibles are off the charts, he’s got leadership potential. I’d be surprised if he’s not a captain down the road.” I’m not in the building, but Schoen’s comments about his leadership make sense. Schmitz’s toughness is palpable, and his movement skills, and ability at the second level, were solid through his rookie season. I love the leverage he plays with, and his wrestling background was perceptible on tape. The interior parts of the line had a turbulent time executing twist pickups. I’m not going to assign full blame to the rookie center for the struggles, but I was pleased to see how effortless it was for Schmitz to open and close his hips. Overall, Schmitz was adequate along an imperfect offensive line. There’s room for growth, but the foundation is solid. GRADE: C “Adequate” is probably the best descriptor for Schmitz since his rookie season. He has improved in each off-season under Carmen Bricillo and is now a perfectly serviceable NFL starter. He might not be a road grader in the run game, but he’s become a reliable pass protector, giving up just one sack and one hit last year. Schmitz’s biggest hurdle has been playing with consistent hand placement, which in turn ha impacted his leverage consistency. He’s capable of anchoring against bigger nose tackles when he plays with good hand placement, allowing him to keep his hips and pads low. Schmitz is in the last year of his rookie contract and the task of getting him to the level of earning a lucrative second contract falls to offensive line coach Mike Bloomgren and assistant offensive line coach Grant Newsome. Not only do they need to perfect his hand usage and leverage, but also help him adapt to Greg Roman’s gap-based…

title: NY Giants training camp: Which undrafted players will make the 53-man roster?
summary: A handful of undrafted players always excite New York Giants fans during the spring and summer, and a few generally make the 53-man roster. With rookies having already reported for training camp, let’s look at which undrafted players could emerge with roster spots. PK Dominic Zvada Zvada has a clear lead over Ben Sauls for […]
full_text: Dominic Zvada attempts a field goal for Michigan. | Getty Images A handful of undrafted players always excite New York Giants fans during the spring and summer, and a few generally make the 53-man roster. With rookies having already reported for training camp, let’s look at which undrafted players could emerge with roster spots. PK Dominic Zvada Zvada has a clear lead over Ben Sauls for the placekicking job entering training camp. Zvada made all 13 of his field-goal attempts during mandatory minicamp, the only times media saw him kick this spring. Veteran Jason Sanders was already released, and Ben Sauls had an inconsistent spring. In an NFL where field-goal attempts from beyond 50 yards, and even 60 yards, are becoming more commonplace, a young placekicker with the ability to make those types of kicks can be an asset. Zvada made 10 of 12 kicks from beyond 50 yards in college, including 7 of 7 in 2024, with a long of 56 yards. Does he have 60+ in game conditions in his arsenal? Maybe we will find out. If Sauls continues to struggle early in training camp, it will be interesting to see if the Giants bring in veteran competition for Zvada. Currently, Daniel Carlson and Brandon McManus are among the available veteran kickers. LS Ben Mann Mann is the only true long-snapper on the 90-man roster after the Giants released journeyman Zach Triner. The long-snapping job probably belongs to Mann until he gives the Giants reason to look elsewhere. RB Damon Bankston Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy, and fullback Patrick Ricard are locked into roster spots. Veteran Devin Singletary probably is, as well. Can Bankston, 23, show enough upside to take a practice squad spot away from Dante Miller, 27, or Eric Gray, 26? OT Ryan Schernecke The Giants thought enough of Schernecke, a Division II right tackle who played at Kutztown, to give him $282,500 in guaranteed salary to sign with them. That is the equivalent of a full season’s practice squad salary. Schernecke worked mostly with the third team in the spring, though he did serve as second-team right tackle when Josh Ezeudu missed some time with an elbow injury. With players like Marcus Mbow, sixth-round pick J.C. Davis, and even Ezeudu appearing to be ahead of him on the depth chart, Schernecke is likely ticketed for the practice squad. OT Jarrod Gray Gray, 6-foot-7, 318 pounds, is a former Australian rubgy player who just took up football in 2025. Gray won’t make the 53-man roster. A practice squad spot with an exemption as part of the International Pathway Program seems like a likely outcome. DT Ben Barten Primarily a nose tackle, the 6-foot-5, 330-pound Barten seems to have a tall mountain to climb to make the roster. The Giants have D.J. Reader, sixth-round pick Bobby Jamison-Travis, and veteran Josh Tupou at nose tackle. DT Anquin Barnes Jr. Like Barten, the 6-5, 340-pound Barnes profiles as a nose tackle. Perhaps the two undrafted rookies are competing for one practice squad spot. In a profile of Barnes, Chris Pflum wrote : Barnes Jr. has the traits to be a real find and a UDFA gem if he can learn to finish his rushes. As it stands now, his disruption and ability to open holes for the Giants’ hyper-athletic linebackers could make Barnes Jr. a player to watch this summer.

title: NY Giants news: Defining success, rookie expectations, good news on Malik Nabers
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about today. Giants WR Malik Nabers is expected to avoid PUP list | Pro Football Talk The question remains about when Malik Nabers will return from rehab on his right knee, with the Giants hopeful he can play the season opener […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about today. Giants WR Malik Nabers is expected to avoid PUP list | Pro Football Talk The question remains about when Malik Nabers will return from rehab on his right knee, with the Giants hopeful he can play the season opener against the Cowboys. The Giants wide receiver, though, is expected to avoid the active/physically unable to perform list to start camp, according to ESPN’s Jordan Raanan. Harbaugh: Real football players play special teams Special Expectations pt2. Banks LT Pepper = Carter Reese Hood? Stay ready.. Want to -Want to! Full @BleavNetwork ep👇🏾 https://t.co/bOq1pSit6a pic.twitter.com/6W0xdvsa4Z — Carl Banks (@CarlBanksGIII) July 23, 2026 8 NFL rookies to watch in training camp and preseason | Yahoo Sports Which offensive and defensive rookies are you most excited to see in training camp and preseason? Defensively, give me Arvell Reese. He was a bit of a surprise pick to the Giants, though his talent is not in question. Reese was a hybrid defender at Ohio State, splitting his time between edge rusher and off-ball linebacker, and it appears the Giants will deploy him similarly. Even with changes up front, Reese could be a monster on a front that features Brian Burns, Kayvon Thibodeaux and Abdul Carter, along with free-agent LB addition Tremaine Edmunds. I’ll be curious to see just how much the Giants put on Reese’s plate. They tried a similar approach with Carter as a rookie, and it took until later in his rookie season for the former Penn State star to really shine. Reese has all the tools to be a star eventually, but his instincts will be put to the test in Year 1. The preseason tape should be fascinating to watch. The Biggest Question for Every NFL Team as Training Camps Begin | The Ringer What will this offense look like if Malik Nabers is sidelined? There’s no certainty that receiver Malik Nabers, who is recovering from injuries to his ACL and meniscus, will be cleared to practice without restrictions at the start of training camp, and we should not assume that the Giants’ best offensive player will be ready by the start of the season. If he can’t go, the Giants will be trying to patch together a passing game with receivers like Darius Slayton, Calvin Austin III, Darnell Mooney, and Odell Beckham Jr. I don’t envision much explosive passing from New York until Nabers is back, and I worry about quarterback Jaxson Dart’s development without him. 2026 NFL training camp previews, projections for all 32 teams | ESPN.com Biggest storyline: How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? New York added a Super Bowl-winning coach with John Harbaugh to work with a young quarterback in Jaxson Dart. That combination alone has some thinking the Giants will have an immediate turnaround. (Reminder: They won just seven games in the past two seasons combined.) Throw in that they had two top-10 draft picks who are expected to contribute immediately and it’s supposed to instantly produce more wins. But with new schemes offensively and defensively, it might not look so promising right away. How will the organization handle that? The increased workload will also be something to watch, especially when Harbaugh is known as an old-school coach who runs one of the league’s harder training camps. Giants’ 10-step plan revisited: Will New York regret lack of investment in trenches? | The Athletic Cutting Okereke, keeping Thibodeaux, re-signing Eluemunor, letting Robinson walk and taking the best player available with the fifth pick were clear similarities between my plan and the Giants’ actions. There were also some differences, particularly in the lack of investment in the trenches in free agency. The Mauigoa pick mitigates that to an extent, but the Giants couldn’t have known they’d have that pick while making free-agency decisions. The biggest divide was the Lawrence situation. It was impossible at the time of my plan to have a full grasp on the interpersonal dynamics that eroded the relationship. I still wonder whether the Giants, if they had proactively made my extension offer, could have avoided the ugly standoff, but all things considered, they made the best of a tough situation by securing the 10th pick in the trade. Ranking the NFL’s Divisions from Worst to First Entering 2026 | Bleacher Report Biggest Additions: The New York Giants are beginning a new era with young players like Malik Nabers, Cam Skattebo, and quarterback Jaxson Dart. This offseason, they added a Super Bowl-winning coach in John Harbaugh to the equation. As a group, the NFC East has the potential to be a very improved division in 2026. If Harbaugh can get the most out of New York’s roster—and players like Dart, Nabers and Skattebo can get and stay healthy—the Giants could make some noise during the regular season. The Cowboys, meanwhile, could make noise in the postseason if their defense plays up to its potential. From Big Blue View What would a successful John Harbaugh Giants tenure look like? His college career started at USC in 2020. He was a member of the Trojans for three years, followed by a two year stint at Kentucky. His performance was a tad uneven. Ford allowed 8 sacks in 11 starts after not allowing one from 2022 through 2025. He went undrafted and initially unsigned. The Jets offered Ford a tryout at their rookie minicamp, and he did enough to score a contract. 2026 will be a success if: Ford makes the practice squad. Like Xavier Hill, who we recently discussed , there isn’t much of a path for Ford to make the 53 man roster. Too many spots along the offensive line are already locked in. Since Ford wasn’t even part of the initial undrafted free agent class, he might face an even tougher path to earning a practice squad spot. If he gets one, he will have done well. Odds of making the roster: Longshot (<25%)

summary: When and where: Week 14 at home Key additions: EDGE Arden Key, EDGE Michael Clemons, LB Akeem Davis-Gaither Key subtractions: WR Michael Pittman, LB Zaire Franklin, RT Braden Smith, EDGE Kwity Paye, S Nick Cross, LB Germaine Pratt, CB Kenny Moore Last season: The Colts completely collapsed, but extended the health insurance of Philip Rivers, […]
full_text: Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen reacts to officials Sunday, Sept. 22, 2024, during a game against the Chicago Bears at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | Christine Tannous/IndyStar / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images When and where: Week 14 at home Key additions: EDGE Arden Key, EDGE Michael Clemons, LB Akeem Davis-Gaither Key subtractions: WR Michael Pittman, LB Zaire Franklin, RT Braden Smith, EDGE Kwity Paye, S Nick Cross, LB Germaine Pratt, CB Kenny Moore Last season: The Colts completely collapsed, but extended the health insurance of Philip Rivers, his wife, and his 10 children another five years. That’s a class act franchise right there. The question for this team: How soon does everyone get fired? The 2025 Colts started 8-2 before hitting their bye in Week 11. They never won again. Daniel Jones had a good but overstated start before getting hurt and the team turned to a 44 year old high school coach to replace him. After 9-8 and 8-9 seasons in the two years prior, this is the kind of petering out that gets people fired. GM Chris Ballard, who has been there since 2017 and has one playoff win to show for it, and head coach Shane Steichen, who is 2-10 against the Texans and Jaguars, got to keep their jobs. This spring, they haven’t done anything to show they deserve to keep them. Michael Pittman was given away for scraps (a 7th/6th round pick swap), the team has no up and coming WR that he was blocking to replace him. Daniel Jones was wisely transition tagged and then given a two year deal, the Colts will save cap space when they cut him after the season because the new GM and head coach want a real QB. The AFC South is a competitive division, with everyone except the Colts winning it twice over the past six seasons. The Colts haven’t won it since 2014. The 2026 Colts seem to be just waiting for the season to end. Indianapolis will be coming off their bye before playing the Eagles. Could that be when a coaching change is made?

title: Eagles News: Philadelphia’s top non-quarterback MVP candidate
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL MVP: One non-QB candidate from each NFC team in 2026 – NFL.comSAQUON BARKLEY – Much was made of the Eagles’ offensive fall-off last season. One of the lesser-discussed aspects was the explosive plays from Barkley drying up. It’s natural to see some regression following […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - DECEMBER 28: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles rushes for yards during the third quarter of the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL MVP: One non-QB candidate from each NFC team in 2026 – NFL.com SAQUON BARKLEY – Much was made of the Eagles’ offensive fall-off last season. One of the lesser-discussed aspects was the explosive plays from Barkley drying up. It’s natural to see some regression following a 2,000-yard campaign, but Barkley lost 1.7 yards per carry from his 5.8 mark in 2024, plummeting to 4.1 in ’25. The RB had just four runs of 20-plus yards — the same number as Jaxson Dart and Marcus Mariota . With the offensive line returning healthier than a year ago, I’m sure we will see a more explosive Barkley. Not a ton is known about new OC Sean Mannion’s plans, but if he takes anything from his former boss in Green Bay, we’d expect Philly to lean on the ground game — Matt LaFleur’s team ran the ball on the fifth-highest percentage of plays last season. Saquon Barkley’s biggest critic is himself – PhiladelphiaEagles.com Change has been afoot for everyone with Sean Mannion joining the team as the new Offensive Coordinator. Mannion has worked in offenses that utilize the quarterback under center in many packages, something that affects the running back position. To prepare for the potential change, Saquon Barkley has been talking to former NFL running back Todd Gurley. Every offseason, Barkley studies film of running backs across the league to see what he can add to his game. Growing up as a fan of the two-time All-Pro, Barkley decided to reach out to Gurley personally to learn more about the way he attacked NFL defenses. “Under center, you can see it a little clear. You’re not blinded,” Barkley said after a June minicamp practice. “There’s a lot of unique things you can do … look forward to doing that. Probably be the most I’ve ever done it under center.” One thought on each Eagles offensive player ahead of training camp – The Athletic Saquon Barkley, RB: He chose Philadelphia in 2024 partly because of its storied offensive line and subsequently broke the NFL’s full-season rushing record en route to a Super Bowl title. Can he experience a similar multiplier season within an overhauled system that will use more wide-zone concepts? Philadelphia Eagles Hidden Gems: 3 underrated players on the 2026 roster – BGN Which is where the trade for former Packers receiver Dontayvion Wicks comes in. Last season, the 6’1”, 206-pound Wicks caught 30 passes on 44 targets for 332 yards and two touchdowns. Calf and ankle injuries, as well as concussion issues, limited his time on the field in 2025, which is why he wasn’t able to replicate his 2024 production, when he caught 41 passes on 80 targets for 454 yards and five touchdowns. Still, when your yards per catch stays exactly the same from one season to the next (11.1), and your catch rate increases from 51.3% to 68.2%, that’s a good thing. “Me and Sean built a relationship, just like [with] Coach Mahaffey,” Wicks said of his new home with Mannion and former Green Bay receivers coach Ryan Mahaffey. “Relationships play a big part in things, so I felt like that was a big part of the reason [for] the trust for me to be here and for them to bank on me.” Howie Roseman explained why Wicks was a consideration before the Brown trade even happened, and why the Eagles gave him a one-year, $10.5 million contract extension with a max value of $12.5 million. ”You see his skill set,” Roseman said of Wicks. “He is a physical, explosive player at the top of routes. He can play inside or out, so he is a guy we had our eye on.” Sirianni has admired Wicks’ abilities to a similar degree. Thorn: 2026 Offensive Line Rankings – Establish The Run 2) Eagles (Chris Kuper). LT Jordan Mailata, LG Landon Dickerson, C Cam Jurgens, RG Tyler Steen, RT Lane Johnson. Unit Profile: Elite bookend-driven unit with rare tackle play, high-end left-side power, and enough center stability to offset the clear RG weak link. Notes: The Eagles had a tumultuous 2025 season due to injuries to Landon Dickerson, who played through a preseason knee injury all year, and Lane Johnson, who missed the final eight games with a Lisfranc injury, along with schematic issues that contributed to the retirement of legendary OL coach Jeff Stoutland. This remains a star-studded line built around an elite tackle duo, including the best pass-protecting tackle in football in Johnson, whose timing, positioning, and one-on-one dominance still separate him from the field. Jordan Mailata remains a high-quality starter with rare run-game impact, while Cam Jurgens gives the unit a solid center with rebound potential if his health returns closer to the baseline. Dickerson is still an elite guard when healthy and, at minimum, a stout, powerful presence on the left side. That core gives Philadelphia enough top-end quality to mask the unit’s weak link, Tyler Steen, whose first full year as a starter showed serviceable run-game play but clear pass-protection limitations. With all five starters returning and a Shanahan-esque structure built on under-center play-action and the zone run game, the unit should have more built-in pass-protection help than ever before. The starting five is more fragile than in recent years due to wear and tear, but the talent remains among the league’s best. Markel Bell was drafted to compete with Fred Johnson at swing tackle, while Drew Kendall headlines the competition for the swing interior role. More Praise for the OL – Iggles Blitz Drew Kendall – Has a chance to be top backup at C/G. Good athlete with solid size at 6-4, 308. Didn’t play much as a rookie, but started the season finale and showed good potential. He does a good job with snaps so he can play C or G. He is quick off the ball and plays with good leverage. Good feet. Moves well and can block on the move. Needs to do a better job of sustaining blocks and finishing blocks. Jimmy Bama has some clips of Kendall here. 2026 NFL training camp previews, projections for all 32 teams – ESPN Biggest storyline: How will Jalen Hurts fare in the reimagined offense? Sean Mannion, the 34-year-old former QB coach of the Green Bay Packers, is implementing a scheme expected to feature more under center, motion and throws over the middle, elements the offense hasn’t leaned heavily into with Hurts as its signal-caller. Hurts appears to have bought into both Mannion and the changes so far, but, as the spring practices revealed, there are going to be some stumbles as the unit works through the learning curve. It is clear the front office wants to move the attack in a more modern and imaginative direction. Whether Hurts’ skill set and Mannion’s vision align is the single biggest question facing an Eagles team trying to round back into championship form following a wild-card exit in 2025. Some takeaways from Nick Sirianni’s pre-training camp press conference – PhillyVoice Tank Bigsby is a hustler. Sirianni: “I told the story about Franco Harris that Tony Dungy told us — and I said this our first year — he was always running to the ball. So basically, what Dungy said was like the act in itself that he caught the ‘Immaculate Reception,’ that may have been lucky. But his habit of being around the football and being there at the right place at the right time was not unlucky because that’s who he was, his habits. Well, now I’m thinking about that, and it’s like, well, that’s Tank Bigsby, he is constantly running to the football, he is constantly doing everything he’s supposed to do.” #JimmySays: This was part of a much longer answer about Nick’s use of ChatGPT. He called it “ChatGP.” Zach Berman had a good story about that. Anyway, I just thought that the quick aside about Bigsby’s practice habits was interesting. Maybe…

full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - NOVEMBER 23: Chandler Martin #54 of the Baltimore Ravens signs autographs for fans after the game against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles waived linebacker Chandler Martin in June with a failed physical designation, and now over a month later, he was back visiting with the team, as noted by Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston . The Eagles signed Martin to a two-year deal just five months after the LB tore his ACL, ending his rookie season in late-November. He was in Philadelphia from March to June before ultimately being waived by the team, but it’s likely this recent meeting is to see if he’s medically cleared. Even if he’s not ready just yet, Martin could eventually be a good developmental player for Philadelphia on both defense and special teams. Martin spent most of his rookie season with Baltimore on the practice squad, but did get elevated to the active roster in three games. The LB only saw playing time on special teams, but did record five total tackles in his 34 snaps.

title: Steelers named top landing spot for Deebo Samuel
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have already made significant changes to their offense this offseason, but one NFL analyst believes another proven playmaker could still be added to the mix. In a recent piece highlighting logical landing spots for veteran players around the league, Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox named free agent wide receiver Deebo Samuel as a […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 25: Deebo Samuel #1 of the Washington Commanders carries the ball against the Dallas Cowboys during the first half of the NFL game at Northwest Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have already made significant changes to their offense this offseason, but one NFL analyst believes another proven playmaker could still be added to the mix. In a recent piece highlighting logical landing spots for veteran players around the league, Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox named free agent wide receiver Deebo Samuel as a potential fit for Pittsburgh. “Wide receiver Deebo Samuel has recorded just one season of 1,000 or more receiving yards during his NFL career,” Knox writes . “However, his ability to contribute as both a receiver and a runner has allowed him to top 800 scrimmage yards in six of his seven campaigns.” Samuel has been one of the NFL’s most versatile offensive weapons since entering the league in 2019. A former First-Team All-Pro, he has excelled as both a receiver and runner, totaling more than 6,000 yards from scrimmage and 43 touchdowns during his career with the San Francisco 49ers and Washington Commanders. While injuries and a reduced role have impacted his production in recent seasons, the 30-year-old still possesses the physical, yards-after-catch ability that made him one of football’s most dangerous offensive players. From the Steelers’ perspective, Samuel could complement an offense that has undergone a major transformation. Adding Samuel would give the Steelers another experienced weapon capable of lining up all over the formation, creating mismatches as a slot receiver, ball carrier and screen-game option. Whether such a move is realistic remains to be seen. Personally, I’d be surprised if the Steelers add another wideout, given their affinity for rookie second round pick Germie Bernard. Samuel’s health history should heavily factor into Pittsburgh’s decision-making. Still, Bleacher Report believes Pittsburgh stands out as one of the more logical destinations, giving the Steelers another intriguing option as they continue building an offense designed to compete in the AFC. title: Seahawks bring back former third-round pick Nick Vannett
summary: On the eve of the first day of training camp, the Seattle Seahawks have found their replacement at tight end for the recently waived Harrison Bryant, and it’s one of their own draft picks from a decade ago. Nick Vannett, a 2016 third-round selection out of Ohio State, has returned to the Seahawks for the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - DECEMBER 23: Nick Vannett #81 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates his touchdown with a fan during the second quarter of the game aganst the Kansas City Chiefs at CenturyLink Field on December 23, 2018 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Otto Greule Jr/Getty Images) | Getty Images On the eve of the first day of training camp, the Seattle Seahawks have found their replacement at tight end for the recently waived Harrison Bryant , and it’s one of their own draft picks from a decade ago. Nick Vannett, a 2016 third-round selection out of Ohio State, has returned to the Seahawks for the first time since he was traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers back in 2019. Vannett most recently played for the Los Angeles Rams, having been poached off the Minnesota Vikings practice squad. He was one of three tight ends Seattle tried out earlier this week . The 33-year-old Vannett caught 48 passes for 463 yards and four touchdowns during his Seahawks career. He was primarily a blocking tight end who backed up Jimmy Graham at the start of his career and then was essentially the top tight end on the roster in 2018 following injuries to Ed Dickson and Will Dissly. To make room for Vannett on the 90-man roster, the Seahawks waived cornerback Tyrone Broden with an injury designation. Broden was on the PUP list with an undisclosed injury before he was let go. Welcome back, Nick!

title: Why Monday is a notable date for a Devon Witherspoon contract extension
summary: Summer is in full swing with just a week left in July, and while the NFL regular season remains a month and a half off, the veteran members of the roster of the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks report for training camp Friday. One of those who is set to report is All-Universe cornerback […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - DECEMBER 07: Devon Witherspoon #21 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates during an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on December 7, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Summer is in full swing with just a week left in July, and while the NFL regular season remains a month and a half off, the veteran members of the roster of the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks report for training camp Friday. One of those who is set to report is All-Universe cornerback Devon Witherspoon, the fifth overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft who has made the Pro Bowl in all three seasons of his career and is in line for a new contract. The Seahawks exercised the fifth year option in Witherspoon’s contract during the spring, and are now reportedly deep in negotiations on an extension to make him the highest paid cornerback in the NFL . As for exactly when that extension might come, there’s no hard and fast deadline so there’s no guarantee of an impending announced. However, a looming roster bonus in Witherspoon’s rookie contract could be enough of an incentive to get the deal done over the weekend, as getting the extension knocked out before Monday could allow the Seahawks to reduce the cash spend and 2026 cap hit of any extension. The reason for this is that Witherspoon’s 2026 cap hit is made up of three parts, including the base salary, the prorated portion of his signing bonus and his 2026 roster bonus. The three parts are as follows: Base salary : $1,145,000 (Fully guaranteed) Prorated signing bonus : $5,042,937 (Already paid, recognizing against the cap for accounting purposes) 2026 Roster bonus : $3,949,702 (Fully guaranteed) Even though Witherspoon’s 2026 roster bonus is fully guaranteed, according to a source who has reviewed the contract, it does not become due and payable until the third day following mandatory reporting to training camp for veterans. With mandatory reporting for training camp being Friday, that makes Monday the third day after the mandatory report date, and the date on which the $3,949,702 moves from fully guaranteed to earned and due to be paid. It’s far from a huge difference, but because the bonus becomes earned Monday, at that point the associated $3,949,702 2026 cap charge connected to the bonus becomes locked in and would not be impacted by a extension between the two sides. In contrast, if the two sides reach agreement on an extension prior to Monday, the roster bonus could be wrapped into a signing bonus, allowing for a small bit of cash flow to be pushed into the future, along with part of the cap hit, which would potentially reduce the 2026 cash obligations of the team. The reason for the difference is that the size of whatever extension Witherspoon signs with the team is unlikely to change based on the cash payout of his current contract. Thus, the only way to wrap the cash spend obligation and cap hit of his 2026 roster bonus into a new contract is by reaching an extension prior to it becoming due. Looking at the cash and cap impact of a hypothetical extension helps lay out the difference. Say Witherspoon and the Seahawks agree to a new contract that pays $100M over three years with a $25M signing bonus and keeps the 2026 base salary at the league minimum for a player with three credited seasons at $1,145,000. Such an extension, if agreed to by the two sides before the roster bonus is due, could have the following cap hits and cash spend obligations: Base salary: $1,145,000 cash, $1,145,000 cap hit Prorated rookie signing bonus: $0 cash, $5,042,937 cap hit Extension signing bonus: $25,000,000 cash, $5,000,000 cap hit Total 2026 cash: $26,145,000 Total 2026 cap hit: $11,187,936 Putting all those together the 2026 cap hit would be $11,187,936 on a cash spend obligation of $26,145,000. That would represent an increase in cash spend of $21,050,298 while Witherspoon’s 2026 cap hit would rise by just $1,050,298, because the roster bonus could be absorbed into the signing bonus. Witherspoon would still receive the same amount of money, just some portion of it pushed out into the future. In contrast, if the same $100M contract extension were to be reached Monday or later, the breakdown would be: Base salary: $1,145,000 cash, $1,145,000 cap hit Prorated rookie signing bonus: $0 cash, $5,042,937 cap hit Extension signing bonus: $25M cash, $5M cap hit Roster bonus: $3,949,702 cash, $3,949,702 cap hit Total 2026 cash: $30,094,702 Total 2026 cap hit: $15,137,639 Now, certainly the Seahawks can afford to pay in either scenario, but almost any business owner who has the option on whether to spend $26,145,000 instead of $30,094,702 now with the difference being paid at some point in the future will opt for the lower amount. So, while it’s not a hard and fast deadline, given reports that the two sides are deep in negotiations, it may just be enough of an incentive for reports of an extension agreement to emerge over the weekend.

title: Seahawks Football 101: What are the different types of tight ends?
summary: The tight end position may be one of the most versatile positions in the NFL. They are blockers, they are big targets for the quarterback, and if your name is AJ Barner, you can run that Tush Push/Barn-yard. The question some fans may have though is what exactly is the role of a tight end? […]
full_text: The tight end position may be one of the most versatile positions in the NFL. They are blockers, they are big targets for the quarterback, and if your name is AJ Barner, you can run that Tush Push/Barn-yard. The question some fans may have though is what exactly is the role of a tight end? Well, I am here to tell you that there are three main roles for tight ends. In this piece, I plan to go over them and provide two Seattle Seahawks examples of those types of tight ends to paint a picture as to what each of those roles do on the field to give you a better understanding of the tight end position as a whole. Time to roll the tape! In-Line Tight End (Y-TE)- Eric Saubert/A.J. Barner/Luke Willson An in-line tight end typically lines up at the end of the offensive line with one hand in the dirt. You may also hear them be referred to as a “Y” tight end. They focus heavily on blocking to assist the offensive line in both run and pass protection, while also running short to intermediate routes. In the current iteration of the Seahawks, Eric Saubert is the primary blocking tight end on the squad who can run shorter routes when needed, such as when he got into the end-zone for the winning two-point conversion against the Los Angeles Rams. Back in the Pete Carroll era of the Seahawks, Luke Willson would be the Y-TE. A.J. Barner is listed as an in-line tight end, but contributes heavily in both the passing game and blocking game and is a bit of a hybrid of an in-line tight end and a flex tight end, which we will be covering next. Sam Darnold and the Seahawks capped an incredible comeback by choosing their finish on TNF. Despite finishing -3 in turnover margin, this 2 point conversion to the backside TE, Eric Saubert, helped Seattle stun the Rams, 38-37, in overtime. #Seahawks #SeahawksvsRams pic.twitter.com/lN86vfDbiN — All 22 Films (@All_22_NFL_Cuts) December 19, 2025 Flex/Move Tight End (F-TE)- Jimmy Graham/Elijah Arroyo The flex/move tight end, also known as the “F” tight end, plays the role of a big wide receiver, running routes against linebackers and safeties in intermediate routes and rarely block. Jimmy Graham played this role throughout his career and excelled at it. He currently holds the majority of receiving tight end records for the Seahawks. Elijah Arroyo would be the current F-tight end. At Miami, he was essentially that X-receiver, lining up out wide and running both intermediate and deep routes, using his big body to get the receptions. If he is able to remain healthy this season, expect to see him to play a similar role as Graham on the team. Jimmy Graham for the touchdown!!! Boxes out the defender. Does a great job at using his body to secure the catch. #Seahawks #SEAvsAZ pic.twitter.com/jVpvR1JB6B — Samuel Gold (@SamuelRGold) November 10, 2017 Hybrid Tight End (H-back)- Robbie Ouzts/Brady Russell The Hybrid Tight End, also referred to as the H-back, is a versatile position that is a mix of a tight end and a fullback. They line up behind the line of scrimmage, usually somewhere in front of the running back, instead of out next to the tackles. Robbie Ouzts and Brady Russell fill this role perfectly. Both former tight ends who are listed as fullbacks, they are the H-backs on the team. They can line up and block for the running back, or they can line up where the in-line tight ends are and block from there, or line up wide with the hybrid tight ends and catch a pass. They are your jack of all trades. Robbie Ouzts, FB, #40 Amazing block in open space. pic.twitter.com/rwlGvp62OL — Alexandre Castro (@alexcastrofilho) January 7, 2026 Whether your tight end is pass blocking, catching passes and touchdowns, run blocking, or carrying the rock themselves, you can expect them to be a key part of the offense. With Brian Fleury as the new offensive coordinator, and was the tight ends coach for the San Francisco 49ers, you can expect the tight ends to be a bit more involved in this offense. Barner, Saubert, Arroyo, Russell, and Ouzts will all be involved in this offense heavily, and who knows? They may even catch a few more touchdowns and two point conversions than they did last year. Why are all these athletic blocking TEs with poor receiving production being drafted so high? Kacmarek, Roush, Boerkircher, Delp, Klein? Because EVERYBODY wants the next AJ Barner… pic.twitter.com/f99qSaK8pr — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) April 25, 2026

Onto today’s links… Agent’s Take: Brandon Aiyuk has only himself to blame for 49ers limbo chaos Aiyuk claimed he fired Williams in November. Williams was still listed as Aiyuk’s agent of record by the NFLPA until the end of June, when Aiyuk sent a written notice as required by their agent regulations. Presumably, Aiyuk told Williams verbally last November that his services were no longer needed. Although Williams hadn’t received a termination letter, it’s understandable that he wouldn’t be trying to protect Aiyuk’s interest anymore after such a conversation. There wasn’t anything preventing Williams from making the split official at any time by sending Aiyuk a termination letter. For example, Antonio Brown and Johnny Manziel were fired by their respective agents. I don’t doubt that Aiyuk was told by the NFLPA and/or Williams that he would be released in early June at the latest. That was likely before Aiyuk went AWOL. The 49ers are less inclined to reward what can reasonably be viewed as negative behavior. George Kittle reveals one area where Kyle Shanahan has grown as 49ers coach “His situational awareness, in my opinion, has grown so much,” Kittle said. “He’s been the head coach for going on 10 years now, and he’s just learned constantly — this part of the game matters the most. Got to hang onto the ball before halftime. Don’t let the other team score. Turnovers, whatever it is. Our whole team has realized that, too. We’ve all grown with it.” “Sometimes we get one of the most difficult game plans I’ve ever seen in my entire life, and then another game, it’ll be the easiest game plan I’ve ever seen, but it’s versus a better team,” Kittle said. “I’m just like, ‘Kyle, what are we doing?’ But then they all work, and I’m just like, oh well. I’m having a great time regardless.” Former All-Pro WR predicts career year for 49ers wideout Coming to San Francisco, the 32-year-old is expected to be the team’s top wide receiver for Brock Purdy to target, and some, including legendary NFL wide receiver Chad Johnson, believe that Evans will be great for the 49ers. In a post on social media, Johnson predicted that Evans will catch 98 passes for 1,343 yards and 12 touchdowns in 2026. That would be the most receptions, the second-most receiving yards and tied for the fourth-most touchdowns that he’s had in year. With Evans coming off of a rough season where he missed nine games due to injury, those are lofty predictions for this year, but if the 49ers got even 80% of that production, they’d probably be thrilled this year. 25 predictions for 49ers’ season: How many games will they win? Tight End Brayden Willis The tight end room is thin, opening a door for Willis. Offensive Tackle Austen Pleasants Pleasants could outshine one of Vederian Lowe or Enrique Cruz. Offensive Lineman Nick Zakelj The versatility of Zakelj gives him a chance to stick around. Interior Defensive Lineman Evan Anderson The following three linemen will all compete for a fifth spot. They will also compete with Gracen Halton for the fourth spot. 49ers starter entering ‘make-or-break’ season, per PFF PFF’s Bradley Locker wrote that Lenoir is one of 10 players on Super Bowl contenders who make or break his respective teams’ 2026 campaign. Locker pointed to a step back in coverage and run defense as reasons for concern with Lenoir. It’s still remarkable that the 49ers reached the divisional round given their defense finished 31st in success rate. While injuries and issues affected almost every level of the unit, Lenoir was also more ineffective than usual. Lenoir led San Francisco in defensive snaps but posted a 65.7 PFF coverage grade, good for the 62nd percentile — a dip from the 74-plus coverage grades he posted in each of the previous two seasons. His 99.8 passer rating allowed still ranked 20th-highest among qualified corners, and he graded in the 51st percentile in coverage at outside corner. He was also flagged a career-high 10 times, and his run-defense grade fell to a personal low of 44.3.

title: 49ers star Nick Bosa makes it known he was not a fan of Ryan Clark
summary: San Francisco 49ers star pass rusher Nick Bosa isn’t known for his social media. He distanced himself from Twitter since his first season as a pro. Since then, Bosa has had several retweets. He shared former teammate De’Vondre Campbell’s post about the NFL needing to do away with turf fields. In between that, there’s a […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers stands on the sidelines during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on September 21, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers star pass rusher Nick Bosa isn’t known for his social media. He distanced himself from Twitter since his first season as a pro. Since then, Bosa has had several retweets. He shared former teammate De’Vondre Campbell’s post about the NFL needing to do away with turf fields. In between that, there’s a Joe Rogan podcast retweet as well as a George Kittle one. But on Thursday, Bosa took the time to quote a tweet where ESPN cut ties with former NFL player Ryan Clark: 👌 https://t.co/hH903xy6zy — Nick Bosa (@nbsmallerbear) July 24, 2026 Instantly, the internet came out in droves to attack Bosa, calling him a racist and saying that he hates black people. Part of the reason Bosa has distanced himself from Twitter was some pre-draft tweets he had. In August of 2016, he had a tweet calling former 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick a clown. That was one of many deleted tweets that would’ve been viewed as controversial. During Bosa’s first press conference, he apologized, saying, “It wasn’t directed towards (Kaepernicks’ stance. It’s not like I’m saying his stance and what he was doing; that’s not what I was calling or talking about at all. It was just a specific thing that happened and me as a young kid a thought popping in my head and boom, decided to tweet it out. Bad decision. I respect what he’s done. If it empowers anybody, then he’s doing a good thing. So I apologize for that.” It has been quite the decade for Bosa and girlfriend-turned-wife, Jenna Berman. She had some regrettable tweets as a kid and some strong anti-vaccination thoughts during COVID-19. After a few quiet years, Bosa was fined over $11,000 for wearing a MAGA hat during Brock Purdy’s postgame interview in November 2024. There’s a faction of people who assume you’re a racist if you support a specific president. While the Bosas’ actions haven’t done them many favors to dispel that, his Ohio State teammates were outspoken about where they stand with Bosa. All this slander on Nick Bosa name revolving racism is ridiculous. The people who truly knows him, know what’s up. That’s my dog! — Tracy Sprinkle | CEO (@TSprinkle93) February 3, 2020 If you click on the quote tweets, several Buckeyes and NFL players chime in on their thoughts. Clark criticized Bosa in 2024 when he wore the MAGA hat, saying there was a double standard in how sports media treats political statements. Clark said that Bosa chose a side of division and called out media figures for not speaking up about Bosa in the ways they have told other athletes to “shut up and dribble.” I think there’s more to it than that, though. Clark used to go out of his way to call Brock Purdy a system quarterback. Clark would have extended rants about how he hated that he had to pretend that Purdy was among the league’s elite and that Purdy never elevated the team around him; rather, they were the ones propping him up. I wonder how much that played a factor in Bosa breaking his Twitter hiatus. Internet sleuths have brought up Bosa using the “okay” hand gesture as another reason to bring race into the conversation. You can read why that gesture has a negative connotation. This feels like nothing more than somebody satisfied with one person who wasn’t good at their job and was criticized personally by said person reacting.

title: NFL writer makes a bold claim about the future for the 49ers at quarterback
summary: The San Francisco 49ers just signed Brock Purdy to a five-year, $265 million contract in the spring of 2025. So there’s no way they’d part ways with him just two years after giving him over $177 million in guaranteed money, right? Purdy is 26 with plenty of valuable traits that make him a franchise quarterback. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - MAY 28: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers works out during a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on May 28, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers just signed Brock Purdy to a five-year, $265 million contract in the spring of 2025 . So there’s no way they’d part ways with him just two years after giving him over $177 million in guaranteed money, right? Purdy is 26 with plenty of valuable traits that make him a franchise quarterback. He’s aggressive, a playmaker, stays out of negative plays by avoiding sacks, and is accurate. While he’s undersized at 6’1″, Purdy isn’t small. He’s about 220 pounds. The 49ers were on the doorstep of a Super Bowl during Purdy’s first season as a starter. They had a halftime lead in the Super Bowl during his first full season as a starter. The team suffered injuries to seemingly every important piece around Purdy during the previous two seasons. Is it fair to say this is somewhat of a prove-it year for Purdy? According to NFL writer Vincent Bonsignore , it is. He believes the 49ers are a team to watch for the potential Joe Burrow sweepstakes next offseason: “Multiple league sources have indicated that San Francisco is a team to watch if Burrow serves the Bengals with divorce papers . For the same reasons (49ers head coach) Kyle Shanahan and (general manager) John Lynch made an earnest run at Lions quarterback Matthew Stafford in 2021, some believe they would not hesitate to do the same if Burrow is available.” The NFL cannot quit Burrow. In ESPN’s annual rankings, Burrow was listed at No. 4 for quarterbacks, even earning a No. 1 ranking. Purdy was banged up last season. He had a catastrophic injury as a rookie that, to me, prevented the Niners from winning a Super Bowl. But Burrow is no stranger to injuries, either. He missed half the season last year and seven games in 2023. Back in 2020, Burrow had a season-ending left knee injury. Bonsignore compared Matthew Stafford’s tenure with the Lions to Burrow, and that’s why he would eventually ask for a trade: “Much like Stafford’s patience with the Lions eventually ran out and ultimately led him to ask for a trade, Burrow could reach his boiling point with the Bengals. And there has been just enough ice cracking in Cincinnati to suggest another lost season could lead Burrow to take a page out of Stafford’s playbook. If that happens, and if Purdy and the 49ers don’t close the deal this season, the 49ers are a logical trade partner. In fact, Purdy could be the focal point of a hypothetical trade with the Bengals, along with a bunch of draft assets.” The 49ers made a run at Stafford in 2021 before they had a franchise quarterback. So it’s not an apples-to-apples comparison. I don’t think anybody would argue that Burrow’s talent supersedes Purdy’s. However, Burrow’s injury history is real. You can’t avoid that. I think this season the discussion around Purdy will be much different now that he has a WR1 to throw to. When he did in 2023, he finished fourth in the MVP voting and seventh in the Offensive Player of the Year voting. I’d also argue that this season will be the best supporting cast Purdy’s had in his career — with the obvious health asterisk. If Evans>Brandon Aiyuk, and — from purely a route-running perspective — Ricky Pearsall>Deebo Samuel, Purdy gets an upgrade on the perimeter, and gets a big-bodied speedster over the middle in De’Zhaun Stribling, not to mention vertical threats in Christian Kirk, Jacob Cowing, and Jordan Watkins. If Purdy is the quarterback the 49ers believed him to be when they gave him a massive deal a little more than a year ago, they’ll give him more than two seasons to prove himself — especially after an injury-riddled 2025.

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - JANUARY 19: Mikail Kamara #6 of the Indiana Hoosiers reacts after a stop during the second quarter against the Miami (FL) Hurricanes in the 2026 College Football Playoff National Championship at Hard Rock Stadium on January 19, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images Training camp for the San Francisco 49ers begins Sunday with the veterans reporting on Saturday. The 49ers’ rookie class has reported, which includes their draft class and the undrafted free agents brought in after the draft. The seven undrafted free agents under contract are: TE Khalil Dinkins, Penn State; DL Bryson Eason, Tennessee; WR Wesley Grimes, NC State; DL Mikail Kamara, Indiana; WR Will Pauling, Notre Dame; S Jalen Stroman, Notre Dame; and DL James Thompson Jr, Illinois. Currently, the 49ers have several players who went undrafted. Center Jake Brendel, OG Robert Jones, LB Luke Gifford, DE Andrew Farmer II, DL Evan Anderson, Safety Derrick Canteen, RB Patrick Taylor, and TE Jake Tonges were all UDFAs. Brendel and Jones could be starting next to each other on the offensive line in 2026. Basically, the 49ers have found production from undrafted players. Which 2026 49ers UDFA has the best chance to make the 53-man roster? The first place to look is the defensive line. That would make Eason, Kamara, and Thompson Jr. the most likely candidates. Dinkins has an outside chance, but that would take George Kittle not being ready for Week 1 and the team cutting Brayden Willis. Perhaps a practice squad spot is more likely for Dinkins. The one player to watch during training camp will be Kamara. The 24-year-old defensive lineman was a force for the national champion Indiana Hoosiers. After three seasons at James Madison, Kamara hit the portal and had two successful campaigns with the Hoosiers. 2024 was his best season with ten sacks and a career-high 86.4 defensive grade and 88.5 pass-rushing grade. 2025 was a step back in the sack department for Kamara, only notching two, but he did finish with nine more hurries than in 2024. Let’s consider his competition for a spot on the defensive line. Your locks are C.J. West, Alfred Collins, Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Osa Odighizuwa, Sam Okuayinonu, Keion White, and rookies Gracen Halton and Romello Height. Kamara would have to jump Evan Anderson and the other UDFA competition for a roster spot. I’d bet on Kamara, who should have been drafted, to impress and open eyes. The 49ers will need as much help as they can get on the defensive line. Waves of pass rushers are important, and Kamara can provide reliable depth. Look out for the Hoosier.

According to Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston, the Niners will work out former UFL MVP Jack Plummer for the Orlando Storm. Plummer led the league with 2,188 yards and had 17 touchdowns with only one interception in 10 games. Plummer went undrafted in the 2024 NFL Draft, but was waived by the Carolina Panthers last August during roster cuts. The 49ers might want to give Brock Purdy rest during the next month, or need a quarterback to throw late in preseason games. To me, the team working out a quarterback is a sign they want to upgrade from Martinez. Plummer’s stat line would suggest he is the kind of quarterback Shanahan would gravitate toward.

title: 49ers news: Apparently, there are 53 players in the NFL better than Fred Warner
summary: Slow news days are about to be a thing of the past, as training camp is underway. It may take a few days for the news to roll in, but we will be back in business in no time. The Feed post of the day that made me laugh: Be sure to sign up for […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 03: San Francisco 49ers' Fred Warner #54 celebrates their 24-9 NFL victory over the Los Angeles Rams at Levis Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif., on Monday, Oct. 3, 2022. (Jane Tyska/Digital First Media/East Bay Times via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Slow news days are about to be a thing of the past, as training camp is underway. It may take a few days for the news to roll in, but we will be back in business in no time. The Feed post of the day that made me laugh: Be sure to sign up for an account if you haven’t. That way you can post your own feeds and participate in the polls listed in The Feed. Onto today’s links… George Kittle Gets Honest About Davante Adams Ahead of 49ers-Rams “He’s fantastic. He’s still such an elite route runner. I try to watch this film and be like, ‘Oh, I could do that. So, I’m just like, ‘Nah, I can’t do that. He’s pretty special,’” Kittle said during the video on X on July 23. “Just to be an elite red-zone threat? Like, ‘Hey, we’re in the red zone. Now, Davante’s going to score.’ To have that confidence from your quarterback, from your team. I don’t think there’s anybody even closer than touchdowns right now. “Share some of those big dog.” 49ers to work out UFL MVP quarterback Jack Plummer ahead of training camp According to KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson, the San Francisco 49ers are set to work out United Football League (UFL) MVP Jack Plummer on Friday, a day before veterans report to training camp. Plummer also has a workout scheduled with the Miami Dolphins. 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp preview Did the 49ers do enough to contend in football’s toughest division? A 35-point playoff defeat would seem to indicate the Niners have a long road back to the top of their division. But they don’t see it that way, as their many offseason moves can attest. They added wide receivers Mike Evans and Christian Kirk , defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa and linebacker Dre Greenlaw . And they figure to get some of their stars back from injury, including defensive end Nick Bosa , linebacker Fred Warner and tight end George Kittle . Even their top three 2026 draft picks (wideout De’Zhaun Stribling , edge rusher Romello Height and running back Kaelon Black ) are age 23 or older and have extensive college football experience. If all of the above falls into place, the Niners hope they can catch — and potentially pass — Seattle and Los Angeles in the NFC West and reclaim the conference’s top spot. The 10 Most Interesting 49ers in Training Camp This Year 7. Renardo Green | Cornerback Statistically, he was the 49ers’ best cornerback last season. But he got in a shouting match with head coach Kyle Shanahan during their playoff loss to the Seahawks, and the 49ers even benched him for a drive, so you know they’re not completely satisfied with him. Then this offseason, they signed veteran cornerbacks Nate Hobbs and Jack Jones. Clearly, the 49ers want to push Green, who’s a subpar tackler and has intercepted just two passes since high school. If he doesn’t have a lights-out camp, he could lose his starting spot for Week 1. 8. Upton Stout | Nickelback He’s the 49ers’ best young defensive player, but he was a non-factor in the playoff loss to the Seahawks because he hardly was on the field. In fact, he played just 18 snaps. The Seahawks offense used lots of tight ends, and Robert Saleh didn’t feel confident leaving Stout on the field against Seattle’s base offense. Will Raheem Morris find a way to keep Stout on the field all the time this season? He’s too good to come off it, especially given the lack of talent the 49ers have in their secondary. The 49ers’ Biggest Weakness Ahead of Training Camp The glaring flaws in depth were seen at linebacker, wide receiver and along the defensive line. The 49ers have been the most injured team in the National Football League over the last 10 years while fielding some of the oldest rosters during that time frame. Depth should always be an offseason point of emphasis. But the 49ers took a different approach to their offseason moves by doubling down on proven veteran talent. The team opened free agency by signing 32-year-old Mike Evans, who has a reputation as one of the best wide receivers of this decade but has also dealt with injuries over the past couple of years. The 49ers’ next-best move was signing Dre Greenlaw, who has spent the last two years in and out of the lineup because of injuries. The 49ers addressed last season’s positional weaknesses with these moves, but they are not transactions to rely on because of the players’ histories of missing time. If that trend repeats itself, the team will be back where it started this offseason. The 49ers’ front office may understand this reality based on the type of contracts Evans and Greenlaw received, which were low-risk, high-reward deals. 49ers’ Fred Warner has something to prove after catastrophic injury: ‘Toughest times’ His absence from the final 11 games of the year seemingly played a role in Warner’s drastic drop on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026. The list is determined by current players, who vote on their peers based on their performance from the previous year. Warner earned the No. 54 spot on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026 after coming in at No. 16 last season. “I always believed strongly that everything happens for a reason,” Warner told The Athletic in a recent feature. “And it would be wrong to abandon that in the toughest times.”

In camp (1 7): Alontae Taylor, Cor’Dale Flott, Amani Hooker, Kevin Winston Jr., Marcus Harris, Tony Adams, Joshua Williams, Jerrick Reed II, Jalen McMurray, Latrell McCutchin, Jeadyn Lukus, Kendell Brooks, Sanoussi Kane, Erick Hallett II, Bishop Fitzgerald, Keydrain Calligan, Micah Robinson. Biggest storyline: The Titans totally revamped the cornerback room, signing Alontae Taylor and Cor’Dale Flott to very lucrative contracts in free agency. They’ll be tasked with being Robert Saleh’s starting boundary corners. This position needed a makeover after trading Jarvis Brownlee and Roger McCreary, and cutting L’Jarius Sneed. The Titans cut Xavier Woods during the offseason to make room for Winston in the starting lineup opposite Amani Hooker. Harris doesn’t appear to have any competition for the nickel role either. Breakout star: Winston Jr. is probably the correct choice. The former Penn State standout flashed an exciting skill set when he was healthy as a rookie. Winston is entering camp fully available and should make a massive impact next to Hooker in the lineup. He possesses every trait to be a breakout defender. Training camp competition: The Titans will only be having competition for back-end roles in the secondary. Is Joshua Williams the CB4 behind the three starters? That’s the expectation, given his experience. The fifth and presumably final cornerback spot will be decided by Micah Robinson, Keydrain Calligan, and three undrafted cornerbacks.

title: 27-yr-old Odafe Oweh poised for career-best season in Washington in 2026
summary: In this week’s Reacts survey, we asked Hogs Haven readers to rate their confidence that this year’s big offseaon free agent signing, edge rusher Odafe Oweh, will live up to his 4-year, $96m contract in 2026. The results are unsurprising, with more than half of all respondents saying that they are ‘generally confident’, which would […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 15: Odafe Oweh #99 of the Baltimore Ravens sacks Gardner Minshew #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders in the first quarter during a game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 15, 2024 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this week’s Reacts survey , we asked Hogs Haven readers to rate their confidence that this year’s big offseaon free agent signing, edge rusher Odafe Oweh, will live up to his 4-year, $96m contract in 2026. The results are unsurprising, with more than half of all respondents saying that they are ‘generally confident’, which would equate to a grade of 4 on a 5-point scale. Visit our partners at FanDuel In fact, 70% of respondents said that they are either generally confident or absolutely confident — a strong indication of support for a player who peaked with 10 sacks in 2024, but who went sack-less in his first 5 games of the 2025 season before being traded from the Ravens to the Chargers. That change of scenery seemed to do Oweh a lot of good. He tallied 7.5 sacks in 12 games in his powder-blue jersey — that pace put him on track for 10.5 sacks in 17 games. What are the expectations, then, for a player who is being paid $24m per season as a pass rusher? According to Over the Cap , there are 4 NFL edge rushers currently on contracts with average annual cap hit of between $22m and $24.5m: George Karlaftis, Andrew Van Ginkel, Odafe Oweh, and Montez Sweat. Here’s a snapshot of some key metrics for those 4 players for the past two seasons combined: Combined 2024 & 2025 statistics Source : Pro Football Reference George Karlaftis leads in 3 metrics: total defensive snaps played, total pressures, and snaps per pressure. Andrew Van Ginkel tallied the most sacks of the four players listed. Odafe Oweh stacks up pretty well overall despite playing the fewest snaps of the group. He is 2nd in sacks and highly efficient, ranking #1 in snaps per sack and #2 in snaps per pressure. It looks like this salary range should buy an NFL team around 674 defensive snaps, with 26 pressures and 7.5 sacks in a 17-game season. In 2024 & 2025, Oweh produced just about exactly that number of pressures and at least that many sacks while playing significantly fewer snaps. If he only reproduces what he did in 2025, this analysis indicates that he’ll be earning his AAV of $24m per season. But can Commanders fans expect even more from Oweh now that he has signed with Washington? A Transition from Rotational to Alpha Role Historically, Oweh’s raw numbers were capped because he was utilized as a rotational asset rather than a true foundational piece. In 2025, he played the first five weeks struggling for snaps in Baltimore before a mid-season trade to the Los Angeles Chargers. Once integrated into Jesse Minter’s defense in Los Angeles, Oweh’s efficiency skyrocketed, culminating in a dominant 17.3% quarterback pressure percentage and a franchise playoff-record 3-sack, 2-forced fumble performance against New England. The turning point for his career has now arrived in 2026. Recognizing this elite trajectory, the Commanders signed Oweh to a massive four-year, $96 million contract ($68 million guaranteed) to serve as the undisputed “Alpha” edge rusher. By stepping out from the shadow of playing behind other veteran rushers, Oweh is expected to see his snap share rise from 575 snaps per year to 670+ defensive snaps in Washington’s scheme. If he can maintain his per-snap efficiency with the increased snap count, he could generate roughly 28 pressures and 10.5 sacks in 2026. If he plays closer to 800 snaps this season, then his production could align closely with that of Andrew Van Ginkel, who averaged 796 defensive snaps per season over the past two years. Backed by a defensive scheme explicitly designed to isolate his 90th-percentile athletic traits and a contract that guarantees he will be on the field as much as possible, Oweh possesses both the proven efficiency and the volume opportunity to make 2026 the most productive year of his career.
